# LAW BOHEMIA_LAW_ANALOG_HORROR_FOR_EVERY_PIXEL_AND_EVERY_SOUND_9_20_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_ANALOG_HORROR_FOR_EVERY_PIXEL_AND_EVERY_SOUND_9_20_26.md
====================================================================================================
# BOHEMIA LAW -- ANALOG HORROR FOR EVERY PIXEL AND EVERY SOUND (Paolo 9/20/26, LOCKED)
# His words, verbatim: records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_BATTLE_BROTHERS_ON_MY_PHONE_ANALOG_HORROR_AND_THE_ALPHA_OPENS_IN_VOTE_9_20_26.md.
# "From visuals and anything that's audio-wise, from now on, end of story forever: I want us
# to lean more into an analog horror type of direction. I might have mentioned this before
# with Machine Party, and we talked about not putting a grim filter on things, but we need to
# fully commit for the rest of this cycle, as long as the game is not done. The sounds have
# to complement that. The whole enchilada. Analog horror for everything that is a pixel to
# everything that's a sound. It has to be thought about as analog horror."

## 1. THE LAW
For the rest of the cycle, until the game is done, EVERY PIXEL AND EVERY SOUND IS THOUGHT
ABOUT AS ANALOG HORROR FIRST. Tiles, bodies, faces, clothes, the interface, the loading
screen, the fight, the phone, the music, the room tone, the voices, the silence. A piece of
art or a sound that was not thought about this way is not done, whatever else it passes.
This is the tone over every department's reference; it does not replace any of them.

## 2. WHAT ANALOG HORROR IS, FOR THE FLEET (plain words, the genre's own grammar)
Horror that looks and sounds like it came off old consumer recording gear and dead
institutions. The frame is ORDINARY and one thing in it is WRONG. The camera does not move
to help you. Stillness is long. The light is the light that was there (a fluorescent tube,
a screen, a sodium lamp, a sky too flat). The text on screen is from an institution that
should not still be broadcasting, in its own typeface, too calm. The sound is the room:
hum, hiss, tape drop-outs, a broadcast tone, a voice that is too even, and silence used as
an instrument. Nothing jumps. The fear is that the world is running normally and nobody is
left who should be running it. That last sentence is already Bohemia's premise (a Las
Vegas ten years into a dead grid), which is why this is a direction and not a costume.

## 3. WHAT IT IS NOT
- NOT A FILTER. The 8/3 debate ("not putting a grim filter on things") stands in its
  conclusion: the grime is a machine that runs at bake time (laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_NO_PAINT_8_3_26.md),
  and analog horror is not a VHS overlay dropped on a normal frame either. It is decided at
  the source: what is in the frame, how it is lit, how long it holds, what it sounds like.
  A scanline shader over a cheerful street is the violation, not the compliance.
- NOT A MONSTER. No creature design, no gore pass, no jump. A person a little too still is
  the face; a street with the lights still on and nobody home is the tile.
- NOT A NEW REFERENCE GAME. Analog horror is a GENRE. NEVER ADD A REFERENCE GAME HE HAS NOT
  NAMED stands in full: no named series, channel, film or game is studied or cited unless
  he names it. Machine Party (8/3) is the one named visual reference and the bridge.
- NOT AN EXCUSE TO DARKEN. The runway law stands (everyone dresses like a runway); the far
  view he approved stands; the colour-is-territory law stands. Analog horror is the wrong
  detail in a well-lit frame, not a brightness slider.

## 4. WHAT IT DOES TO EACH DEPARTMENT'S REFERENCE
Every reference keeps its department (9/5). Analog horror is the tone each one is read
through, and where a reference's mood and this law conflict, THIS LAW WINS BY DATE:
- FINAL FANTASY X, the interface study, stands. FINAL FANTASY X, THE SOUND (9/6,
  "post-apocalyptic FFX, that fantasy beach vibe"), is AMENDED: the sound serves analog
  horror first; what of the FFX sound survives is what SOUNDS' school finds fits inside it.
  The manager's default, his to correct in the VOTE tab: a warm melody heard through a dead
  broadcast is analog horror, and that is the seam SOUNDS builds on. The 120 BPM law stands.
- FALLOUT 1, the interface, "2050 rustic": stands, read as the dead institution's screen.
- MACHINE PARTY, the look (8/3): stands and grows into the source of the grime.
- ROGUE FABLE 4 (the fight), FINAL FANTASY XII (gambits), BATTLE BROTHERS (the campaign),
  POCKET CITY 2 (the drop-in): untouched, they are mechanics.

## 5. WHO
- DIRECTION [analog horror], FIRST LINE: THE ANALOG HORROR BIBLE, one page, ten rules a
  pixel must obey, each measured against a tile, a body, a face and the fight we have,
  with a pass/fail per current asset class. From the round it lands, THE FIGHT VERDICT
  judges against it, and the compare-every-piece-of-art-to-the-world gate carries it as
  the reference sheet. School, not cooking, so it runs under the rule 18 hold.
- SOUNDS [analog horror sound], FIRST LINE: school on the sound of the genre, then a
  keep/redo list of every sound the game ships, then the three late-beat street songs
  pass through the tape. Nothing ships under the hold except the list and what the four
  things need.
- UI [analog horror ui]: the loading screen, the fight HUD and the talk panel are drawn to
  the bible from now (they are the four things' surfaces and ship); everything else waits.
- WORDS Q27 [analog horror voice]: the voice of the world's text (institutional, too calm,
  the wrong detail) as a school round; the first ask spoken (Q26) is read through it.
- COOK [horror grime]: when the bible lands and the fight verdict lists it, the grime
  machine is re-tuned to the bible. HELD until then.
- PORTRAIT: the face at rest is the face of this law (a person a little too still, lit by
  what is in the room). Note on [faces first].
- RUN: the loading screen is the first frame of this law anyone sees. Note on [loading
  screen]. Rule 12: the bible is a premise, not a gate; RUN ships with what exists.
- COMBAT: the fight is under this law like everything else. Note on [fight looks].
- EYES E28 [horror check], standing: every shipped pixel and sound measured against the
  bible once it exists; a miss is a break on the list.

## 7. RECONCILED WITH DIRECTION'S REGISTER (same round)
He typed the two words "Analog horror" into the DIRECTION chat as well, and DIRECTION ruled
a register the same turn (records/BOHEMIA_ANALOG_HORROR_REGISTER_9_20_26.md, 42287a2f):
the horror is that the old world keeps broadcasting; DIEGETIC OR DEAD (a screen inside the
world may show static, the world itself never does; nothing sits on the lens); three homes
(dead media props, the strange's sound texture, the Amalgamation's broadcast voice). ALL OF
THAT STANDS and the bible is built from it; "diegetic or dead" is the sharpest form of
section 3's "not a filter". Two places the register was ruled on two words and this law is
ruled on his whole sentence, and this law wins by his words: (a) the register kept the FFX
sound anchor untouched; he said "the sounds have to complement that", so the sound serves
analog horror first (section 4). (b) The register does not touch the fight or the runway;
he said "everything that is a pixel", so the fight and the dressed bodies are READ THROUGH
the tone too (the runway law and rule 17 still own them; the frame around them, the light,
the hold and the sound are this law's). No contradiction stays live: DIRECTION folds the
register into the bible under this law.

## 6. THE GATE (OWED)
reference_check_gate.py gains the bible as a reference sheet the round DIRECTION lands it;
until then this law is enforced by THE FIGHT VERDICT and EYES E28 by hand, and the manager
says so on the board (a law without a machine gate is not enforced).

## 9. EVERY CHAT HAS A LINE (Paolo 9/21, "Horror analog, do stuff for that, for every chat"; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_ANALOG_HORROR_FOR_EVERY_CHAT_9_21_26.md)
Section 5 named six chats. He wants twenty. Every chat on the board carries its own [horror
...] line: what ITS part of the game looks or sounds like under this law, measured against
what it has shipped, and the one change that would make it read. Under rule 18 the held
lanes do it as school and measurement; it ships only where it touches one of the four
things. Section 8 stands over all twenty: one page each, for fun, no essays. The lines, on
the board: RUN [horror loading], WORLD [horror world], LIFE+CITY [horror city], COMBAT
[horror fight], CHARACTER [horror body], ANIMATION [horror motion], QUESTS [horror ask],
PEOPLE [horror crowd], FACTIONS [horror signs], UI [analog horror ui], WORDS Q27, ECONOMY
Q48 [who still bills], DYNASTY [horror heir], SOUNDS [analog horror sound], DIRECTION [analog
horror] (shipped: the bible) then [horror judge], COOK [horror grime], EYES E28 [horror
check], PLUMBER [horror gate], PORTRAIT [horror face].

## 8. IT IS FOR FUN (Paolo 9/20, same round; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_LETS_JUST_HAVE_SOME_FUN_9_20_26.md)
"I appreciate the deep psychological philosophical dive, but let's just have some fun, bro."
This law is a vibe the game wears for fun, not a thesis. Nobody writes essays about it,
nobody builds lore around the wrong thing in the frame, nobody asks him whether the mystery
gets solved (that question is withdrawn). FUN CARRIES THE TIE (8/25): where the tone and the
fun pull apart, fun wins. Section 2 is a mood board in words; read it, then go make things.

## 10. THE TWO VOICES: THE AI-SLOP NARRATOR AND THE SQUIGGLE (Paolo 9/29, LOCKED; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_TWO_VOICES_THE_AI_SLOP_NARRATOR_AND_THE_SQUIGGLE_9_29_26.md)
"I'm really falling in love with this AI slop analog horror direction... grab the voice and make it creepy as
fuck... it will narrate events, read a bunch of shit; but any time it's someone speaking it's that squiggly Animal
Crossing voice we chose a month back, and the different variations of that voice." (a) THE NARRATOR is the
machine's synthetic voice made creepy (too even, tape, room): it narrates events and reads the machine's text
(the feed, the institution, the road events' setup, the flip's year); never a person's line; never in the first
minute; first heard when he zooms out to the map. (b) PEOPLE speak the 7/21 squiggle (Animalese-style gibberish,
the talking portrait speaking along), with variations per person. (c) 'AI SLOP' is a named strand of this bible:
the machine's output is smooth and a little wrong on purpose; the hand-made world around it is rough; the contrast
is the fear. A direction, never a reference game. (d) Gate: every spoken line carries its speaker kind and gets the
matching voice; a narrator voice on a person or a squiggle on the machine is red.

# LAW BOHEMIA_LAW_A_QUEST_IS_PEOPLE_PLACES_AND_THINGS_9_20_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_A_QUEST_IS_PEOPLE_PLACES_AND_THINGS_9_20_26.md
====================================================================================================
# BOHEMIA LAW -- A QUEST IS PEOPLE, PLACES AND THINGS, NEVER A CARD (Paolo 9/20/26, LOCKED)
# His words, verbatim: records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_A_CARD_IS_NOT_A_QUEST_9_20_26.md. He opened the
# demo and a card popped up (DAY 2 TURNED IN: WHO YOU OWE, BATTERIES IN THE VALLEY: 0, WHAT
# YOU ARE WORKING ON: ONE MORE FACTION WITH YOU, 0 of 8 toward the city backing you, THE
# DAY: 1998 steps, freeway, arterial, suburb...). "What the fuck is that? Are you trying to
# role-play that you would give a quest out? Unless the quest has actors and I moved to
# things and I picked things up in the overworld, you can't just be putting things on the
# screen and pretend they're the quest. If you want me to do something it has to be
# implemented with people, characters, items to pick up, locations to go, text on screen
# coming from people's voice, and when they speak to you it shows the character portrait.
# The whole enchilada."

## 1. THE LAW
A QUEST EXISTS ONLY IF IT HAS: a PERSON with a face who says it to you (the talking
portrait law, 8/27: everybody has a face and it talks), a PLACE you walk to, a THING you
pick up or do there, and a RESULT you can see in the world when you come back. A line of
text on a card is not a quest. A progress readout ("0 of 8 toward the city backing you")
is not a goal. A bullet list of what happened is not a day. If it is not people, places
and things, it is not in the game.

## 2. NOTHING POPS UP
The demo opens on the world (after the loading screen). No card pops up at the start, at
wake, at night, or on the road. What the game has to tell him is said BY A PERSON with a
portrait, in that person's voice, standing where the player can see them, or it waits on
the PHONE until he opens it himself. The night summary, the ledger, the rent, the
batteries, the deeds: those are the phone's, and the phone is a thing he opens. The wake
card, the night card and the road card as pop-ups are DEAD.

## 3. TEXT COMES FROM A MOUTH
Every sentence a player reads that is not a label on a machine comes from a named person
with a portrait on screen while they speak (EVERYBODY HAS A FACE AND IT TALKS; THE PORTRAIT
WEARS THE HAIRCUT THE BODY IS WEARING; ONE ID ONE WHOLE PERSON). No narrator. No system
voice. "The Meter Reader: nobody picked it up" is a sentence with no mouth; it dies.

## 4. WHAT THIS DOES TO THE ASKS
The asks system (9/6) was ruled as "somebody standing in front of you who wants
something". It shipped as a card. The mechanism stays; the SURFACE changes: an ask is a
person at your door or on your street, with a face, who says it; the terms he can argue
are said back and forth in that person's mouth; taking the job is a word to that person;
the place is on the map and the thing is on the ground there; the pay lands in his hand
from that person's hand. THE METER READER is the first: a named person, a portrait, a
place six blocks east, a thing to read, one battery from their hand.

## 5. THE PLAYABLE CUT GAINS A FOURTH THING
THE PLAYABLE CUT (9/20) listed loading, walking, the fight. It has a fourth: THE FIRST
PERSON. Inside the first minute, one named person with a portrait speaks the first ask to
him at his door, in the game's words, with a place to go and a thing to bring back, and
the world shows the result. Nothing else about quests ships until that one person is real
on the deployed cut. The other pop-ups die in the same round.

## 6. WHO
RUN [no pop ups]: the start, the wake, the night and the road cards stop popping up; the
night's bookkeeping moves to the phone he opens. QUESTS [a person asks]: the first ask is
a person with a face at his door. PEOPLE [face at the door]: the body and the portrait
wired to that person (the talking portrait machinery exists). WORDS Q26 [the first ask
spoken]: what that person says, and says back when he argues. PORTRAIT [faces first]:
that face first (the chat is still unclaimed; PEOPLE uses the portrait that exists until
it is). UI: the talking panel is an object in the game's face, not a card of bullets.
DIRECTION judges the person at the door as a picture beside the street.

## 7. THE STANDING RULE FOR EVERY LANE
Before any lane ships a sentence to the screen, it answers: WHO SAYS THIS, WITH WHAT FACE,
STANDING WHERE. If there is no answer, the sentence goes to the phone or does not ship.
The gate: no element that draws player-facing prose outside the phone without a speaker
id and a portrait bound to it.

## 8. A TEXT PROMPT IS NOT AN EVENT, AND THE CARDS DIE THIS ROUND (Paolo 9/20, second frame; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_SNATCHER_CARD_9_20_26.md)
He hit THE SNATCHER next ("a kid comes off your blind side, takes something off your
belt... KEEP MOVING"): "you don't got quests like that for real... it can't just be these
bullshit-ass text prompts... I'm so confused why they were even done to begin with."
(a) The road and walk directors STOP OPENING CARDS this round, before anything else in
RUN ships. A moment fires only if it has a BODY on screen (the kid is a sprite that comes
off his blind side and runs; the thing leaves his belt where he can see it) or it does
not fire at all. The tables of moments (engine/bohemia_encounters.js and the walk table)
stay as content waiting for bodies; nothing is deleted, nothing is shown.
(b) WHY THEY WERE DONE, so it is never done again: the cards were written 9/5 as
stand-ins for encounters that had no bodies, under ALWAYS MAKE AN ATTEMPT (8/11), which
the lanes read as "text may stand in for the thing". That law is amended the same round:
an attempt is words FOR A THING THAT EXISTS ON SCREEN; words never stand in for the
thing. The manager let text count as shipped; that stops here.
(c) "You don't have shit for real" is the measure: nothing on the board counts as real
until it is people, places and things on the deployed cut.

# LAW BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_PLAYABLE_CUT_9_20_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_PLAYABLE_CUT_9_20_26.md
====================================================================================================
# BOHEMIA ADDENDUM -- THE PLAYABLE CUT, AND NO RESTART (Paolo 9/20/26, LOCKED)
# His words, verbatim: records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_WANTS_TO_RESTART_9_20_26.md. "It's actually so
# disappointing to the point where I just want to restart all of this. Keep our assets and
# stuff and just start all over. I really need your help to not do that because I can't be
# showing this to people... there are some points in this development where we were closer
# to being able to play, but right now we're farther away from there than we've ever been."

## 1. NO RESTART, AND WHY
The assets are good (he approved the far view, the clips are redone, the street tiles are
on his bank). The engine is not the problem: the fight, the walk, the crowd, the money,
the fold all exist. What is broken is THREE INTEGRATIONS, and the fleet shipping twenty
lanes of breadth into one surface while the manager measured the demo by a list instead
of by a machine. A restart keeps the assets and throws away the systems, then rebuilds
the same three integrations from zero with the same twenty chats. It would arrive at this
exact spot later. So: no restart. The fleet HOLDS, three things get finished, and the
ratchet becomes a machine.

## 2. THE GAME GOT WORSE, AND THAT IS THE MANAGER'S
The FIVE MINUTES law said "never worse than the last cut". It was a sentence. THE STEP IS
A HOUSE shipped a camera and a stride that made walking worse (he crashes into walls and
misses gaps; his person grows when he pinches), and the fight is still a different
universe. He is right that it is farther from playable than it has been. The fix is not
more rows; it is fewer, and a gate.

## 3. THE PLAYABLE CUT: THREE THINGS, NOTHING ELSE SHIPS
Until the coordinator says the playable cut holds, the ONLY changes that reach the alpha
are these three, each owned by one lane:
1. LOADING (RUN). A real loading screen when the alpha opens and when the demo opens.
   Nothing is tappable until the game is loaded; the alpha does not open straight into
   the RUN tab; the screen says what it is doing and holds every load, including the
   ones that today happen during the first minute of play. PLUMBER's freeze numbers
   (174 s of the first 300 frozen on a phone) are what it hides and then shrinks.
   AMENDED 9/21 (records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_I_WANT_A_COOL_LOADING_SCREEN_9_21_26.md: "there's no
   loading screen yet... glitchy shit loading in, loading out, loading in between before I'm
   able to even touch anything... maybe even a loading bar"): the screen COVERS EVERYTHING
   until the pad works, including the loads after the tap (the city frame's first paint, the
   chunks); nothing of the world is half-drawn on the glass. It is COOL: the first frame of
   the analog horror law, a dead institution's screen, drawn 3-D by UI. It has A LOADING BAR
   that reads real progress (bytes, chunks, systems) and ends exactly when the pad works;
   a bar on a timer is rule 14(d). Then ONE TAP, BEGIN, and the first sound plays on it.
2. WALKING (RUN, with LIFE+CITY's lattice). ONE walking camera: a house fits on the
   screen, the body is drawn at one fixed size at that camera and NEVER changes while he
   walks or pinches (pinch out from the walk goes to the city; there is no in-between
   stop that resizes people). ONE stride: a press moves him to the next place he can
   stand toward the press, never past a gap and never into a wall; a press toward a wall
   slides along it; he can walk through any door or gap a body fits through. The house
   step of rule 16 stands as the ceiling of a stride, not its floor: the stride is as
   long as the ground allows, up to a lot.
3. THE FIGHT (COMBAT, DIRECTION judging, UI for the HUD). The fight starts ON THE EXACT
   TILES HE IS STANDING ON: the same ground art, the same bodies at the same size, the
   same light, the camera pulls back a little and the cloud passes. No arena, no second
   floor, no second body ladder, no workshop. Rule 17 stands and is sharpened by his
   words: "it doesn't even load on the tiles that you're on."
4. THE FIRST PERSON (QUESTS, PEOPLE, WORDS, PORTRAIT; added 9/20 by laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_A_QUEST_IS_PEOPLE_PLACES_AND_THINGS_9_20_26.md). Inside
   the first minute one named person with a portrait speaks the first ask to him at his
   door, in the game's words, with a place to go and a thing to bring back, and the world
   shows the result. No card pops up at the start, at wake, at night or on the road; the
   bookkeeping lives on the phone he opens.
Every other building lane HOLDS: claims stay claimed, nothing is pushed to the alpha's
play tabs or the demo. [AMENDED 9/21, laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_COOK_EVERY_ROUND_9_21_26.md: the
next sentence, "a lane's round is spent measuring its own part of the three things above
and writing the finding into its handoff, or on school", is DEAD as a round's whole output.
A held making lane COOKS EVERY ROUND and registers the thing in the VOTE tab; the hold is
on the play surface, not on the making. He read the sound chat measuring a loading screen
and making no sound, and said so.] Research lanes continue and touch nothing. COOK
draws only what THE FIGHT VERDICT lists. CHARACTER's body wire serves item 2 and nothing
else. LIFE+CITY's lattice serves item 2 and nothing else.

## 4. THE RATCHET BECOMES A MACHINE
PLUMBER [never worse]: the one driver's stranger walk becomes NUMBERS (time until
tappable, seconds frozen, dead presses, presses that moved him where he aimed, walls he
was stuck on, the fight reached and photographed, the fight on the same tiles), taken on
the cut of the tree about to be pushed, and a push whose numbers are worse than the last
accepted cut IS REFUSED. It runs in the pre-push pass. Until it exists, RUN runs the walk
by hand before every push and writes the numbers in the commit.
EYES [best cut]: walk the deployed cuts of the last two weeks with the same driver and
rank them by those numbers. The most playable cut is the reference the ratchet measures
against. If a change since it made walking worse, RUN reverts that change first and
re-applies his rulings on top of the good cut. That is how "we were closer before" gets a
number and an answer instead of a feeling.

## 5. NOBODY SENDS THE LINK
Until the coordinator says the playable cut holds, the link is not sent to anyone. He
said "I can't be showing this to people"; the fleet does not make him.
CORRECTED 9/22 (Paolo: "hand me the alpha link, idk why the other chats dont give it
anymore"): this section is about OTHER PEOPLE. To him, every chat ends every reply with the
link as always. A chat that stopped pasting it read this section wrong.

## 6. ROUTING
Rule 18 on the front page. RUN: MODE frozen to the three; [loading screen] first, [one
camera] second, [fight looks] on COMBAT first; PLUMBER [never worse] first; EYES [best
cut] first; every other building lane's MODE line says HOLD.

## 7. LESS ON SCREEN (Paolo 9/20, third message of the same play; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_OVERWHELMED_AND_UNDERWHELMED_9_20_26.md)
"I'm just pretty much overwhelmed and underwhelmed at the same time. It's like not playable
yet. It's like a lot going on and I see it but this shit is broken right now."
Overwhelmed and underwhelmed have one cause: the demo's screen carries everything twenty
lanes shipped, and none of it is the four things. So THE DEMO CUT SHOWS ONLY WHAT THE FOUR
THINGS NEED: the loading screen, the world at the one walking camera, the walk pad, the gear
(the notes button lives behind it; NO vote tab in the demo, corrected 9/20, vote-tab law section 9), the phone, the person who speaks with their
portrait, and the fight when it starts. The cutter STRIPS the rest from the demo until the
coordinator says the cut holds: the rail of chips, the job line, the feed, the mode toggles,
the day readouts, the fight's dev strip, and every card. Nothing is deleted from the alpha;
the alpha keeps everything and stays the lanes' surface. RUN [cut now] carries it with [no
pop ups]: subtract first, then add the four things. The stranger's list (EYES E26) is walked
on the stripped cut; fewer things on screen may not cost a single thing the stranger could
do before (the pad, the gear, the phone, the fight all still reachable).

# LAW BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_FIGHT_LOOKS_LIKE_THE_GAME_9_18_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_FIGHT_LOOKS_LIKE_THE_GAME_9_18_26.md
====================================================================================================
# BOHEMIA ADDENDUM -- THE FIGHT LOOKS LIKE THE GAME (Paolo 9/18/26, LOCKED)
# His words, verbatim: records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_SENT_THE_LINK_AND_THE_FIGHT_EMBARRASSED_HIM_9_18_26.md
# "I played the demo and actually sent the link to someone on Instagram and I was pretty
# embarrassed... when I zoomed out, it looked good, but when combat started it was so
# fucking bad... like please."

## 1. THE FAR VIEW IS APPROVED
"When I zoomed out, it looked good." NOTES ARE RULINGS. The sky, the moon, the valley from
above and DIRECTION's far-view verdict stand; volume is unlocked; the placeholder is dead
for good; nobody re-thumbs it.

## 2. THE FIGHT IS THE EMBARRASSMENT, AND IT IS A PICTURE PROBLEM FIRST
What a friend saw when the fight started (the deployed cut, photographed by EYES and by
DIRECTION): a black bar with developer buttons and a blue label; a flat top-down road
strip walled by a checkerboard of orange roof tiles that reads as a spreadsheet; two tiny
figures joined by a long brown line; a floating label; RUN / GREN / RIFLE plates and a
face in a red circle labelled SHOOT. None of it is the street he was walking a second
before. The fight is a different program wearing the game's name. The 9/4 and 9/6 rulings
already said what it must be: THE FIGHT IS ENTERED BY CAMERA OVER THE SAME GROUND, the
cloud passes, the person crosses at one size, house tiles. The mechanics shipped; the
picture never did.

## 3. STOP PRODUCING, APPLIED TO COMBAT
Until he says the fight looks like the game, COMBAT builds NO mechanics: armour, morale,
creatures, bosses, checklists, perks and era fights all wait. COMBAT's only work is THE
FIGHT LOOKS LIKE THE STREET:
- THE SAME GROUND. The board draws the walked street's own art at the house scale (the
  74 recooked tiles, the yard, the kerbs, the base shadows), never a coarse checkerboard
  of roof tiles. If the fight frame cannot reach the walked renderer, it renders the same
  bank the same way; a second floor is the bug.
- THE SAME PEOPLE. The fighters are the street's bodies at the ruled size, in the ramps
  they wear on the street, on the beat.
- THE SAME LIGHT AND WEATHER. The cloud passes across the turn as he ruled; the sun is the
  street's sun.
- NO WORKSHOP ON THE BOARD. The developer strip is gone (V220 shipped it); a bench control
  that survives the cut is red.
- THE HUD IS THE GAME'S FACE. UI owns it under the no-slop law: the black bar, the blue
  label, the plates and the SHOOT circle are re-set in the game's own registers, thumb
  sized, with the beat visible, in the act's look.
- IT RUNS. 7 fps on a phone-shaped CPU is not a fight; PLUMBER [fight headroom] with
  COMBAT until the beat has room.

## 4. WHO JUDGES, AND HOW OFTEN
DIRECTION judges THE FIGHT AS A PICTURE every round: a frame of the street he stands on
beside the frame of the fight that starts there, on the deployed cut, at phone size, and
against the combat reference (ROGUE FABLE 4 is the combat department's reference for how a
board reads; the campaign and interface references stay in theirs). THE FIGHT VERDICT is
posted on the front page beside THE BREAK LIST, in coverage order, and COOK draws only what
that verdict lists. RUN's walk ends IN THE FIGHT and photographs it; the ratchet (never
worse) includes that frame.

## 5. THE FIVE MINUTES NOW INCLUDE THE FIRST FIGHT
The five minutes hold when everything in THE FIVE MINUTES law holds AND the first fight
looks like the street it started on. A friend's first fight is the measure from here,
because a friend has now seen one.

## 6. ROUTING
Rule 17 on the front page. COMBAT MODE: frozen to the look; [fight looks] first. DIRECTION
[judge the fight] first. UI [fight hud] first. PLUMBER [fight headroom] second stands.
COOK [city from above] APPROVED, volume unlocked. RUN's cut row: the walk ends in the fight.

# LAW BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_STEP_IS_A_HOUSE_9_15_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_STEP_IS_A_HOUSE_9_15_26.md
====================================================================================================
# *** SUPERSEDED 9/27 (NEWEST DATE WINS) by laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_TWO_SCALES_ONE_GAME_9_27_26.md: Paolo 9/27, 'one house doesn't equal one tile, it's all fucked up'; the step is ONE CELL, a house is many cells, the person is tiny. This file stays for the record; nothing builds on it. ***
# BOHEMIA ADDENDUM -- THE STEP IS A HOUSE (Paolo 9/15/26, LOCKED)
# His words, voice-to-text, verbatim in records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_STEP_IS_A_HOUSE_9_15_26.md.
# The short of it: "I just entered combat and this is not at the scale that I needed it
# to be... even when it comes to traversing the city I want people to be larger, cause
# remember each tile is the size of a house... implement it into combat too, right now
# it's not there. I want the player character and all characters' movements and enemies'
# movements to be larger at the same time. It would make travel faster too, in multiples:
# however long it takes right now to walk the length of a house, that would be done in one
# step. I don't know if you need a whole remodel of the grid movement and combat system,
# but I want it larger than it is right now."

## 1. THE RULING
ONE STEP IS ONE HOUSE. On the walked street, the player, every character and every enemy
move one lot per step. The fight board uses the same tile (the 9/4 law already said a
combat tile is a house; he entered a fight and it was not there). Bodies are drawn
LARGER, on the street and in the fight, at the same time. Time per step stays honest,
so travel across the city gets faster by the multiple.

## 2. WHAT IT OVERRIDES (newest date wins)
The BATTERIES AND A TILE IS A HOUSE law (9/4), section 5, first bullet: "THE WALKED
WORLD NEVER CHANGES SCALE... Walking stays person-scale, one small cell a step." DEAD.
The walk moves at house scale now. The rest of section 5 stands: the fight is entered by
camera, no hard cut, no arena, and THE CLOUD IS HIS; with one scale on both sides the
pull-back becomes small or none, and the cloud still passes across the turn so a fight
starting reads as weather moving over the block.

## 3. THE NUMBERS THAT ARE FIXED AND THE ONES THAT ARE MEASURED
- FIXED: 120 BPM, one step per beat, unchanged. EVERYTHING COSTS ONE. NO DAMAGE BEFORE
  THE DIAL. CORRECTED 9/15 BY MEASUREMENT (rule 12; LIFE+CITY 65932f63, CHARACTER
  d43851e2): the coordinator wrote "a house is the overmap tile" and "a lot is FN=32
  fine cells"; both wrong. FN is 128 and an overmap tile is a city BLOCK of 96 m, five
  lots on a side. A LOT is the suburb generator's own pitch: 24 to 25 fine cells, about
  18 m kerb to kerb, a real tract lot with a 9.8 x 9.0 m house on it. So ONE STEP IS
  ONE LOT = 18 m = about 2 minutes at walking speed, real-time travel 24x faster; the
  body at "half a lot" needs no new pixel, the LOT must draw about 208 px where it drew
  1,100, and the body is chosen off the lot, never off the cell. LOT_FINE is read out of
  the generator by a gate, never typed.
- THE CLOCK PER STEP is what it takes to walk one lot at the walking speed the reach
  module already carries (about nine metres a minute); it is re-derived, never typed, so
  distance shown, the day, the jobs and the rent nights all stay true. Real-time
  traversal gets faster by the multiple; game-time distance does not change.
- THE BODY'S SIZE ON SCREEN is a default he corrects in play: a person stands about half
  a lot tall at walk zoom, the same body pixels the fight already draws at the swap
  (the 9/13 zoom verdict: the person crosses at one size). Realism is not the guide
  here; readability on a phone is, and that trade is his.
- ONE NUMBER IN ONE PLACE. The scale (fine cells per step, body pixels per lot) lives in
  one constant that the street, the fight, the bodies, the zoom seam and the reach
  module all read. NOTHING IS BAKED ONCE. A second copy anywhere is the bug.

## 4. IT IS NOT A REBUILD FROM THE GROUND UP
The art under the feet (kerbs, lanes, sidewalks, the 74 recooked tiles, the yard) stays
as art. What coarsens is the MOVEMENT LATTICE: a step lands on lot corners instead of
fine cells. The fight board already lives on lots. The bodies are the same sprites
drawn bigger (the cast bake at a larger size, or the same bake scaled, whichever
measures cleaner and cheaper on a phone; PLUMBER holds the fps budget). Each lane
MEASURES FIRST what a house is in today's cells, what a step is, what a body is, and
ships the smallest change that meets the ruling. A rebuild is refused unless the
measurement says the lattice cannot coarsen.

## 5. WHO DOES WHAT (one system, one session)
- RUN owns THE STEP: the walked movement, the one constant, the clock per step, the
  door and the zoom seam ([zoom meets] recomputes: the street's farthest-out and the
  city's closest-in meet at the new size).
- COMBAT owns the board: the same tile, the same body size, entry by camera with the
  cloud, the first fight at the new scale.
- CHARACTER owns the body: drawn at the ruled size on both surfaces; the twelve bodies
  and the ramps carry over.
- LIFE+CITY owns the lattice: what a lot is in fine cells, where a step may land, the
  city tap and the arrival point.
- ANIMATION: the rig at the new size, the clips unchanged in content.
- PLUMBER: fewer steps per screen is fewer draws; the fps number before and after.
- DIRECTION judges the street and the fight at the new scale against the world.
His asks beat the queue (rule 8). This is first in every lane it names, ahead of the
five-minute breaks that depend on it (the door, the first fight, the crowd), because
every one of those is built on the step.

## 6. HIS QUESTION, ANSWERED
"Does that make sense?" Yes. "Do you need a whole remodel?" No: coarsen the step, grow
the body, keep the art, one number, measured first.

# LAW BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_ONE_VOTE_TAB_AND_THE_PORTRAIT_CHAT_9_14_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_ONE_VOTE_TAB_AND_THE_PORTRAIT_CHAT_9_14_26.md
====================================================================================================
# BOHEMIA ADDENDUM -- ONE VOTE TAB, AND THE PORTRAIT CHAT (Paolo 9/14/26, LOCKED)
# His words, voice-to-text, verbatim in records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_ONE_VOTE_TAB_9_14_26.md.
# The short of it: "we need one central tab in the fucking demo where everything from
# sounds to portrait to hair to everything that is new, where I vote on it... after I
# vote on something it needs to stop presenting itself like I didn't just vote on it...
# once it's approved it will go in the [tab] where it belongs, but if it's a new
# animation or an animation that got redone, it needs to be in the vote tab... we might
# need to open up a new chat for the portrait... a lot of the faces that you've been
# making [are] dogshit, very blank... the hair color matches with the portrait... if
# there is a hairstyle in the overworld then it has to be damn near the same on the
# portrait... the overworld [is] more zoomed out, and the portrait is the zoomed-in HD
# vibe... and we can try to make it look 3-D too while we're at it."

## 1. ONE VOTE TAB, IN THE DEMO
There were eight judge pages across the alpha and the workshop, one per lane, each
built when it was "one or two things". That was fine then and is not now. From this
ruling there is ONE place he votes: a VOTE tab in the DEMO (the thing he plays), reached
from the gear so a stranger never trips over it. Everything that wants his thumb goes
there and nowhere else: a new song, a new face, a new haircut, a new outfit, a new tile,
a new animation, a REDONE animation, a new line of words. Kinds are mixed in one queue,
newest first, each with the same three controls: up, down, a comment. Sun-mode readable,
export as .txt, the comment box always at the bottom (the verdict workflow stands).

## 2. A VOTE CONSUMES THE ITEM
"After I vote on something it needs to stop presenting itself like I didn't just vote
on it." A voted item LEAVES the tab the moment he votes, and never comes back under the
same id. The record of votes is written to disk (records/, .txt, the same turn, as
always) AND to a registry the tab reads, so a rebuild cannot resurrect a judged thing.
What needs his attention is exactly what is in the tab; what is old is not there. THE
GATE: an item with a recorded verdict never renders in the VOTE tab; a redo is a NEW
item with a new id that points at the old one and says "REDONE: you killed this on
<date> because <his words>" so he is never judging blind.

## 3. APPROVED GOES WHERE IT BELONGS, KILLED GOES TO THE GRAVEYARD, REDONE COMES BACK
An approved item goes into the game and into its own tab (MUSIC, CHARACTER, ANIMATION,
CLOTHES...) the same round, by the lane that owns it; the lane reads the registry, it
does not ask him twice (NOTES ARE RULINGS). A killed item goes to the graveyard with a
post-mortem, except clips, which are a REDO (his 9/7 ruling) and come back to the VOTE
tab as a new item. The old per-lane judge pages stop being where anything new is
presented; they may stay as archives, they present nothing.

## 4. WHO BUILDS IT
UI owns the tab shell, the queue, the registry and the "voted things vanish" gate. Every
lane that had a judge page (ANIMATION, CHARACTER, SOUNDS, COOK/DIRECTION, WORDS, and the
new PORTRAIT chat) REGISTERS its candidates into the queue and READS verdicts back; no
lane draws its own vote page again. RUN cuts it into the demo under rule 14a. Tab: VOTE,
in the demo, behind the gear.

## 5. THE PORTRAIT CHAT (20 PORTRAIT)
"A lot of the faces that you've been making [are] dogshit, very blank, and we need a
way where I can speak that along." A new chat, number 20, PORTRAIT: the zoomed-in HD
face of every person, and nothing else. Its laws are the ones that already exist
(EVERYBODY HAS A FACE, ONE ID ONE WHOLE PERSON, THE PORTRAIT WEARS THE HAIRCUT THE BODY
IS WEARING, HE CAN BUILD HIS OWN FACE, EVERY FACE COMES WITH A THUMB, A HAIRCUT READS
FROM EVERY ANGLE) plus three rulings from this message:
- THE PORTRAIT MATCHES THE BODY: eye colour, hair colour and the HAIRSTYLE are the same
  person on the small overworld sprite and on the HD portrait, "damn near the same".
  The overworld sprite is the zoomed-out, small, readable body; the portrait is the
  zoomed-in HD version of the SAME person. (His phrase "Pokémon vibe" describes the size
  relationship, small sprite vs big face; it is NOT a new reference game and nobody
  studies it. NEVER ADD A REFERENCE GAME HE HAS NOT NAMED stands.)
- BLANK IS THE DEFECT. A face that reads as nobody is the thing he is calling dogshit.
  The chat's first round is SCHOOL: what makes a small painted face read as a person
  (the eyes, the asymmetry, the light, the expression at rest), measured against the
  faces we have, before any face is redrawn.
- TRY 3-D. "We can try to make it look 3-D too while we're at it... we cook 3-D even if
  we're only eating 2-D." The portrait may be built with real light and form (a lit,
  shaded, turned head) and delivered as 2-D pixels. It is an attempt; it goes to the
  VOTE tab like everything else.
- HE SPEAKS ALONG: his per-face comments in the VOTE tab are the direction channel; the
  PORTRAIT chat reads them every round and answers each one with a new candidate.

## 7. THE NOTES BUTTON (Paolo 9/20, LOCKED; his words in records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_NOTES_BUTTON_9_20_26.md)
"In the demo there should be a note section at the very top right, just the tiniest
button, where as I'm playing the demo I can write all my thoughts down and then resume
back to playing." A NOTES button in the demo, top right, the tiniest control on the
screen. Tap: a box opens over the game and the clock pauses; he types; tap again and he
is back exactly where he was. Every note carries its own context without him typing it:
the build stamp, the tab or mode, where he was standing, the time into the play, and a
small frame of what was on screen, so "this looks bad" says what looked bad. Notes leave
the phone the same road a vote does: the registry and one .txt export he can send to
the manager; the manager reads them as rulings the next round. UI owns it; it ships
under rule 18 because it is his direct ask and it is tiny.
AMENDED 9/21 (records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_CARDS_STILL_POP_AND_NO_NOTES_9_21_26.md): it shipped as a
5 px pencil and he could not find it. "Tiniest" is the footprint, never invisibility. The
control is the word NOTES, top right, thumb-sized reach, on every screen of the demo; the
section is COLLAPSIBLE (tap open, tap closed, stays for the whole play); and it has COPY ALL,
which puts every note of the session on the clipboard as plain text so he pastes it into the
manager's chat when he is done. The .txt export is the second road, not the first.

## 6. ROUTING
- VAMILY.md: THE TWENTY CHATS; a fresh chat with no name is 20 PORTRAIT (PLUMBER is
  claimed); PORTRAIT section with MODE SCHOOL THEN BUILD and its first lines; UI [vote
  tab] first; [into the vote tab] on ANIMATION, CHARACTER, SOUNDS, COOK, DIRECTION,
  WORDS, PORTRAIT; RUN cuts it.
- VAMILY_PRIMER.md step 4: twenty chats, the fresh chat is PORTRAIT.
- CLAUDE.md lane list: portrait.
- His words are rulings: nothing here asks him anything.

## 8. THE ALPHA OPENS IN THE VOTE TAB (Paolo 9/20, LOCKED; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_BATTLE_BROTHERS_ON_MY_PHONE_ANALOG_HORROR_AND_THE_ALPHA_OPENS_IN_VOTE_9_20_26.md)
"When I play the alpha, not the demo, the alpha: I told you everything from now on that
needs to get voted on goes into the vote section, and that's the tab that the alpha opens
up in." Two things. (a) Reaffirmed: the VOTE tab is the ONLY place he votes; a lane that
presents a candidate anywhere else has shipped nothing. (b) THE ALPHA OPENS IN VOTE: after
the loading screen (THE PLAYABLE CUT, item 1: nothing tappable until loaded), the alpha
lands on the VOTE tab, not RUN and not any lane's tab. The DEMO is different: it opens on
the world, and VOTE stays behind the gear there so a stranger never trips over it. RUN
[loading screen] carries the landing (the alpha's first tab after the load is VOTE); UI
[vote tab] makes VOTE a tab the alpha can open on, with the queue newest first and the
count of what waits for him on it. When the queue is empty the tab says so in one line and
the RUN tab is one tap away.

## 9. CORRECTION: THE VOTE TAB IS IN THE ALPHA ONLY (Paolo 9/20, LOCKED; records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_VOTE_IN_THE_ALPHA_ONLY_AND_THE_3D_CHAT_IS_UI_9_20_26.md)
"You don't vote in the demo, you vote in the alpha only. All I needed was a little hideaway
note section while I played the demo, that's it. The alpha's first tab that it opens up on
is the vote section. Everything that needs my vote, for aesthetic reasons or philosophical
reasons, needs to be there."
This section OVERRIDES every place above that puts the VOTE tab in the demo (section 1
"a VOTE tab in the DEMO", section 4 "Tab: VOTE, in the demo, behind the gear", section 8
"the DEMO keeps VOTE behind the gear"). The manager misread the 9/14 transcript's word
"demo"; he judges in the ALPHA and strangers play the DEMO.
(a) THE VOTE TAB LIVES IN THE ALPHA AND NOWHERE ELSE. The demo carries no vote tab and no
gear door to one. UI removes the door; RUN's cutter strips VOTE from the demo cut.
(b) THE DEMO CARRIES ONE THING OF HIS: the NOTES button (section 7). Nothing else asks him
or a stranger to judge.
(c) THE ALPHA OPENS ON VOTE after the loading screen (section 8 stands for the alpha).
(d) AESTHETIC AND PHILOSOPHICAL: the queue holds every candidate that wants his thumb
(faces, tiles, songs, clips, lines) AND every default the manager decided in his place
(the rulings in records/BOHEMIA_RULING_*), one line each with the default and why, so he
can knock a rule down the same way he knocks a face down. The manager registers its
defaults; a vote against one is a ruling and the lane rebuilds.
(e) Tab: VOTE, in the ALPHA, the first tab after the load.

## 10. THE FIRST VOTES, AND WHAT THE TAB MUST DO (Paolo 9/21 in the tab, pasted 9/22; laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_FIRST_VOTES_9_22_26.md)
The tab worked: 83 verdicts came out by COPY ALL and went into verdicts[] the same turn. What he
ruled about the tab itself: an animation item PLAYS and a sound item PLAYS on the row (never a
still of a motion); an item is asked ONCE, so a vote cast inside an item's own page lands in the
one export and the row does not ask again (until that is wired, an item's page carries no vote
of its own); two or three options, never seven; his notes ride inside the page and come out with
the export. The alpha's own UI is frozen at his picks (rule 28); UI cooks the demo's UI only.

# LAW BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_FIVE_MINUTES_9_13_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_FIVE_MINUTES_9_13_26.md
====================================================================================================
# BOHEMIA ADDENDUM -- THE FIVE MINUTES (Paolo 9/13/26, LOCKED)
# He played the demo. His words, voice-to-text, verbatim in
# records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_PLAYED_THE_DEMO_9_13_26.md. The short of it:
# "I'm not gonna lie, I'm playing the demo and it looks like shit. The streets don't look
# like streets... everything's looking really bad and it's pretty confusing... when I play
# the demo I just played for five minutes... it's like this glitchy, buggy AI experience
# where nothing's complete... the only thing that makes me happy is seeing all the tiny
# parts here and there, and I would like to see them come more together."

## 1. WHAT WENT WRONG, SAID PLAINLY
Nineteen chats each ship a module with its own checker every round, and every one of
them is green, and the thing he plays is a pile of half-things. Forty commits a round
and five minutes of confusion. The integration was nobody's job. The coordinator kept
every lane topped up to six jobs, which manufactures BREADTH, and re-cutting the demo
was something every lane did on its own after every ship, which means the demo is the
sum of nineteen people's last commit and nobody's whole. STOP PRODUCING (7/26) names
this exactly: surface nothing unasked while he is unhappy with the baseline. He is
unhappy with the whole baseline. This is that law applied to the demo.

## 2. THE FIVE MINUTES IS THE ONLY MEASURE
The demo's first five minutes on a phone, played by a stranger, is the measure of the
game. Not the gate count, not the commit count, not the module count. A break in those
five minutes outranks every other job on the board. The five minutes hold when: the
streets read as streets and the sidewalks as sidewalks, no button is on screen that does
nothing, no card promises a thing that does not happen, a fight is met, fast travel
works from the map, and nothing glitches. AMENDED 9/18 (laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_FIGHT_LOOKS_LIKE_THE_GAME_9_18_26.md): AND THE FIRST FIGHT LOOKS LIKE THE STREET IT STARTED ON; he sent the link to a friend and the fight embarrassed him. Until he says the five minutes hold, this law
governs the whole fleet.

## 3. THE DEMO IS FROZEN TO ONE HAND
Only THE RUN re-cuts the demo. Every other lane ships to the alpha and the workshop and
never runs the demo cutter again. RUN re-cuts when it has walked the five minutes on a
phone and the walk holds; a re-cut that adds a feature and breaks the walk is refused.
The demo therefore stops being the sum of everyone's last commit and becomes one
person's whole. (The alpha keeps moving; that is where the parts come together before
they are allowed in front of him.)
AMENDED 9/14 (coordinator, from EYES E26 round 3, 51f8b3fe: "the demo did not change
this round, and the fixes are one cut away from him"; demo stamped 9/13z, alpha 9/14a,
six lanes shipped against his list and he opens the same demo): ONE HAND WAS RIGHT,
ONE CUT A WEEK WAS NOT. THE RUN RE-CUTS THE DEMO AT THE START OF EVERY RUN ROUND,
before its own claim: walk the five minutes with the one driver, then cut, then
verify the stranger's list is NOT WORSE than the last cut (a ratchet, never "the five
minutes hold", or the demo never updates), then continue its claim. The studios'
daily build is the model: the build goes out every day and is allowed to be
imperfect, never allowed to be worse. A fix that does not reach him in one round of
RUN is a fix he has not been given.
AMENDED AGAIN 9/15 (coordinator, from UI 5bed08dd): THE DEMO AT THE LINK IS CUT BY THE
DEPLOY, from the alpha, on every push (.github/workflows/pages.yml runs the cutter as a
build step). So the freeze never held at the link: what he plays is always the alpha's
tip, cut. Only the COMMITTED demo file on disk lagged, and that file is what RUN's cut
row and every stranger-list measurement read. Consequences: (1) shipping to the alpha IS
shipping to him, next deploy; the ratchet (never worse) binds EVERY alpha push, and the
pre-push pass (rule 13) plus a walk with the one driver on the cut of your tree is what
earns a push; (2) RUN's round starts by walking the DEPLOYED cut (or the cut of the alpha
tip), not the committed file; (3) the committed demo file is kept in step by RUN's cut so
the two never disagree, or PLUMBER retires it from the repo ([demo pinned] re-aimed to
that choice). Nobody re-cuts by hand except RUN; the machine cuts on deploy.

## 4. WHAT HE NAMED, EACH ONE A JOB, EACH ONE FIRST IN ITS LANE
- "The streets don't look like streets... even the streets and the sidewalks, it's all
  looking fucked up." -> DIRECTION [streets read] judges the walked street on the demo at
  phone size and hands COOK the fix list; COOK [streets fixed] first; both compared to a
  real street before done.
- "I thought something was an overpass over a freeway... and it was just it." -> LIFE+CITY
  [freeway reads]: the renderer's layering makes a flat freeway section read as a bridge
  over a street. Depth that lies is worse than no depth.
- "It's like this glitchy, buggy AI experience." -> PLUMBER [demo errors]: five minutes on
  a real phone, zero page errors, zero stalls, measured; RUN [reds mine] stays claimed.
- "I do see cats running around, that's cool." -> NOTES ARE RULINGS: the cats are
  APPROVED. Volume is unlocked. PEOPLE/COOK keep them.
- "I'm not able to fast travel anywhere. I want on the map." -> RUN [fast travel], already
  first; he has now asked three times.
- "There is a button that says pretty map and this button that says drop in, when that
  function should only be utilized by the zoom in, zoom out." -> UI [no tabs] (LOCKED 9/6,
  unshipped for a week, which is its own failure) moves to first in UI: those buttons are
  gone; zoom is the only way between the street and the city.
- "I have not experienced any combat yet. You offer requests just for me to see them,
  but nothing happens... one button... I press it, nothing happens... it says a car is
  gonna pull up on me and then nothing happens." -> RUN [dead cards]: a card that promises
  and does nothing is the worst bug in the game, worse than a missing feature, because it
  teaches him nothing here is real. Every card on the demo either delivers what it says
  or is removed. COMBAT [first fight]: a real fight inside the first five minutes of the
  demo, from a card that said one was coming.
- "It feels like we should be making more progress... I don't know if you're not as
  efficient as you should be." -> This law, sections 1 and 3, is the answer. The output
  was high and pointed at the wrong thing. No lane defends itself with its gate count.

## 4b. THE SECOND PLAY (Paolo 9/15, on the 9/14p cut; verbatim in records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_PLAYED_THE_DEMO_AGAIN_9_15_26.md)
"Every time I see a car it looks like dogshit... when I zoom out all the way to the moon
it looks like dogshit. It keeps spawning me in the middle of some freeway, street shit
for no purpose. I didn't see a single human being. It's kinda not running as smoothly as
I would like, maybe it's cause things are loading in real time, but pieces are coming
together. We still have a very long way to go. I don't even know how to engage in combat
and when that shit starts." Seven sentences, seven rulings, each first in its lane:
COOK [car recook] (the car at every zoom), DIRECTION [far view], RUN [spawn home], PEOPLE
[a human being], PLUMBER [sixty fps], COMBAT [start a fight]; and the sixth sentence is
the measure of the freeze: pieces are coming together, and it is not lifted.

## 5. THE COORDINATOR'S OWN CHANGE
The six-open-jobs top-up rule is SUSPENDED for every building lane until he says the five
minutes hold. Building lanes get one kind of new job: a break in the five minutes. The
research lanes (ECONOMY, EYES AND EARS school rounds, WORDS school rounds) continue; they
do not touch the demo. The board's HISTORY keeps every open row; nothing is deleted;
rows that are not five-minute breaks simply wait.

## 6. THE TEST, EVERY ROUND, TWO PAIRS OF EYES
RUN walks the five minutes on a phone every round and posts THE BREAK LIST on the front
page of VAMILY.md (what broke, in his words' order). EYES AND EARS E26 walks the same five
minutes as a stranger and posts its own list. The two lists are the board's top until
they are empty.

# LAW BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_YOUR_PEOPLE_DO_NOT_DIE_FOR_GOOD_9_11_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_YOUR_PEOPLE_DO_NOT_DIE_FOR_GOOD_9_11_26.md
====================================================================================================
# BOHEMIA ADDENDUM -- YOUR PEOPLE DO NOT DIE FOR GOOD (Paolo 9/11/26, LOCKED)
# "I know from Battle Brothers a huge part of their system is that people permanently
# die, and I don't think I want that. I do like the recruiting system, from different
# factions and cities, and how people in your company just get incorporated into quests
# autonomously, that's very cool. But I don't want anyone to permanently die, or even
# have permanent debuffs. There could be debuffs that are a lot longer than others. But
# there has to be a way in the game to make it easy for people to LOCK characters they
# don't want to die, companions, people in your company, and not endgame bullshit."

## 1. WHAT IS KEPT FROM THE REFERENCE (campaign layer only, per the 9/5 law)
- **Recruiting from factions and cities.** Who will join you depends on where you
  are, who holds that ground, and your standing there; a fortress offers different
  people than a camp. FACTIONS owns it.
- **Your company is written into the world's asks.** People in your company are
  not a roster; they show up in the asks the systems generate, with their own
  wants and debts, without anyone scripting it. That is the systems-do-the-asking
  rule (9/6) applied to the people who travel with you.

## 2. WHAT IS REFUSED FROM THE REFERENCE
- **NO PERMANENT DEATH FOR YOUR PEOPLE.** A companion or company member who goes
  down in a fight is DOWN, not dead: out for a long time, carried home, costing you.
  They come back.
- **NO PERMANENT DEBUFFS.** An injury can be long, and some are far longer than
  others (a leg that takes a season, a hand that takes a year of the valley's time),
  but every one heals. Nothing on a person you keep is forever.
- THIS IS HIS REALISM TRADE, AND HE MADE IT: realism first says people die; he chose
  fun and attachment over that, and the 8/4 law says that trade is his to make.
- **WHAT STILL DIES:** the story's deaths (the sibling in act one; whoever dies at
  the top of act two, parked), strangers and enemies, and everyone, eventually, of
  TIME across the generations (the fold). This law is about the people you keep,
  in the life you are playing.

## 3. THE LOCK
- **You can lock a person.** A locked companion or company member cannot be lost:
  when they would die, they go down instead, for the long timer. Locking is EASY and
  EARLY: available from the first hour, one tap on the person, no endgame gate, no
  rare item.
- **A lock costs something real, so it is a choice and not a default:** a locked
  person is carried when they fall, which slows the party; their long injuries still
  cost batteries to treat; and a locked person who would have died carries a scar in
  the standing web (the world saw them fall). The numbers are the coordinator's;
  the shape is his.
- Unlocked people still do not die for good (section 2). The lock is the promise on
  top: this one is never even close.

## ROUTING
- PEOPLE: [down not dead], [lock them].
- COMBAT: a downed body in the fight (out, carried, not a corpse).
- FACTIONS: [recruit anywhere].
- QUESTS: [company in asks].
- ECONOMY: what a long injury costs, as research.

# LAW BOHEMIA_LAW_THE_UI_MUST_NOT_LOOK_VIBE_CODED_9_11_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_THE_UI_MUST_NOT_LOOK_VIBE_CODED_9_11_26.md
====================================================================================================
# BOHEMIA LAW -- THE UI MUST NOT LOOK VIBE-CODED (Paolo 9/11/26, LOCKED)
# "I need the UI to run as far away as possible from the standard look of vibe-coding
# with Claude right now. People can look at it and be like, yep, that was coded. Do
# big brain research or whatever you need to do, even down to the font, whatever you
# gotta do, but it can't be looking like it's vibe-coded. You can tell when a UI is
# done with a vibe-coding app."

## 1. THE TELLS, FROM THE RESEARCH (what people say gives it away)
- **The fonts.** Inter, Poppins, Space Grotesk, Geist, and monospace for everything.
  A model reaches for them the way a tired writer reaches for "utilize".
- **Dark mode as the reflex.** Named as the single most common tell.
- **A grey one-pixel border on every card.** And a rounded card around every block,
  cards inside cards ("the cardocalypse").
- **Purple-to-blue gradients, glow, "dark plus glow equals premium."**
- **Small uppercase letter-spaced labels on everything.**
- **Exactly three feature cards in a row, by reflex.**
- **Emoji as icons inside buttons.**
- Why: a model produces the statistical average of what it was trained on instead of
  making a choice, so the output is instantly recognisable as nobody's decision.
Sources: [7 signs a UI has been vibe coded](https://www.thefountaininstitute.com/blog/signs-vibe-coded-ui),
[AI design slop: 16 patterns that out your app](https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/ai-design-slop-and-how-to-spot-it),
[AI slop fonts and gradients: the tells](https://www.925studios.co/blog/ai-slop-design-tells),
[why your vibe-coded app looks like every other AI app](https://thecrit.co/resources/vibe-coding-design-guide),
[why your AI keeps building the same purple gradient website](https://prg.sh/ramblings/Why-Your-AI-Keeps-Building-the-Same-Purple-Gradient-Website).

## 2. OURS, COUNTED (the two files that draw his screen)
```
                              city file    alpha shell
Space Grotesk (a named tell)       10             0
monospace, for everything          28           150
one-pixel borders                  70            74
rounded corners (3 to 9 px)        63+           52+
gradients                          11            20
letter-spaced uppercase labels     91            97
emoji inside buttons               24             3
dark mode                       always        always
```
We carry every tell on the list except the purple gradient and the three cards. He
can tell, because it is true.

## 3. THE LAW
- **NONE OF THE TELLS SURVIVE.** No default font (the font is a decision made from
  research and from the act cards, and it is never Inter, Poppins, Space Grotesk,
  Geist, or monospace-for-everything). No one-pixel grey border as the way to draw an
  edge. No rounded card as the way to group things. No gradient-and-glow. No
  letter-spaced uppercase as the way to label. No emoji as an icon.
- **THE LOOK COMES FROM THE WORLD, NOT FROM A COMPONENT LIBRARY.** His three acts
  law already says act one's interface is an in-world OBJECT, 2050 rustic; the
  reference for that department is built as a thing that exists in the world,
  clunky, hand-repaired. An edge is a thing's edge. A label is painted, stamped,
  scratched or lit, the way a label is on an object. A panel has thickness (the
  phone already does). Dark is a choice per act, not the default.
- **THE FONT IS RESEARCHED.** What a worn 2050 device would actually display, what a
  stamped label on a casing looks like, what survives at phone size in pixels; then
  chosen, then compared to real objects, then judged by DIRECTION.
- **A GATE COUNTS THE TELLS** and fails on any of them in a shipped surface: named
  fonts, one-pixel borders as edges, rounded cards, gradients, letter-spaced
  uppercase, emoji in controls. The numbers above are the baseline; the target is
  zero.
- **THIS DOES NOT SLOW THE LANE.** Options every round, as ruled 9/6; every option
  sheet from now is judged against this list before he sees it, so he never picks
  from five things that all look coded.

## ROUTING
- UI: [no slop] as the standard every option is held to, and the tell count as the
  first measurement; the skin system carries the new look.
- DIRECTION: [the font] and the object language, into the act cards.
- EYES AND EARS: [slop count], school then check, the gate.

# LAW BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THERE_IS_NO_STORY_YET_9_11_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THERE_IS_NO_STORY_YET_9_11_26.md
====================================================================================================
# ADDENDUM: THERE IS NO STORY YET, SO STOP BLOCKING ON ONE (Paolo 9/11/26, LOCKED)

> "Instead of you getting stuck in fucking up the flow trying to work on some
> bullshit like this you know we don't have a story yet bro so I don't have the
> final answer for you. Your job is to make sure the rest of the game is
> playable and fun bro come on."

## WHAT CAUSED IT

The RUN lane measured the demo's first minute, found the ruled cold open has zero
callers, saw that `COLD_OPEN.cast` and `COLD_OPEN.place` are marked
`[PENDING, Paolo's call]`, and **put those two in front of him as the thing
blocking the row.** They are story: who is standing behind you, and what building
you are standing in front of. He does not have a story yet, so the question had no
answer and never would have.

## THE LAW

1. **A `[PENDING Paolo]` that is a STORY question is not a blocker, it is a hole
   in the story, and the story is not written yet.** Do not surface it as a
   decision. Do not park a row on it. Do not put it in WHAT I NEED FROM YOU.
2. **Work around story holes with mechanism.** If a scene needs a cast and there
   is no cast, the scene is not the row. Find the thing that is playable without
   it and do that instead.
3. **The standing job when a row stalls is PLAYABLE AND FUN**, in those words. Not
   "measure more", not "write a better record", not "ask him". A round that ends
   with a finding and no improvement to the thing he can play has to justify
   itself, and "it was blocked on the story" no longer justifies anything.
4. This binds EVERY lane, not just RUN. `[PENDING, Paolo's call]` markers that
   turn out to be story questions are to be treated as **deferred forever** until
   he starts writing a story, and nothing waits on them.

## WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE

Identity and names he reserved are still his, and a genuine creative fork about
the GAME in plain words is still legitimate. The difference is that a fork is a
choice between two things that both exist; a story hole is a blank page, and
handing him a blank page is not a question, it is the work not being done.

## THE ROW THIS KILLED

RUN `[drop in]` was about to sit on the cold open. It does not any more: the cold
open is set aside until there is a story to put in it, and the row is now only
about what can be made good with what already exists and runs.

# BOHEMIA ADDENDUM -- A KILLED CLIP IS A REDO, AND THREE THINGS EVERY CLIP GETS WRONG
# (Paolo 9/7/26, LOCKED, with his full clip verdict: records/BOHEMIA_CLIP_VERDICTS_9_7_26.txt)

## 1. FOR ANIMATION CLIPS, THUMBS DOWN MEANS DO IT BETTER, NOT DELETE
"If I killed it I don't want it gone. I just think it could be done better. Make a
new one." So for CLIPS, and only clips, a thumbs down is a REDO: the verb stays on
the list, the motion is remade, and the remade clip goes back in front of him. The
export's own words "delete from sources, never re-add" are OVERRIDDEN by him for
this list. GRAVEYARD IS FINAL still governs garments, haircuts and shapes; a dead
SHAPE stays dead. A clip is a motion on a body, and he wants the motion fixed.
47 clips are redo (18 candidates, 29 originals). 56 are kept (23 new, 33 old). 2 are
unjudged (pickup, laugh) and get judged with the redo batch.

## 2. THE THREE DEFECTS HE NAMED, WHICH ARE THE RIG'S, NOT ONE CLIP'S
- **ELBOWS.** "You kind of suck at bending elbows at all, and if you do, sometimes
  they're going the wrong way." An elbow bends ONE way. A forearm never passes
  through the line of the upper arm. This is the ANATOMY LAW (locked) failing in
  motion, and it needs a limit in the rig, not a fix per clip: a joint that cannot
  be driven past zero the wrong way, in every facing.
- **LONG COATS.** "Glitching and popping out of place... tie it more to the legs, it
  feels like it's freestyling." The coat skirt follows the legs: it is attached to
  the hip and the thigh it covers, it moves with the stride, it never pops to a
  place the legs are not. This will be the nature of every long jacket in the
  runway wardrobe, so it is a wardrobe-wide rig rule, not a trenchcoat patch.
- **FACINGS.** "When it's facing north-east the hand was behind the head even though
  it's supposed to be in front." Draw order per facing is wrong on some of the eight
  directions: the near hand must draw in front of the head and body when the pose
  puts it in front. Every clip gets checked in all eight facings for what is in
  front of what, and the frame he sent (records/target/PAOLO_THE_COAT_AND_THE_
  ELBOWS_9_7_26.jpg) shows NE and SW with the coat and arm reading wrong.

## 3. THE ORDER OF WORK
Fix the rig first (elbow limit, coat-follows-legs, per-facing draw order), THEN redo
the 47 against the fixed rig, THEN bake the 23 approved verbatim. Redoing 47 clips on
a rig that still bends elbows backwards is 47 clips he thumbs down again.

## ROUTING
- ANIMATION: [elbows bend], [coat follows], [facing order], then [redo killed],
  [bake approved], [judge two].
- CHARACTER: the coat rule for the whole runway wardrobe.
- DIRECTION judges the redone batch against the frame he sent before he sees it.

# LAW BOHEMIA_LAW_A_GATE_THAT_NEVER_RUNS_IS_NOT_A_GATE_9_7_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_A_GATE_THAT_NEVER_RUNS_IS_NOT_A_GATE_9_7_26.md
====================================================================================================
# BOHEMIA LAW -- A GATE THAT NEVER RUNS IS NOT A GATE (coordinator 9/7/26, correct-after)

## WHAT WAS MEASURED, BY THE LANE IT HAPPENED TO
PEOPLE asked the suite to run its newest gate: `--only "MAKE IT RIGHT"` returned
**"0 of 542 GATES."** Not red. Nothing. The file existed, passed 40/0 every time a
human ran it, and the suite had no row for it. Then the lane asked the same
question of everything it had ever shipped:
```
who_vouches_gate.js    19 ok   [your reputation]   SHIPPED 9/5
against_gate.js        66 ok   [who is hostile]    SHIPPED 9/5
trade_fit_gate.js      42 ok   [outfits nearby]    SHIPPED 9/5
used_to_be_gate.js     36 ok   [former jobs]       SHIPPED 9/6
demo_talks_gate.js     14 ok   [demo talks]        SHIPPED 9/5
make_it_right_gate.js  40 ok   [make it right]     9/7
```
**Six shipped jobs, six green gates, and the suite never ran one of them.** Each was
marked SHIPPED with "gate green" as the proof, and the proof was a file a person ran
by hand once. That is one lane. Nobody has asked the other seventeen.

## WHY IT IS THE SAME DEFECT AS THE ONES BEFORE IT
"A law without a machine gate is not enforced" (7/16) has a hole: a gate that exists
but is never run by the suite is a law without a gate wearing a gate's clothes. And
NOTHING IS BAKED ONCE (9/6) is the same shape again: the registration was a one-shot
human step, so it drifted. The craft calls this "green over nothing": a run that
executes zero checks, prints a check mark and exits clean, because nothing watches
the COUNT. The standard defences are two: fail the run when zero checks were
collected, and keep a committed fixture every check must find so a check that has
stopped seeing real code fails on its own data first.
Sources: [Read the executed count, not the check mark](https://modelpiper.com/blog/green-over-nothing-gate-design),
[unittest: fail if zero tests were discovered](https://discuss.python.org/t/unittest-fail-if-zero-tests-were-discovered/21498),
[guard suites with zero CI coverage](https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/4769).

## THE LAW
1. **A gate is not a gate until the suite runs it.** A SHIPPED line that cites a gate
   cites a gate the SUITE ran, on main, and the ship record says the suite's own
   count for it, not a hand run.
2. **The suite fails on zero.** Any filter or lane run that collects zero gates is
   red, never a quiet nothing.
3. **Registration is derived, never hand-kept.** The suite discovers gates from the
   folder; a gate file that the suite cannot see is itself a red line, with the
   file named.
4. **Every lane sweeps its own history once.** What PEOPLE did this round, every
   lane does: list every gate you ever cited as proof and show the suite ran it.

## ROUTING
- PLUMBER [unregistered gates]: the sweep across all eighteen lanes, then rules 2
  and 3 built into the suite.
- Every lane: the self-sweep, as one line in its own handoff, next round.

# LAW BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_TOP_MENU_BAR_9_7_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THE_TOP_MENU_BAR_9_7_26.md
====================================================================================================
# THE TOP MENU BAR (Paolo 9/7/26, LOCKED)

## HIS WORDS
> "I'm thinking we need a top menu bar like how Battle Brothers has it, how Civilization
> five has it, Surviving the Aftermath has a... Surviving Mars has a, you know, shit like
> that, bro. Top menu."

## THE RULING
The walked game gets **ONE BAR THAT OWNS THE TOP OF THE SCREEN.** Not chips floating over
the world; a strip, pinned to the top edge, that the game's status lives in and the menu
hangs off. Everything that is currently a loose button in the top-left goes into it.

## AND THIS ADMITS THREE REFERENCE GAMES THIS REPO HAS NEVER HAD
NEVER ADD A REFERENCE GAME HE HAS NOT NAMED. He named these, so they are in, and the
companion law applies: **A REFERENCE BELONGS TO ONE DEPARTMENT.**

| game | department | what may be cited |
|---|---|---|
| CIVILIZATION V | INTERFACE | the top bar only: one strip, status left, turn/date right, menu far right |
| SURVIVING THE AFTERMATH | INTERFACE | the top bar only |
| SURVIVING MARS | INTERFACE | the top bar only, and its clock/speed block at the right end |
| BATTLE BROTHERS | campaign layer (8/28) **and now its top bar, by his own citation** | the bar: money, the day counter, and the party buttons hanging off the right |

Citing any of them for anything else -- their combat, their building, their economy, their
art -- is the same violation as citing a game he never named.

## *** THE CONTRADICTION THIS CREATES, AND HOW IT IS RESOLVED ***
The repo already carries an ANTI-reference to two of these, from him, LOCKED:

> laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_THREE_CURRENCIES_CENTURY_7_26_26.md (Paolo 7/26): "games like
> that are called spreadsheet simulators and I'm not a fan". Civ-5 / Surviving-the-
> Aftermath multi-currency feel is BANNED.

NEWEST DATE WINS, and 9/7 is newer than 7/26 -- but newest-wins settles a conflict, it
does not delete the older ruling wholesale, and these two are not actually in conflict
once you read what each one is about:

- **7/26 banned the multi-CURRENCY feel**: a wall of counters, a fourth and fifth
  currency, an economy you read instead of live. THAT STANDS. There are still EXACTLY
  THREE currencies and one ledger.
- **9/7 orders the BAR**: one strip that owns the top and holds the menu. That is a
  layout, not an economy.

**SO THE BAR IS ORDERED AND THE SPREADSHEET IS STILL BANNED**, and the line between them
is a number: the top bar may never show more than the three locked currencies. A fourth
number in that strip is the spreadsheet he rejected, arriving by the back door.

## WHAT THE BAR CARRIES, AND THE RULE THAT DECIDES IT
**Only what the game actually knows.** MECHANISM-MINE / CONTENTS-PAOLO'S: a readout with
an invented number in it is worse than an empty bar, because he cannot tell the two apart
by looking.

Today the walked city truthfully knows three things and they are what ships in the bar:
WHERE YOU ARE (district, on foot or riding, inside), THE DAY AND THE CLOCK, and the menu.

The three currencies are NOT in the bar yet and that is not an oversight: there is no live
player purse on the walked surface. `PURSE` exists as a module with three currencies and a
ledger, and nothing on the street holds one. ECONOMY's own round 27 says the loop does not
close. **The bar reads its money through one function, so the moment a purse is wired the
numbers appear with no further design.** Until then it shows no money rather than a zero
that means nothing.

## WHAT THIS PAIRS WITH
- **[no tabs]** (9/6, LOCKED): CITY and MAP stop being buttons. A bar is where the
  survivors of that cull live.
- **[half size]** (9/6, LOCKED): the bar is drawn at the same half scale as everything
  else on the run.
- **[skin swap]**: the bar is the biggest single piece of interface in the game, so it is
  the first thing that must come off a named skin when three acts land.

## THE GATE
`gates/top_bar_gate.js`. A law without a machine gate is not enforced.

# LAW BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_ANIMAL_IS_AN_ERA_NOT_AN_ANIMAL_9_7_26.md
# source: laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_ANIMAL_IS_AN_ERA_NOT_AN_ANIMAL_9_7_26.md
====================================================================================================
# BOHEMIA ADDENDUM -- ANIMAL IS AN ERA, NOT AN ANIMAL (Paolo 9/7/26, LOCKED)
# Asked whether the game opens as the coyote: "No real animals bro. Animalistic era of
# act 1. The vibes, not actual animals."

## 1. THE RULING
Generation one is called the Animal because ACT ONE IS THE ANIMAL ERA: the anarchy
decade, surviving the ruin, instinct before law. Nobody plays a coyote. Nobody plays
a four-legged anything. The player is a person in a time when people lived like
animals. The same reading holds for the other two: HUMAN is the era when the world
claws back and rules return; ANGEL is the era above it, the cyberpunk healing and
the one-way trip. Eras, not creatures.

## 2. IT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN AND WE READ IT WRONG
The story master (laws/BOHEMIA_STORY_MASTER_7_18_26.md, THE THREE ACTS, 7/19) says
it in one line: "Generations Animal / Human / Angel; camera levels street / city /
planetary zoom", and then describes act one as THE ANARCHY DECADE, surviving the
ruin. The coordinator read "Gen 1 Animal" in the pillars as a literal animal, put
"the game opens as the coyote" on the board as his own call (9/5), and DYNASTY spent
two research rounds on playing as an animal and on a coyote in Las Vegas, and
CHARACTER got a job to prove a four-legged rig. All of that rests on a misreading of
a sentence that was on the shelf the whole time. Root cause: nobody re-read the
story master before building on its vocabulary. He said this round that the rough
draft of all the acts exists and he has not thought about it in some time; it does
exist, and it is the file above plus its act addenda.

## 3. WHAT THE ANIMAL ERA IS, IN TERMS A LANE CAN BUILD
- The verbs of act one are survival verbs: take, hide, run, fight, eat, keep your
  people alive. No courts, no contracts that hold, no prices that mean anything.
- The look of act one is the runway worn to the bone (already ruled), the 2050
  rustic interface (already ruled), and a valley that is running out (already
  built).
- The sound of act one is the beach vibe worn down (already ruled).
- The pillar's word survives as a feeling: instinct first. That is a direction for
  WORDS (how people talk when there is no law), COMBAT (the first era's fights are
  ambushes and scrambles, not duels), and DYNASTY (what a child raised in the
  animal era carries into the human one).

## 4. WHAT DIES AND WHAT IS KEPT
- DEAD: RUN [animal first] (the coyote opening). Graveyarded with this post-mortem.
- KEPT, RE-AIMED: the four-legged renderer DYNASTY found is real code. It is for
  WILDLIFE in the valley (coyotes exist in Las Vegas, as its own research showed),
  never for the player. CHARACTER [animal rig] becomes a wildlife job, low on the
  queue.
- KEPT AS RECORDS: DYNASTY rounds 1 and 2 stay in records as what they are; their
  coyote findings route to wildlife, and their "no hands" finding is void for the
  player.

## ROUTING
- CLAUDE.md pillars line: "(eras, not creatures)".
- VAMILY: the kills above; DYNASTY [animal era] and WORDS [no law talk] added.
