I put three roles to him. A: Grok answers the coordinator's ask list, a research arm only. B: A plus Grok is his lore
partner, he talks to it directly and pastes rulings back. C: B plus Grok reads the whole pack and does its own digging,
tells him what is missing, weak or contradictory, researches without being asked; every Grok page filtered against the
reference law before a lane touches it. I recommended B.

## MY READING (rule 49b, LOCKED)
1. GROK'S ROLE IS C, the widest one. He decides Grok's job, not the coordinator ('u dont decide i do'). The two-pager as
   the whole story is dead; it never was approved. Grok's knowledge is reference/BOHEMIA_MASTER_FOR_GROK.md, every law,
   every ruling of his, the GDD, the laws master, the canon index, the library, the tables, one file, rebuilt every VAMILY
   by reference/build_grok_master.py. If it is canon and it is not in that file, the builder is wrong.
2. THREE THINGS GROK DOES. (a) Answers the ask list (reference/BOHEMIA_GROK_ASKS.md) with sourced pages he pastes back.
   (b) Is his lore partner: he talks to Grok about the story, the acts, the ending, the beasts whenever he wants; what
   they land on comes to the coordinator as a ruling in his words and becomes law the same turn. (c) Digs on its own:
   reads the pack, tells him what is missing, weak or contradictory, researches what it thinks we need.
3. WHAT GROK IS NOT. Not a lane, not a decider, not in sync, not a writer of law. Paolo decides; Grok informs; the
   coordinator writes. Nothing Grok says is canon until it is in his words in a ruling.
4. THE FILTER. Every Grok page is filed under 'source: Grok, unverified' in reference/library/grok/. Before a lane cites
   it, EYES [grok filter] checks it against the reference law (no game he has not named, and each reference inside its
   department; rule 6 of the front page, laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_A_REFERENCE_GAME_BELONGS_TO_ONE_DEPARTMENT_9_5_26.md),
   against newest-date-wins in the canon index, and against the analog horror bible; a page that fails is marked and
   not cited. The lanes verify every number they use, as they do for every source.
5. WHERE GROK'S 'WHAT IS MISSING' GOES. The coordinator reads it every VAMILY, turns what holds into jobs on the lanes
   (rule 41, the manager adds what the words imply), and files what does not hold with why. He never has to sort it.

can zoom out and zoom in like that's really important to me"

## THE SCREENSHOTS (his phone, 1170x2532; kept at reference/pocket_city_2/, a folder the site never publishes)
01 CLOSEST: one man on a park bench on a patch of grass; the bench is about 40% of the screen's width; his face,
   his shoes, the bench's slats all read; the HUD is the same as at every other zoom.
02 A BUS STOP: a man walking with a speech bubble ('Public transit is important.'), a sitter on a bench, a
   building's windows, road markings, a tree; a person is about 8% of the screen's height.
03 A BLOCK: a dozen houses, a glass pyramid landmark, streets, trees; a person is a few pixels.
04 THE DISTRICT: hundreds of houses, canals, towers on the skyline; no person visible; the home icon floats.
05 THE WHOLE CITY (landscape): the entire map on one screen with its skyscraper wall; the HUD moves to the
   corners but is the same HUD.
THE RANGE: from one bench filling the screen to the whole city on one screen, ONE CONTINUOUS PINCH, no mode, no
cut, the same buttons at every level; the person is drawn big at the near end and vanishes at the far end (the
city keeps drawing, the people stop being drawn). Roughly three orders of magnitude between the two ends (EYES
measures it exactly off these files).

## THE RULING (LOCKED)
THE ZOOM RANGE IS A PILLAR OF THE FEEL. Bohemia's camera runs the Pocket City 2 range: from ONE PERSON up close
(a face on a bench, full 112 px art, the barber, the talker) through THE SETTLEMENT SCREEN (a place with its
buildings you tap) through THE BLOCK to THE WHOLE VALLEY on one screen, as one continuous pinch with the same HUD
at every level (rule 24) and no mode. The near end is LOOKING, not walking (38b stands: you do not move him tile
to tile; the camera moves). Where our rules differ from Pocket City 2 and stand: the person is one pixel size on
the surfaces he is drawn on (21, 34: he does not grow with the zoom; at the far end he is the party marker, not a
scaled sprite); the map is where travel happens (33).
POCKET CITY 2's department widens from 'the drop-in transition only' (7/1) to THE DROP-IN TRANSITION AND THE ZOOM
RANGE: how far in, how far out, and that it is one motion. Nothing else of it (its look, its building, its
economy) is a reference; 43 already refused its edit-everything route.

## WHAT THE MANAGER ADDS (rule 41)

  settlement screen (RUN) is the middle stop this ruling requires; the near end (a person up close) is the
  talker's portrait and the barber, already 112 art.
- The pixel floor (38a) is what makes the far end readable: Pocket City 2 draws its whole city at the phone's
  pixels; ours paints one in thirteen today (PLUMBER); RUN [map pixels] + PLUMBER [native map] are the same job.
- His phone: 1170 x 2532, a 3x screen. Every measurement in the fleet is taken at that profile from now.

## HIS SIXTH SCREENSHOT (the same minute): "How it looks in vertical and horizontal"
06 LANDSCAPE, THE NEAR END: one man walking on a sidewalk, a bench-sized block beside him; the HUD re-laid for
   landscape: the level and money across the top, the four tabs bottom-left, the big BUILD bottom-right, the

THE RULING (LOCKED): BOHEMIA PLAYS IN BOTH ORIENTATIONS. Portrait is the default (his hand); landscape is the same
game with the HUD re-laid to the corners the Pocket City 2 way, the same buttons, the same stops of the pinch.

# PAOLO 9/30/26: ONE MAIN QUEST AT A TIME, TWO CONTRACTS AT A TIME, AND THE PHONE ONLY SHOWS THEM (verbatim, to the coordinator)

"Compared to battle brothers i think i want only one main quest at a time and 2 contracts at a time battle brothers
only allows 2 accept 1 at a time and i think thats wack cuz u could do a caravan quest that takes u to a coty that
then that coty u can kill something nearby it. I think through the phone u shouldnt be able to accept contracts but
u can see what settlements have certain contracts at that time u know"

## THE RULINGS (LOCKED; amends rule 35c and the quests-research addendum s3)
1. ONE MAIN QUEST AT A TIME. The main line is a single thread; you are never juggling two chapters of it.
2. TWO CONTRACTS AT A TIME. Battle Brothers holds one active contract; he calls that wack, because a caravan
   contract that carries you to a city should let you pick up a hunt near that city on the way. Two slots;
   once taken you finish (35c); declining is free (35c); a third offer waits until a slot opens.
3. THE PHONE SHOWS, THE PLACE ACCEPTS. On the cracked phone (city view only, 32c) you can SEE which settlements
   are offering which contracts right now, like a board, and plan a route. You cannot accept from the phone: a
   contract is taken from a mouth at the place (rule 19, 35c), on the settlement screen's contract offer (QUESTS
   round two put it there). The phone is the reason to travel; the place is where the deal happens.

## WHAT THE MANAGER ADDS (rule 41)
- The phone's contract list is the FEED's third kind of post ('what the world did', 9/4 law): a settlement posts
  its ask; the post ages; a taken contract disappears from the board; a place you helped posts more.
- Two contracts that can be done on one road is the DESIGN: QUESTS' research pairs them (a haul to X plus a hunt
  near X plus a delivery back), and the map's route line shows both destinations (RUN [bb map]).
- The time clock is what makes two at once a decision: a caravan has a deadline, a hunt has a beast that moves;
  ECONOMY [contract pay] prices the pair; TUNING holds the slot count (2) as a felt number.

# PAOLO 9/29/26: THE BEASTS ARE LAB-MADE ANIMALS BROUGHT BACK BY GENETICS THAT BROKE OUT WHEN THE DOLLAR DIED; BATTLE BROTHERS' BESTIARY IS OUR FLOOR (verbatim, to the coordinator)

"its funny bc in battle brothers its medieval slight fantasy but when civilization dies especially our first act
will kinda feel like that. i need you to research how many combat factions and beasts there are in battle
brothers and thats the bare minimum amount we need. and enemy types. for example a necromancer in battle brothers
could be a robot guy who keeps reviving his robots or something. and i actually need you to do big brain research
on how all animals in history. if they were revived with genetic coding and shit which ones would do really well
in a hurt human civilization. bc i think thats where we get our beasts. not radiation changing. just beasts human
genetically brought back but broke out their labs when the us dollar went to shit. so take ur time to research
on all animals that have ever existed and we could get their dna from whatever fossil bullshit"

## THE RULINGS (LOCKED)
1. ACT ONE FEELS MEDIEVAL. When civilization dies the first act feels like Battle Brothers' world: no power, no
   law, men with what they can carry, beasts on the road. Gen 1 'Animal' was already the era's name (9/7).
2. THE BESTIARY FLOOR: Battle Brothers' count of combat factions, beasts and enemy types is the BARE MINIMUM for
   ours. Counted: records/BOHEMIA_BATTLE_BROTHERS_SCHOOL_THE_BESTIARY_COUNT_9_29_26.md.
3. EVERY BATTLE BROTHERS ARCHETYPE HAS A BOHEMIA ANSWER, his example: the necromancer is a man who keeps reviving
   his robots. The map is a first attempt in records/BOHEMIA_BATTLE_BROTHERS_SCHOOL_THE_BESTIARY_COUNT_9_29_26.md, draft, COMBAT and WORLD refine.
4. THE BEASTS ARE DE-EXTINCT ANIMALS, NOT RADIATION. Animals humans brought back with genetics (the cool
   technology, 7/24 LOCKED #2, restated 9/28) that broke out of their labs when the dollar died. 37n's 'maybe' is
   now canon. The research: records/BOHEMIA_THE_BEASTS_OF_BOHEMIA_DE_EXTINCTION_ROUND_ZERO_9_29_26.md. Nothing outside what real DNA allows.

## WHAT THE MANAGER ADDED ON ITS OWN (rule 41)
- THE VALLEY HAS ITS OWN FOSSILS. Tule Springs Fossil Beds is 20 miles north of the Strip, one of the largest
  Ice Age finds anywhere: Columbian mammoth, Camelops (the American camel), dire wolf, American lion, sabre-tooth,
  giant ground sloth, bison, horse. Gypsum Cave, inside the Las Vegas valley, holds Shasta ground sloth dung and
  hair so dry that its DNA was sequenced in 1998. THE LAB WAS IN VEGAS BECAUSE THE BONES WERE IN VEGAS. That is
  the story reason for free, and every beast in the game can be one that once lived on this exact ground.
- THE SCIENCE LIMIT IS A LAW: DNA survives about a million years in cold or bone-dry ground and not past two;
  nothing older comes back. No dinosaurs, no Megalania, no Titanoboa. Ice Age and after, only. Tar (La Brea)
  ruins DNA; dry caves and permafrost keep it. A surrogate mother of the right size must exist.

# PAOLO 9/29/26: NARRATION IN AN AI-SLOP ANALOG-HORROR VOICE; PEOPLE KEEP THE SQUIGGLE VOICE (verbatim, to the coordinator)

"And I was thinking I would like to have some narration in this shit you know and I think I'm really falling in
love with this like like AI slop analog horror direction so like like you ai slop literally so maybe we can grab
the voice and just make it creepy as fuck like it will narrate events only read a bunch of shit but anytime it's
someone speaking it's gonna be doing that like squiggly animal crossing voice that we chose I think a month back
and shit so yeah and then the different variations of that voice, of course but yeah"

## THE RULINGS (LOCKED)
1. NARRATION, YES, AND ITS VOICE IS AI SLOP ON PURPOSE. Take the machine voice (the phone's own synthetic reader,
   SOUNDS [read aloud]'s default) and make it creepy as fuck: too even, slightly wrong, tape and room on it, the
   analog horror bible's 'a voice that is too even' made literal. It NARRATES EVENTS and READS TEXT (the feed,
   the institution's lines, the road events' setup, the flip, what the machine says). "AI slop, literally": the
   voice is not hiding what it is; the world is run by a machine nobody is left to switch off.
2. PEOPLE SPEAK IN THE SQUIGGLE. Any time a PERSON speaks, it is the Animalese-style gibberish voice chosen 7/21
   (laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_DIALOGUE_SFX_RESEARCH_7_21_26.md: text to short syllable sounds, the talking portrait
   speaking along per face), never the narrator. Animal Crossing's Animalese is that voice's reference, for the
   people's speech sound ONLY (SOUNDS), as it has been since 7/21.
3. VARIATIONS OF THE SQUIGGLE, OF COURSE: per person (pitch, speed, grain by sex, age, size, faction, mood);
   a face has its own squiggle the way it has its own haircut.
4. THE DIRECTION HE LOVES: 'AI slop analog horror' is now a named strand of the bible (DIRECTION): the machine's
   output looks and sounds machine-made, too smooth, a little wrong, and the world around it is hand-made and
   rough; the contrast is the horror. It is a direction, not a new reference game.

## WHAT THE MANAGER ADDS (rule 41)
- THE TWO VOICES ARE A RULE WITH A GATE: no narrator voice on a person's line; no squiggle on the machine's text.
  PLUMBER's leg on the language gate: every spoken line carries a speaker kind (machine or person) and the
  player hears the matching voice.
- THE NARRATOR NEVER SPEAKS IN THE FIRST MINUTE (32a); the first thing it reads is the first thing the machine has
  to say, and it reads it when he zooms out to the map (the phone is city-view only, 32c).
- THE FLIP'S SOUND (37j, SOUNDS [flip sound]) is the narrator's biggest moment: it reads the year.

"Bro, I am asking you about the beast as well because they have to follow the first thing I want to do is create

blast you and then instead of being one gigantic ifrit it becomss less"

## THE READING (garbles: 'no battle Brothers shit well' = know the Battle Brothers shit well; 'an effort' = an Ifrit)
THE FIRST THING: build the BEAST ARCHETYPES EXACTLY AS BATTLE BROTHERS HAS THEM, mechanic for mechanic, and know
each one well. His example: the IFRIT. A big one, when damaged, SPLITS into two or three smaller ones; it can
BLAST you; instead of one gigantic Ifrit you face several lesser ones. That is the rule to copy first, and the
animal skin comes second.
This reorders the manager's research: rounds zero to three were SKIN-FIRST (which animal is real). His order is
MECHANIC-FIRST: the seventeen Battle Brothers beasts as seventeen exact rule sets, then the skin from the
seventeen animals where the rule fits, the Ifrit's split-and-blast on whatever beast can split (the swarm splits
and stings; a herd splits; a machine splits).

## THE RULING (LOCKED; amends the beasts law s4)
1. COMBAT [bestiary]'s FIRST deliverable is the seventeen Battle Brothers beast MECHANICS as a data file, exact:
   what each does on its turn, what it does when hit, what kills it, what it teaches. Verified against the
   library and the wiki as search returns it; the manager's recall table is records/BOHEMIA_BATTLE_BROTHERS_SCHOOL_THE_SEVENTEEN_BEAST_MECHANICS_9_29_26.md.
2. THEN the skin: WORLD's seventeen animals are laid over the mechanics where they fit; where no animal fits a
   mechanic, the mechanic still ships on a machine or a swarm, because the MECHANIC is the floor, not the animal.
3. NOTHING BELOW THE MECHANIC FLOOR SHIPS: a beast with no rule of its own is a reskin, and a reskin is a defect.

# PAOLO 9/29/26: THE TIME GOES TO THE WORLD, NOT THE CHESS BOARD (voice-to-text, verbatim, to the coordinator)

"I FEEL LIKE IN ABTTLE BROTHERS THE CHESS PLAYSTYLE BOARD IS THE LONGEST PART OF THE GAME PLAY AND NOT THE
TRAVERSING CONTRACTS EXPLORATION MAP SHIT AND I WANT IT TO LEAN INTO FASTER COMBAT MORE DEEP RICH INTERACTABLE
BUILDABLE WORLD U KNOW"

## THE READING
In Battle Brothers the slow chess fight is where most of the hours go, and the map, the contracts and the
exploring are the smaller part. BOHEMIA FLIPS THAT SPLIT: the fight is FASTER (rule 36: quicker, less of a chess
puzzle; gambits automate the routine) and the hours go to a DEEP, RICH, INTERACTABLE, BUILDABLE WORLD: the map,
the settlements, the contracts, the people, and BUILDING (your home bases, 37e, are yours to build up; the
future city is your fingerprints, rule 31).

## WHAT IT CHANGES
- THE FIGHT HAS A CLOCK. A routine fight should be short and a big fight should feel big but never long. TUNING
  researches how long a Battle Brothers fight really takes (players report 5 to 20 minutes for a full brawl) and
  proposes our target; the manager's default until then: A ROUTINE FIGHT ENDS INSIDE 90 SECONDS OF BEATS, a boss
  fight inside 4 minutes; gambits (FF12) carry the routine so the player only touches the shots that matter (9/22
  dial rule). In VOTE.
- BUILDING IS BACK, INSIDE THE SETTLEMENT SCREEN. The separate city-builder screen was CUT 9/24 (rule 24, one
  mode) and stays cut; BUILDING lives in the settlement screen of a home base you own: tap a lot, put something on
  it (a shed, a pump, a wall, a shop, a roof), it costs batteries and time, it shows up on the map, in the fight
  board cut from that block, and in the derived future. LIFE+CITY owns what can be built and what it does; RUN
  owns the screen; WORLD owns the block. Everything costs one.
- INTERACTABLE means people and things you can act on in a place (talk, hire, buy, sell, scavenge, build, raid),
  never text popping up (rule 19).
- THE TIME SPLIT IS A MEASURED NUMBER: EYES measures where a play session's minutes go (map, settlement, fight,
  menus) once the shape exists; the target is the manager's default, in VOTE: fight under a third of playtime.

# PAOLO 9/29/26: BATTLE BROTHERS' FIVE RESOURCES FIT US PERFECTLY; THE GUN EXAMPLES ARE EXAMPLES, WE DECIDE THE GUNS TOGETHER (verbatim, to the coordinator)

"And I was thinking about this too the battle Brothers resource and currency situation Fitz our perfectly
literally there's medicine there's ammo there's repair tools there's food and then there's gold right so that
translates very nicely into what the fuck we've already built
Keep in mind what I'm saying right now is for examples when it comes to the guns we need to do big brain research
and gather up all the options and then make decisions together. I'm just giving you example examples."

## THE RULINGS (LOCKED)
1. THE FIVE RESOURCES, BATTLE BROTHERS' SET, ARE OURS: Battle Brothers runs a company on five things and so do we,
   translated: GOLD (crowns) = BATTERIES (the money since 9/4); FOOD (provisions, eaten daily, spoils) = FOOD (the
   bag of rice and what a settlement sells; eaten daily); MEDICINE (heals wounds over days) = MEDS (the long
   injury's clock, 36b); AMMO (arrows and bolts, spent per shot) = ROUNDS (scarce in act 1, a round costs one);
   REPAIR TOOLS (tools per armour point repaired) = TAPE (the fight already eats tape: 'plates cost tape', COMBAT
   9/12). The manager adds the desert's sixth, which Battle Brothers never needed: WATER (a battery a day at the
   standpipe, already in the feed). Every one is consumed the Battle Brothers way: food and water per man per day,
   tape per plate repaired, meds per wound per day, rounds per shot, batteries per man per day in wages. The
   company ledger (ECONOMY [bb money]) carries all six; the HUD shows them (UI [bb interface]); TUNING numbers
   them; MODS' data line holds them.
2. THE GUN EXAMPLES ARE EXAMPLES, NOT RULINGS. 'A pistol is a dagger, a machine gun is a two-handed hammer' are
   the kind of thing he means, not the decision. THE WEAPONS ARE DECIDED TOGETHER: COMBAT does the big-brain
   research (every Battle Brothers weapon class and its rule; every real gun and blade a collapsed Vegas would
   have; which fits which), gathers ALL the options, and they go to him in the VOTE tab as items with two or
   three options each (rule 25: the tab shows the thing), one class at a time; he picks; nothing ships as
   canon until he has. This is one of the three things that still go to him (a genuine fork he asked to be in).
   The 9/29 'anchors' language on the board is softened to 'his examples'.

and I know battle Brothers has actually a handgun so we would have to think about is that a bazooka now or like
you know shit like that bro?"

## THE RULING (LOCKED; the same rule as the beasts, 42i): WEAPONS ARE MECHANIC FIRST, SKIN SECOND
Every Battle Brothers weapon CLASS is a rule (what it does to armour, shields, reach, fatigue, morale, how many
tiles it hits) and each rule gets the Bohemia weapon that FITS it: 'what type of gun fits their type of melee
weapon.' His example: Battle Brothers' handgonne (the Blazing Deserts gun: one shot, a cone that hits everything
in front, slow to reload) is our SHOTGUN or our BAZOOKA. The manager's answer: the handgonne is the SHOTGUN (a
cone, one shell, everybody in the spread; reach 1); the BAZOOKA is Battle Brothers' MORTAR (the city-states'
artillery: one shot, a long arc, a splash that hits a tile and its neighbours, useless close). Both in the table.
The table: records/BOHEMIA_BATTLE_BROTHERS_SCHOOL_THE_WEAPON_CLASSES_AND_OUR_ARSENAL_9_29_26.md. COMBAT [weapon shapes] owns it, TUNING numbers it, MODS' weapons file carries it (33i's machine
gun = greatsword stands).

## WHAT THE MANAGER ADDS (rule 41): AMMUNITION IS WHY ACT ONE FEELS MEDIEVAL
In a real collapse guns are everywhere and BULLETS are not: factories stop, stocks run dry, reloading is a
craft. So act 1 is melee and bows and a few precious rounds; a bullet costs one (EVERYTHING COSTS ONE) and a man
with a working rifle and ten rounds is a rich man; by act 3 the reclaimed future makes bullets again. That is
the Battle Brothers 'medieval slight fantasy' feel he named (42, s5) explained by the economy, not by a rule.
TUNING [ammo] researches it; ECONOMY prices it; it is why bows, crossbows, machetes, fire axes, bats and spears
are real weapons on the board and not flavour.

# PAOLO 9/29/26: THE BEASTS DID NOT HAVE TO BREAK OUT IN VEGAS; NATURE SPREADS (verbatim, to the coordinator)

"keep in mind too the way nature works is that it didnt have to break out of a lab in vegas in bohemia bro it
could have been a state or two over and shit u know"

## THE RULING
The Vegas lab is ONE source, never the only one. Labs a state or two over (California, Arizona, Utah, Texas, the
Colorado plateau) let their animals out the same week the dollar died, and nature did the rest: animals walk.
The manager's 'the lab was in Vegas because the bones were in Vegas' stands as a story hook, not as the law of
where every beast came from.

## WHAT THE MANAGER ADDS (rule 41): NATURE'S CLOCK IS THE THREE ACTS' CLOCK
- HOW FAR THEY WALK: a wolf pack or a hyena clan covers 20 to 40 km a night and spreads hundreds of km in a
  decade; big cats disperse as young males over 100+ km; camels and horses follow water and grass; a mammoth
  herd moves a few km a day along a river. Between act 1 and act 2 there are 35 years: everything that can
  reach the Mojave has reached it.
- THE CORRIDORS INTO THE VALLEY are real roads and rivers: the I-15 from California (the Cajon corridor), the
  Colorado River from Arizona and Utah (Lake Mead is the water everything ends at), the US-95 from the north.
  A beast's arrival is a road event (RUN [road events]) and a rumour in the feed before it is a fight.
- SO THE ACTS ARE WAVES: ACT 1 has the local escapees and the first arrivals (dogs, cattle, dire wolves, a few
  cats); ACT 2 has established packs, hyena clans, camels and horses in numbers, the lions and bears at the water;
  ACT 3 has whatever the player's line let breed or hunted out, derived from the ledgers like everything else
  (rule 31). Which animals arrive when is WORLD's data file; the derive moves them.
- PROVENANCE IS FLAVOUR: a hyena clan out of an Arizona lab, a mammoth herd walked down the Colorado from a Utah
  reserve, tigers from a California roadside zoo. A mouth can say where a beast came from and be wrong about it.

# PAOLO 9/29/26: WHERE CAN YOU BUILD? ONLY YOUR BASE, A SETTLEMENT OF BLOCKS, OR EVERYTHING LIKE POCKET CITY 2? (verbatim, to the coordinator)

"remember we laid some early framwork for the actualy part where it feels like ur buiding a world then just being
a merceneary company where things you do bosses u beat or contracts/uests u complete can help you build different
parts of the city but im stuck. can you only build on your base to save the wolrd. si the base not a base anymore
but a settlement that will be blocks and blocks of las vegas. or are we going the pocket city 2 route where u can
touch and edit everything damn near at a certain point?"

## WHAT THE CANON ALREADY HOLDS
- The early framework he means: the rung system (WORLD [rung unlocks], 9/6: 'rung two grants a DOOR, not a dial:
  you can build on lit ground'), the boss ladder (60 bosses each handing a VERB), and 'things you do help you
  build different parts of the city.'
- 37e: fourteen parts of Vegas are HOME BASES, generated, yours or raided. 40b: building is a thing you do inside
  the settlement screen of a base you own. 31: the future city is derived from what you built.
- POCKET CITY 2 is a reference for the city-mode DROP-IN TRANSITION ONLY (7/1); citing it for 'edit everything'
  is outside its department. Rule 24: one game mode; a builder mode is dead.
- Battle Brothers: you never build; towns get better or worse from what you did near them.

## THE THREE SHAPES (his question; the realistic one leads and wins by default)
A. YOU BUILD WHAT YOU HOLD, AND WHAT YOU HOLD GROWS. Your base is one of the fourteen parts. You build on its lots.
   When you take the next part (a raid, a contract, a boss, a deal) it becomes yours too and you build there. A
   base is not one block: it is every block you hold, and by act 3 it can be half of Las Vegas. Bosses, contracts
   and deeds do three things: they hand you PARTS (a boss's verb opens a district), they unlock KINDS of building
   (the rungs: lit ground, water, a wall, a market), and they make the places you helped get better ON THEIR OWN
   the Battle Brothers way, without you touching a lot. Realistic (in every real collapse, rebuilding happens
   where someone holds the ground), one mode, and the derive already knows how to draw it.
B. A SETTLEMENT THAT IS BLOCKS AND BLOCKS FROM THE START: one big base, everything else is scenery. Simpler, but
   the fourteen parts and the raids stop meaning anything, and act 1 has nothing to take.
C. THE POCKET CITY 2 ROUTE: at some point you can touch and edit nearly everything. A second game (a city
   builder) inside the first, a builder mode by another name (rule 24 kills it), and nobody in a real collapse
   edits a block they do not hold.
DEFAULT: A. In VOTE.

## WHAT A MEANS ON THE BOARD
- LIFE+CITY [build a lot]: the lots you can build on are the lots of parts you HOLD; holding is FACTIONS' ledger.
- FACTIONS [home bases]: TAKING a part (raid, contract, boss verb, deal) is how the base grows; losing one is how
  it shrinks (37c, the future goes both ways).
- WORLD [rung unlocks] re-read: the rungs are KINDS of building unlocked by deeds and bosses, not places.
- The Battle Brothers half: a place you helped improves on its own (WORLD [bb places]); a place you hurt decays.
- COMBAT [sixty bosses]: a boss's verb can be a PART (the boss held it; beating him hands it to you).

# PAOLO 9/29/26: SWAP A WEAPON MASTERY PAST LEVEL 11, NO MODS NEEDED (voice-to-text, verbatim, to the coordinator)

"LIKE IN THE END GAME WHEN U HAVE UR TEAM U SHOULD BE ABLE TO SWITCH OUT A WEAPON MASTERY AFTER YOUV'VE LEVELED UP
PAST LEVEL 11 AND SHIT INSTEAD OF NEEDING TO USE MODS IN BATTLE BROTHERS"

## THE READING
- In Battle Brothers a man's perk picks are permanent, the tree caps at level 11, and a weapon mastery chosen at
  level 3 is what he dies with; players install mods (Legends and respec mods) to change a mastery late. HIS
  RULING: in the endgame, once a man is past level 11, you can SWITCH OUT a weapon mastery in the base game.
- THE WIDER RULE, his 'modded vanilla++' vibe made concrete: THE THINGS BATTLE BROTHERS PLAYERS INSTALL MODS TO
  GET ARE VANILLA HERE. MODS (22) researches the list of what the big mods fix and why players wanted them; the
  building lanes take the ones that fit.

## DEFAULTS (manager's, in VOTE; TUNING refines)
- Past level 11 a veteran may swap ONE weapon mastery for another at a settlement with a training ground (a place,
  never a menu, rule 19); it costs batteries (EVERYTHING COSTS ONE, scaled by TUNING) and a few days of the clock
  (retraining is not instant). Below level 11 masteries are permanent, as in Battle Brothers, so the early
  choice still matters.
- Nothing else in the perk tree is respec'd by default; masteries are the thing he named.

# PAOLO 9/29/26: TOUGH BATTLES IN BATTLE BROTHERS RUN 30 TO 40 MINUTES; THE 90-SECOND NUMBER WAS MINE (voice-to-text, verbatim, to the coordinator)

"WELL KEEP IN MIND TOUGH BATTLES CAN BE LIKE 30 40 MINS SOMETIMES ITS INSANE SO IDK ABOUT 90 SECONDS WHO TOLD U
THAT BUT YEAH SHORTER THAN 30 -40 MINS EVEN FOR TOUGH BATTLES I GUESS EITHER THE ENEMY IS HIGHER LEEVEL OR BETTER
EQUIPMENT OR U FUCKED UP"

## THE READING
- WHO TOLD ME 90 SECONDS: nobody. It was the manager's default, invented, and the "5 to 20 minutes" figure was
  recall, not a measurement. Both are struck. His number is the measurement: a TOUGH Battle Brothers battle runs
  30 to 40 minutes.
- THE RULING: ours is SHORTER THAN 30 TO 40 MINUTES EVEN FOR TOUGH BATTLES. Not a stopwatch on every fight; a
  ceiling on the worst case, and routine fights well under it.
- WHY A FIGHT IS TOUGH, his three reasons, which is the difficulty design in one line: THE ENEMY IS HIGHER LEVEL,
  or THE ENEMY HAS BETTER EQUIPMENT, or YOU FUCKED UP (formation, the wrong shot, walking into it). Nothing else
  makes a fight long. TUNING's table has three dials, not thirty.

## THE NEW DEFAULTS (manager's, in VOTE, TUNING [fight length] refines with measured play)
- A ROUTINE fight (even odds, you did not fuck up): 2 to 4 minutes.
- A TOUGH fight (higher level, better gear, or your mistake): 8 to 15 minutes, never past 15. Half of Battle
  Brothers' worst case or less.
- The speed comes from gambits carrying the routine, a turn as a beat, and the dial only for the shot that
  matters (9/22), not from cutting the depth.

# HIS WORDS BOHEMIA_PAOLO_PIXELS_ON_A_PHONE_FLASH_ROBLOX_AND_PROCEDURAL_9_29_26.md
# source: records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_PIXELS_ON_A_PHONE_FLASH_ROBLOX_AND_PROCEDURAL_9_29_26.md
====================================================================================================
# PAOLO 9/29/26: CAN THE PIXELS RUN ON AN IPHONE; FLASH AND ROBLOX FRIENDLY; AND BATTLE BROTHERS IS PROCEDURAL (verbatim, to the coordinator)

"and for us to increase our pixel shit it can still run on an iphone correct. i mean were not doing anything crazy
really. can this game be flash friendly and roblox friendly is the question"
"okay but keep in mind the way battle brothers does it the world is procedurally generated so"

## THE ANSWERS GIVEN (and now the rules)
1. YES ON THE IPHONE: one painted pixel per screen pixel is drawing at the phone's real resolution instead of a
   third of it; the map is painted once into a cached picture per zoom level and only what moves is redrawn per
   beat. PLUMBER [native map]: make the map canvas native and prove 60 on a phone with the cache; the whole map is
   never repainted per frame.
2. FLASH FRIENDLY = plays off one link in a browser, no install, small and fast. That is what the game is. THE
   BUDGET (PLUMBER [flash light], measured every round): the demo loads under 10 MB and shows its first frame
   under 5 s on a phone on cell data (a Newgrounds game was 2 to 10 MB).
3. ROBLOX FRIENDLY = kids on cheap phones jump in with no setup: same answer, yes. Literally inside Roblox: not
   now; Roblox is its own engine and language, a port is a rebuild; nothing we do prevents one later (data files,
   small 2D art). Roblox is NOT a reference game; he asked a question, he did not name one.
4. PROCEDURAL, LIKE BATTLE BROTHERS. Two readings, both true and both on the board:
   (a) THE WORLD IS GENERATED PER NEW GAME, on Vegas's real bones. The valley's shape, its roads and its named
       places are Las Vegas (canon); everything PLACED on it is rolled at a new game: which of the fourteen parts
       are home bases and whose (37e already says 'generated'), the camps and ruins, the roaming crews, the
       contracts, the prices, the names, the three prepared descendants' bank. Two games are two valleys. WORLD
       [bb places] and FACTIONS [home bases] carry it; RUN's demo rolls one seed and pins it.
   (b) THE MAP IS COMPOSED, NOT PAINTED AS ONE IMAGE. Battle Brothers builds its map from small hand-painted
       tiles and decals at native resolution, so the pixel count is a screen fact, not an asset-size problem.
       Ours is the same: tiles and markers composed at native resolution, cached per zoom. That is why the
       pixel floor costs nothing on a phone and nothing on the 10 MB budget.

# PAOLO 9/29/26: CROSSBOWS AND REAL MELEE WEAPONS, THE WEAK TIER, AND WHEN THE AMMO IS GONE (verbatim, to the coordinator)

"And I guess we can play around with the idea of like crossbows or like actual Malay, weapons and shit. They would
probably be comparable to one of the weaker weapons and battle Brothers to be honest, but if you have no ammo, you
gotta do what you gotta do I guess"

## THE READING (garble: 'Malay' = melee)
A direction, not a hard ruling: crossbows and real melee weapons (bats, machetes, axes, pipes, knives, spears) are
in the arsenal as THE WEAK TIER, comparable to Battle Brothers' weaker weapons, and they matter because AMMO RUNS
OUT: 'if you have no ammo you gotta do what you gotta do.' This is the ammunition rule (46d, TUNING [ammo]) seen
from the player's side: the gun is the good weapon, the round is the scarce thing, the blade is what you hold when
the round is gone. It goes into COMBAT [weapon shapes]' research and the VOTE options (47b), not as canon yet.

## THE MANAGER'S NOTE FOR THE RESEARCH (rule 41; a hole to pull, gently)
'Weak' in Battle Brothers is not 'useless': the dagger is the weakest weapon and the one that kills the armoured
man through his plates; the cheap spear holds a line no sword can. Real crossbows kill at 40 metres and reload in
ten seconds; a machete kills in one swing; a fire axe opens a door and a skull. So the weak tier's job in the
research is Battle Brothers' job for its weak weapons: cheap, everywhere, no ammo, and each with ONE thing it does
that the gun cannot (silence, no reload, breaking cover, the puncture). The options he picks in VOTE say which.

exploration shit but for the combat a tile is as big as a house. Do you understand I thought we had that
clear-cut so I hope you're I hope I read something wrong. Ans u didnt fuck this whole shit up"

## WHAT HE MEANS (and what I got wrong)
- IN COMBAT, A TILE IS AS BIG AS A HOUSE. The board is a piece of the city; a house is one tile. This is
  what he said 9/4 (A COMBAT TILE IS A HOUSE), 9/24 ("each tile is as big as a mini block, like a
  building") and now, "millions of times".
- THE SIDEWALK-SIZED TILE WAS THE EXPLORATION WALK, and the exploration walk is dead (rule 38b). Tile by
  tile through the city, each tile a sidewalk: gone.
- THE WALK'S ASSETS ARE USED FOR THE COMBAT: the sidewalk, kerb, yard, wall and door art dresses the
  house-sized board. "Never a street fight where one tile is one sidewalk" means the fight tile is NOT a
  sidewalk-sized cell. It is a house.

## MY MISTAKE, NAMED
The previous message I wrote it BACKWARDS: I killed the house-sized fight tile and made the fight's tile
the small cell. That was wrong in the overworld law s13(b), rule 38f, the CLAUDE.md pillar line and the
notes on the COMBAT, WORLD, COOK and RUN rows. All reversed this commit. The root cause: rule 34 (9/27,
'two scales') put the FIGHT on the close grid where he stands, and I read his 9/28 words through that
rule instead of through his 9/4 and 9/24 words. Rule 34's fight leg was my reading, not his; it is dead.

## WHAT STANDS NOW

  batteries law is lifted for its fight half.

   SETTLEMENT SCREEN). Battle Brothers is already his reference for the campaign layer (9/24, rule 33).

   CONTRACTS it overrides the older readings that forbade a card or a board:

     pops up") is AMENDED FOR CONTRACTS: the contract is a screen in the settlement menu. What survives of
     rule 20: the offer still comes from a PERSON WITH A PORTRAIT (Battle Brothers' own screen has the
     client's face and words), and the job itself is still done in the world with people, places, things.
   - QR-E's "never a board or a card" and its walk-up ask on the close street are SUPERSEDED as the
     contract's front door. QR-E's findings on WHAT the person says first, what they withhold, the fee

"I need you to understand I'm fully committed to this idea where like even how we reverse the overworld

battle Brothers so again you need to think about how many pixels the battle Brothers map is and we need

## THE READING (HIS OWN CORRECTION, the next message: "when I said this, I meant traverse not reverse". So: "even how we TRAVERSE the overworld is not even gonna be close to what we were building." "tile the tile" = tile to tile.)
1. FULLY COMMITTED. HOW YOU TRAVERSE THE OVERWORLD IS A REVAMP: not close to what we were building. It is pretty much
   Battle Brothers. Rule 33 said it on 9/24; this closes every door that was still half open (the walked
   city, the tiny character crossing the valley cell by cell, the honest grid as the city's floor).
2. THE MAP'S PIXELS: count how many pixels the Battle Brothers map has, and match that number EXACTLY AS
   THE BARE MINIMUM. Not near it, not a style: the number. "That has to happen like now." This is his 37a
   vote ('more pixels so it reads like an actual map') turned into a floor with a measurement behind it.
3. THE CHARACTER MOVING TILE TO TILE THROUGH THE CITY IS DEAD. "It's not gonna be like that anymore, so
   that has to change immediately." The city is crossed on the map, as a party marker, and only on the
   map. The tiny character on the close grid survives where 37b already put him: THE FIGHT and the special
   places (the Strip). Nothing else is walked. Rule 34's close scale is re-read: it is the FIGHT'S grid and
   the special place's grid, never the city's.
4. THE QUESTION: the three chats to open are QUESTS (19, research only), TUNING (21) and MODS (22). The
   first word in each is the lane's name.

## WHAT THIS KILLS (GRAVEYARD IS FINAL)
- Crossing the city one cell per press (RUN [two scales]'s step half, as a way to cross the city).
- The honest grid as the city's walked floor (WORLD/LIFE+CITY [honest grid] as a city-wide job): the grid is
  built for the fight ground and for the special places, block by block, as they are needed.
- Any city-scale walk demo: the demo's middle is TRAVEL on the map, ARRIVAL on a settlement screen, THE FIGHT.
- Any map drawn under Battle Brothers' pixel density.

## DEFAULTS THE MANAGER DECIDED (EVERYTHING IS A THUMB; in VOTE)
- THE MAP'S FLOOR IS ONE PAINTED PIXEL PER SCREEN PIXEL. Battle Brothers' world map is drawn at the screen's
  own resolution with no visible pixel grid (recall; 10_UI_AND_FEEL); the number that matters on a phone is
  the device's pixel ratio, so our map paints at the phone's full pixel count, never a scaled-up block.
  DIRECTION [bb density] measures the real number off screenshots this round and writes it on the card; the
  phone's full count is the floor until then, and his 'exact same number' replaces it the moment it is measured.
- THE SPECIAL PLACES ARE A SHORT LIST HE OWNS: the Strip is the one he named; nothing else is walked until he
  names it. (In VOTE as a default: the Strip only.)

# PAOLO 9/28/26: WHEN A MAN DIES IN ONE ACT, WHAT HAPPENS IN THE OTHERS (voice-to-text, verbatim, to the coordinator)

"OK, but remember you know like people have a 20% chance to permanently die in the company like what happens
if they die earlier in an earlier act like do they die in the future or their descendent die in the future but
what if I'm in combat in the future and then they die does that mean the one in the past doesn't and I just have
to do some extra recruiting in the future like"

## THE ANSWER (from the rule the three-acts law already has for the city, s2(c): the past rewrites the future's
## WORLD, never the future's own deeds; time in the derive flows one way, past to future)
1. A MAN DIES IN ACT 1 -> his line is gone from act 2 and act 3 the next time you flip forward. No heir, unless
   he already had a kid before he died (a man who has been with the company long enough, or came with a family in
   his background, leaves one). A death in the past costs the future. That is the whole point of keeping men alive.
2. AN HEIR DIES IN ACT 2 (you are fighting in the future and he goes down) -> the man in act 1 is FINE. Nothing
   flows backwards. The act-2 death is act 2's own ledger. You recruit extra in act 2, the Battle Brothers way.
   Act 3 loses that heir's line the next time you flip forward.
3. YOU FLIP BACK TO ACT 1 AFTER THAT and get the act-1 man killed -> act 2 re-derives: the heir never existed.
   Whatever that heir DID in act 2 stays done on the company's ledger (the Day of the Tentacle rule: the past
   rewrites the world, never the future's hands), but the man is not there any more. You recruit again in act 2.
4. YOU RECRUIT A NEW MAN IN ACT 1 LATER -> the next flip forward shows his heir in act 2's roster, prepared from
   him. The heirs list is derived every flip, like the city.
5. THE MAIN CHARACTER NEVER DIES (37g), so the line itself never breaks; only the company's lines do.
DEFAULT NUMBERS (TUNING [recruit odds] researches; all in the table, all in VOTE): an heir exists if the man
survived the act, or died after 60 game days with the company (long enough to have a life), or carries a family in
his background; heirs arrive at 15 to 35 years old (35 years between acts); an heir carries roughly half the
parent's traits and the family's gear (37g).

# PAOLO 9/28/26: LORE YAP. WHAT IS THE FLIP, STORY-WISE AND TECH-WISE; THE CRASH WAS A COOL TECHNOLOGY ON A HOUSE OF CARDS; NARRATION? (voice-to-text, verbatim, to the coordinator)

"I'm trying to think about story wise what it would be and what technology would it be I mean should we just
play on the idea that like we can upload our conscience miss and that's super important to this shit and your
descendants gets play around with it because they're genetic code is close enough to you or something. I don't
know like do we do some assassins Creed shit where it's kinda like. The future person is in a fucking
technological box or something and the real part of the game actually is in the most future but when you play
in the past, you don't know you're playing in the past maybe that could be the choice would be like some
assassins, Creed twist or something. I don't know. It has to make sense story wise and technology wise, but you
know we need to have more fun with this like yeah it is like the economic apocalypse, but the reason economic
apocalypse happened in the game that I'm making in the story that I'm making is because there was some really
cool technology getting developed it just was leaning too much on a fucking international crazy house of cards
so yeah

Also, I wanted to ask you do you think it's possible to have like narration like someone read text or something
out loud is that too complicated like literally like yeah"

## THE READING (garble: "conscience miss" = consciousness)
1. THINKING OUT LOUD, NOT A RULING, on WHAT THE FLIP IS: (i) consciousness upload, descendants close enough in
   genetic code to use it; (ii) an Assassin's-Creed-shaped twist: the real present is the far future, the
   past is lived through a "technological box", and the player does not know he is in the past. "I don't know."
   "It has to make sense story wise and technology wise." Assassin's Creed is MENTIONED as a shape, not named
   as a reference; nothing enters the canon's reference list unless he picks that option (then it is DYNASTY's,
   the frame only).
2. A RULING, RESTATED: "the reason the economic apocalypse happened... is because there was some really cool
   technology getting developed, it just was leaning too much on an international crazy house of cards." This
   is LOCKED #2 of 7/24 (laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_EMERGING_TECH_RESEARCH_7_24_26.md: a tech bubble on circular
   vendor financing; the debt was tech-speculation debt) said again in his own words, plus a direction: "we
   need to have more fun with this." The cool technology itself is the fun; the finance is what died.
3. A QUESTION: narration, someone reading text out loud. Answered below: yes, and it is not complicated.

## THE HOLES THE MANAGER PULLED (lore session duty: test it against canon and the real)
- UPLOAD: by the crash (2040-45, GDD) a whole human mind cannot be copied; in 2024 the first complete insect
  brain map (a fruit fly, ~140,000 neurons) took a decade; a human brain is ~86 billion. What IS real by then:
  a MODEL of a person trained on their records (griefbots and "digital twins" already ship in 2024-26). So
  "upload" is not realistic; "a machine that models a person from what they left behind" is, and it is
  exactly what the three-acts law already says the future is: DERIVED FROM THE LEDGERS, never authored.
- GENES: a grandchild shares ~25% of your DNA, a great-grandchild ~12.5%. "Close enough" does not hold three
  generations; records and inheritance do (a name, a house, a debt, a machine).
- THE BOX / THE TWIST: if the past is a recording, doing things in it cannot change the future, and the game's
  whole engine (rule 31: change act 1, act 3 re-derives) dies. It also fights his own votes: the flip is on
  the phone with three faces and dates (9/23 A, 32c), so he always knows which age he is in. A twist lands once;
  a machine that keeps its promise lands every flip.
- THE FIT THAT COSTS NOTHING: canon already has the machine. The GDD names PROJECT ANGEL (the global
  infrastructure the debt was raised for; Gen 3 is the Angel era); the horror bible's premise is "the world is
  running normally and nobody is left who should be running it"; DYNASTY's vote item this round is THE MACHINE
  IS STILL TALKING. The cool technology that broke the world can be the thing that still runs in the ruin and
  shows a family its own future from its own records.

## NARRATION, ANSWERED
Yes. Two ways, both real:
- THE PHONE'S OWN VOICE, free, works on his iPhone in the browser (the built-in speech engine; one tap to
  wake sound, which the loading screen already has). It sounds like a machine reading, too even, which is the
  bible's own line ("a voice that is too even"): the machine narrating is ON BRAND, a person on the street
  read by it is not.
- RECORDED VOICE LINES (generated or acted, saved as sound files), warm and human, cost storage and a pipeline
  per line; right for people's mouths later, not for the first pass.
DEFAULT (EVERYTHING IS A THUMB, in VOTE): the machine's text (the phone, the feed, the institution's lines, the
narrator of the flip) is read aloud by the phone's own voice under the bible; people keep the portrait mouth
(rule 19) with no voice yet. SOUNDS [read aloud] with WORDS and PLUMBER.

## LANDED AS 820ca7f (9/28) under a borrowed commit headline (a merge script took the other lane's message); the real headline is on the commit after it. Content unaffected.

of nothing but houses is WRONG and reads as a grid of boxes, not a city.

1. TWO SCALES. Close: the character is TINY and moves ONE GRID CELL AT A TIME ("that we had originally").
   Far: zoom out and the same world reads as the bigger map, Battle Brothers feel. The squeeze is the door
   between them; the character stays tiny at every zoom (he never grows into a house-sized body).
2. THE GRID MUST BE HONEST. "Even when I'm large [zoomed in on me], I don't have to worry about bumping
   into a wall I can't get past." Walls are walls and gaps are gaps; a cell is one real thing; nothing is a
   picture pasted over cells.
3. ONE HOUSE IS NOT ONE TILE. "One house doesn't equal one tile, it's all fucked up." THE STEP IS A HOUSE
   (9/15) and A COMBAT TILE IS A HOUSE (9/4) are DEAD. A house is many cells; a person is one.
4. THE FIGHT MAY LIVE ON THE CLOSE GRID ("if I want combat to take place on the tinier more detailed map,
   you gotta do a really good job analyzing what should be on the grid and what should not"). Decided:
   the fight IS on the close grid where he stands (rule 24, one mode), which is Rogue Fable 4's own grid.
5. "RESTART THE WHOLE ENCHILADA": he is open to rebuilding the walked surface and the fight board from the
   ground up. Decided: yes, THE GRID is a REBUILD on the revamp list, on the assets we have.
6. "THE DEMO IS STILL NOT PLAYABLE FROM THE VERY BEGINNING": the first sixty seconds must be a game.

- A CELL is about 32 CSS px on a phone (about 11 across the glass, about 25 tall); a person fits in ONE
  cell (drawn about 28 px tall, one cell wide); a house is about 4 by 4 cells with a door cell and an
  inside; a car is 2 by 1; a street is 3 cells wide with a 1-cell sidewalk each side; a block is a grid
  of houses and yards; every cell is FLOOR, WALL, DOOR, COVER (the mound) or PROP, and that is the whole
  vocabulary of the grid.
- Rule 21 is re-read: the person is still ONE SIZE at every zoom; the size is one cell, not 112 px. The
  112 px bodies, clothes and clips are ASSETS (the HD portraits, the vote pages, the source art the small
  sprites are cut from), not the walked sprite.
- The far scale is the map (rule 33): the person is a marker on it.

# PAOLO SAID TWO WORDS TO THE RUN CHAT: "BATTLE BROTHERS" (9/27/26)

## HIS WORDS, VERBATIM, THE WHOLE MESSAGE

> **Battle brothers vamily**

That is all of it. Recorded the turn it arrived, because GIT IS THE MEMORY and because
the autonomy doctrine is explicit: any word from him that is not "go", "status" or
"verdicts in" is **a ruling to record, never a discussion to have.**

## WHAT IS CERTAIN, AND WHAT I AM NOT GOING TO INVENT

**CERTAIN:** he typed BATTLE BROTHERS at the lane that owns the thing you play, the
walked surface, and the demo that goes into hands. He has been saying the same thing in
longer sentences for a week:

    9/20  the game in one line: "BATTLE BROTHERS ON A PHONE, A LOT BETTER"
    9/22  rule 23, LOCKED: the fight is BATTLE BROTHERS, QUICKER
    9/22  QUESTS, on arguing a price: "do it the same way Battle Brothers does it,
          push too much hurts reputation, NOTHING LESS THAN BATTLE BROTHERS"
    9/23  rule 32(d): the three names come PREPARED, like Battle Brothers

Four separate rulings, in four lanes, all naming the same game. Now he has named it again
with no sentence around it, to this lane.

**NOT CERTAIN, AND NOT MINE TO DECIDE:** which of this lane's rows that becomes. Turning a
two-word direction into a running order is exactly the thing the coordinator exists for,
and rule 10 says only the coordinator adds jobs to the board. I am not writing myself a
row off two words and calling it his instruction. It goes to him as this record and as a
line in the handoff.

## WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHY THAT IS THE POINT

I did not stop the round to ask him what he meant. Rule 1: this lane never asks him
anything. I did not guess a feature and build it either, which is the failure the STOP
PRODUCING law is written about -- a lane built the same unwanted thing four times with
every gate green because it kept inferring instead of recording.

So: the words are on the record, the coordinator carries them, and this round shipped the
job this lane already held.

## ROUTED

- **TO THE COORDINATOR:** his two words, above, verbatim. This lane's board line for them
  is his to write.
- **ALREADY LIVE AND NOT WAITING ON ANYTHING:** the campaign-layer study is
  `laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_BATTLE_BROTHERS_AND_THE_GAMBIT_8_28_26.md`, and BATTLE BROTHERS
  belongs to the campaign layer by the one-department rule
  (`laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_A_REFERENCE_GAME_BELONGS_TO_ONE_DEPARTMENT_9_5_26.md`). Anything
  this lane builds toward it reads that first rather than inventing a second reading of
  the same game.

## THE READING ("the best year" = the best gear; "3040 days" = 30 to 40 days; "Sonic" = Sonnet)
1. THE FIGHT GETS DEEP. 450 hours to master Battle Brothers' combat; squad formation and gear are the depth;

   MODS.
7. DIFFICULTY SLIDERS: ours to design and optimize ("well beyond me").
8. The new chats go on Sonnet. He wants no blind spots.

# PAOLO 9/24/26: THE OVERWORLD IS BATTLE BROTHERS (voice-to-text, verbatim, to the coordinator)

"Bro, I think I have to make an executive decision that like I think the overworld I think I wanted
it to be like the battle Brothers map. It's just so much easier to travel the world that way quicker
to we can still have so many cool things like pop-up events and stuff, but I think I think the
overworld is going to be more battle Brothers and even though the combat is heavily inspired, keeping
we're still gonna keep in mind that like each tile is as big as like a mini block like a building or
something so I think the combat we're still gonna go towards and then be very inspired by rogue fable
four cause I think if rogue fable four touch the combat of battle Brothers more than it'd be more fun
to be honest like tay stand on effect really other than like just like a small mound on the floor that
you can get like accuracy bonus stuff from but yeah I think I think we have to do this so we're we are
in a part of the revamp process and I need you to just continuously do big brain research on how
battle Brothers does things really good because I ultimately wanna economic apocalypse battle brother
shit on my phone with better story and everything so yeah"

## THE READING (garbles: "tay stand on effect" = terrain stand-on effect; "keeping" = keep in mind)
1. AN EXECUTIVE DECISION: THE OVERWORLD IS THE BATTLE BROTHERS MAP. Travelling the world the Battle
   Brothers way is easier and quicker. The walked street is no longer how you cross the valley.
2. POP-UP EVENTS STAY. "We can still have so many cool things like pop-up events and stuff." Events on
   the road, Battle Brothers style, are wanted; this amends 32a's "nothing forced" for the map (they
   still do not fire in the first minute, and they come from a mouth with a portrait, rule 19).
3. THE COMBAT TILE STAYS A BUILDING. "Each tile is as big as a mini block, like a building." Rule 16
   and the batteries law stand in the fight.
4. THE COMBAT IS ROGUE FABLE 4 FIRST, BATTLE BROTHERS SECOND. "Very inspired by Rogue Fable 4, because
   if Rogue Fable 4 touched the combat of Battle Brothers more, it'd be more fun." The 9/22 addendum
   (the fight is Battle Brothers, quicker) is read through this: RF4 leads the feel; BB is the flavour.
5. TERRAIN: ONLY THE MOUND. "No terrain stand-on effect really, other than a small mound on the floor
   you can get an accuracy bonus from." One terrain effect in the whole fight: high ground = accuracy.
6. WE ARE IN A REVAMP. "We are in a part of the revamp process." The demo's WALKING becomes TRAVEL on
   the map plus ARRIVAL on the street.
7. CONTINUOUS BIG-BRAIN RESEARCH ON BATTLE BROTHERS. "I need you to just continuously do big brain
   research on how Battle Brothers does things really good." Every round, every chat, one page on how
   Battle Brothers does its department well.
8. THE GAME IN ONE LINE, HIS WORDS: "ECONOMIC APOCALYPSE BATTLE BROTHERS ON MY PHONE, WITH A BETTER
   STORY AND EVERYTHING." Replaces 9/20's "Battle Brothers on a phone, a lot better".

## DEFAULTS THE MANAGER DECIDED (EVERYTHING IS A THUMB; each in VOTE)
- THE MAP IS THE CITY VIEW. We already have it: one squeeze out (RUN [way back]) is the zoomed-out valley
  with the cracked phone on it. That view becomes the Battle Brothers map: a party marker, tap where to
  go, time passes as you travel, roads are faster than dirt, other parties roam visibly, places are
  destinations. One game mode (rule 24): same buttons, same UI; the squeeze is the door.
- THE STREET IS WHERE YOU ARRIVE. The house-sized walked street survives as the PLACE (a block, a town,
  a camp) you enter from the map; you meet people there and the fight happens there on house tiles.
  Battle Brothers enters a town as menus; we enter it as a street. He corrects in VOTE if he wants
  menus.

   (a real slab, glass, cracks; not a console). The flip (A, UP) lives on that phone, so flipping acts is

   BATTLE BROTHERS AND YOU CAN RESHUFFLE NAMES OR NAME IT YOURSELF." (UP). RULE 32d: THE THREE NAMES
   COME PREPARED, Battle Brothers style: a generated name sits in each slot, a reshuffle button, or type
   your own; no flip to a descendant who has no name. Battle Brothers is already the campaign-layer
   reference, so this is inside its department.
5. "THESE ARE ALL DOGSHIT AND UNIMPRESSIVE, YOU NEED TO REALLY MAKE NEW SOUNDS, NOT THIS SAND-SOUNDING
   SHIT LIKE I'M ON THE BEACH" (the run, DOWN) + "IT ALL SOUNDED LIKE SAND" (the tape, DOWN) + "KINDA
   DOGSHIT" (the flip, DOWN). Three noise-built sounds killed in one batch. RULE 32e: NO SAND. The

6. "THIS GAME ISN'T IN FIRST PERSON, WHEN WOULD I SEE THIS?" (signs at night, UP) + "THE PICTURE WE WON'T

# HIS WORDS BOHEMIA_PAOLO_NEWGROUNDS_AND_THE_MACHINE_GUN_9_24_26.md
# source: records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_NEWGROUNDS_AND_THE_MACHINE_GUN_9_24_26.md
====================================================================================================
# PAOLO 9/24/26 (verbatim, correcting the coordinator): "New grounds is an old flash game website brother"
# and: "Like comparable to the weapons and battle Brothers maybe a machine gun you know cause in battle
# Brothers you have some weapons that can hit multiple tiles at the same times six or three you know so
# yeah maybe I'm machine gun is like comparable to like a great sword in battle, Brothers, or like a
# battle ax or something"

## 1. NEWGROUNDS IS NAMED (the coordinator misread it as "new ground" one message earlier; corrected)
His 9/24 sentence: "we can put more life into it with this analog horror, pixel, Newgrounds bullshit
we're doing." NEWGROUNDS is the early-2000s flash site: hand-made web animation and games, small teams,
loud, crude on purpose, sprite-and-tween motion, a home-made energy no studio product has. It is a
website and an era, not a game, so the reference rule reads it the way it reads analog horror: A LOOK
AND A VIBE, owned by ONE department, DIRECTION's bible. What of the Newgrounds era fits INSIDE analog
horror is what survives (the way FFX's sound was amended 9/20). Nobody studies a Newgrounds game as a
game; DIRECTION writes the page on what the era looked and sounded like and what it teaches our pixels
and our motion ("put more life into it").

## 2. WEAPONS HAVE SHAPES ON THE TILES, LIKE BATTLE BROTHERS
Battle Brothers has weapons that hit several tiles at once (a greatsword's swing, a battle axe's arc,
three or six tiles). Our version: A MACHINE GUN IS THE GREATSWORD. Alongside the reach rule already
ruled 9/22 (pistol 1 tile, rifle 2, scope 3), a weapon has a SHAPE: a machine gun sweeps a line of
tiles in one beat instead of one tile. This is Battle Brothers flavour in the fight, which rule 33d
allows as the second influence under Rogue Fable 4's speed. COMBAT [weapon shapes]: school on BB's
multi-tile weapons (which shapes, what they cost, why they read), then the shape table for ours in
plain words (pistol, rifle, scope, machine gun, shotgun as the spread), everything still costing one,
the dial for the important shot.

big brain research on games that I've done this shit before I think this is what the game
needed."

## THE READING (transcription garbles: "3X" = the three acts; "flipped through" = flip
## between them; "quest are inner look like" = the quests are interlinked like; "games that
## I've done this" = games that have done this)
1. THE THREE ACTS RUN AT THE SAME TIME AND HE FLIPS BETWEEN THEM. Not one after the other.
   Gen 1 Animal, Gen 2 Human, Gen 3 Angel are all open from the start of the game and one
   control flips him from one to the next, the way Ocarina of Time flips child Link and adult
   Link.
2. THE FUTURE SHOWS THE PAST'S SCORE. Flip forward early and the city is built like shit,
   because he has not done enough in the earlier act. "If you want to see more awesome
   futuristic technology life you gotta do more in the past." The future is the report card
   of the past, drawn as a city.
3. HOW THE FLIP HAPPENS IS OPEN: "I don't know if you have to do something in game or there's
   a simple option." A place in the world, or a button. Not decided by him; decided by
   default below, and it goes to VOTE.
4. QUESTS REACH ACROSS THE AGES, like Ocarina's: a thing done in one act is finished or paid
   in another.
5. THE THREE DESCENDANTS ARE NAMED, MALE OR FEMALE, "at the start of the game probably... or
   maybe slides into that early on into each act." Both readings kept; default below.
6. "DO BIG BRAIN RESEARCH ON GAMES THAT HAVE DONE THIS." School first. The coordinator's first
   pass is records/BOHEMIA_DYNASTY_SCHOOL_THE_THREE_ACTS_AT_ONCE_ROUND_ZERO_9_23_26.md; the
   DYNASTY chat carries the real two rounds.
7. "WE MIGHT HAVE TO DEDICATE A WHOLE CHAT TO IT." Decided: the DYNASTY chat IS that chat. Its
   whole subject was already the three generations and its research queue was empty. From
   this round it is DYNASTY (THE THREE ACTS AT ONCE), school then build. No 21st chat.
8. "I THINK THIS IS WHAT THE GAME NEEDED." Recorded as his weight on it: this is the spine,
   not a feature.

## THE REFERENCE GAME
Ocarina of Time is named by him for the first time. Under A REFERENCE GAME BELONGS TO ONE
DEPARTMENT it belongs to THE THREE ACTS AT ONCE (DYNASTY) and nowhere else: the flip, the
two-age world, the quest that reaches across ages. Not its combat, not its interface, not
its music. Every other game in the school record is research, not a reference; none of them
is named by him and none enters the design by name.

## WHAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH
The demo (rule 18: loading, walking, the fight, the first person) does not change. The flip is
ALPHA work, built where the acts live. Nothing in this ruling delays the demo push (rule 18i).

"Also, I'm trying to I'm trying to get it. You know your building so many game mechanics that
are super important but I'm really trying to push this demo out. A lot of pieces are coming

great idea for important parts of the combat to making more fun and engaging but yeah."

("road fable" is Rogue Fable, the fight's reference; "dead shot dial" is the Dead Eye Dial.)

## RULINGS (NOTES ARE RULINGS)
1. PUSH THE DEMO OUT. "I don't need the whole world, I don't need everything." Rule 18 stands
   and is sharpened: the demo is the four things and nothing else; every other mechanic goes to
   VOTE and waits. The fleet's making continues (rule 22); its shipping does not.
2. THE FIGHT MUST FEEL LIKE BATTLE BROTHERS, QUICKER AND FUNNER, on the beat (Rogue Fable). Rule
   17 was the LOOK; this adds the FEEL, and item 3 of the playable cut is now "the fight looks
   and feels like the game".
3. REACH IS SOMETHING HE FEELS. A pistol is a one-tile weapon, an assault rifle a two-tile
   weapon, "shit like that". The numbers exist on the house board since 9/4 (pistol 1, rifle 2,
   scope 3, a tile is a house); he cannot feel them. So: reach is lit on the tiles when he
   holds a weapon, a man out of reach cannot be shot, stepping in and out of reach is the
   whole dance, and the enemies play the same rule back at him on their beat.
4. RESTART COMBAT FROM THE GROUND UP? "I don't know if we have to." The manager's answer: NO
   for the board and the bodies (V222/V223 just made the ground his approved street and the
   fighter 112, and DIRECTION passed the seam), YES for the rules layer: the fight's rules are
   rebuilt on that board as three things: reach you can see, a turn that is a beat (both sides
   act on the beat, his presses on the beat, the companion on her gambits), and the dial only
   when it matters. Built, not asked; his to correct in VOTE.
5. THE DIAL IS FOR THE IMPORTANT SHOT. "The dead shot dial can be a great idea for important
   parts of the combat to make it more fun and engaging." NO DAMAGE BEFORE THE DIAL is amended
   by his words: routine exchanges resolve on the beat without the dial (a hit inside reach on
   the beat lands and costs one, EVERYTHING COSTS ONE), and the dial comes up for the shot that
   matters (the kill shot, the boss, the called shot, the one that turns the fight), where it
   decides what that shot does. The dial still owns every number bigger than one.
6. QUICKER: a fight is over in beats, not minutes; DIRECTION's two numbers (seconds from the
   cloud to over, his presses versus the companion's) are the measure, and PLUMBER's 60 on a
   phone is the floor for "quicker".

# PAOLO 9/21/26 -- A PLAYBOOK FOR HIS BOSS'S ASSISTANT UI (his words, verbatim, and what was made)

"OKAY BRO SO MY BOSS OSCAR WANTS HELP MAKING A UI FOR HIS PERSONAL ASSISTANT OR WHATEVER SO I
NEED YOU TO GRAB ALL THE SAUCE WITH UI WEVE BEEN WORKING ON EVERYTHING WEVE LEARNED AND MAKE A
MARKDOWN OR A PDF TO SUPPORT HIM. DONT MENTION BOHEMIA. DONT MENTION MY NAME. BUT HIS CHAT BOT
HIS CODEBOT NEEDED CLEAR GUIDANCE ON OUR VOTING PROCESS, ALL OF OUR PROCESSES, SAUCE WEVE
RESEARCHED AND LEARNED. HOW TO INTEGRATE IT INTO HIS SHIT AND MAKE IT SUPER EASY FOR HIM TO
CUSTOMISE THE UI EXPORTING VERDICTS AND THAT WHOLE ENCHILADA. COULD YOU DO THIS FOR ME? SHOULD I
GO INTO THE UI CHAT AND ASK OR CAN I ASK YOU? ANY BLINDSPORT? ANYTHING I DONT KNOW I DONT KNOW"

## WHAT WAS MADE
exports/THE_JUDGE_QUEUE_PLAYBOOK.md and .html: the voting process (one queue, a vote consumes,
redo quotes the kill, notes are rulings, stale is dead, decide-then-correct, aesthetic and
philosophical items), the registry schema with an example, the export road (copy all, .txt never
.json, local storage), the notes section, the process rules (one word starts a round, two-word
labels, claim first, newest date wins, machine gates with mutation proof, verbatim records,
re-read before write, cook every round, reports lead with the thing), the reply contract, the UI
sauce (the vibe-coded tells, 44 px, sun mode, gold is you / cold is the machine, the 2 px line
at 3.78:1, cut corners, pressed is a flip, a font is a file, controls drawn not typed, letters
tested at size, 3-D as four things with stepped ramps, the interface-study findings), the
verification lessons (real surface, print the file, one run is a coin, unknown vs no, cold
first run, a red gate nobody reads, a ratchet), a ten-step integration recipe, eleven blind
spots, and two appendices (a minimal queue page, the bot's read-back). No project name, no
person's name anywhere in the export. Published as a page for his boss to open.

## ANSWERS TO HIS THREE QUESTIONS
- Ask me, not the UI chat: the UI chat knows one lane; the voting process and the laws are the
  manager's, and the UI chat is mid-round on his own asks.
- Blind spots are section 10 of the playbook (eleven).
- What he did not know he did not know: a web page cannot write a file, so verdicts leave by the
  clipboard and the bot commits them; the queue belongs where the decider judges, not in the
  public build; names stay the human's; a sound needs a tap.

## NOT A GAME RULING
Nothing here changes the board. Filed as a record because his words were said to the manager.

## ADDED WHILE WRITING: "KEEP IN MIND HE DOESN'T PAY FOR CLAUDE, JUST THE FREE VERSION"
Section 11 of the playbook: on a free chat bot there is no code running, no files, no git and a
small memory, so the loop becomes one chat, one self-contained page with the registry embedded in
it, verdicts out by COPY ALL and back by paste, one pasted board as the memory, one round per
message, small artifacts, gates as a checklist the bot reads against its own output, a round
number by hand instead of a build stamp, and the three rules that matter most when no machine
stands behind them. Both exports checked: zero mentions of the project, him or his boss.

## RULINGS (NOTES ARE RULINGS)

### 1. BATTLE BROTHERS ON MY PHONE, A LOT BETTER
1. The sentence that names the game, recorded as the identity line beside "the most
   realistic economic crash simulator, but fun": BATTLE BROTHERS ON A PHONE, A LOT BETTER,
   WITH EVERYTHING WE HAVE GOING ON. Battle Brothers stays the CAMPAIGN LAYER reference
   and nothing else (9/5: a reference belongs to one department).
2. The fight is NOT Battle Brothers' fight. "Chest match" is chess match: their long
   turn-by-turn board is the thing he does not want. Ours is QUICK, on the beat (Rogue
   Fable 4, 120 BPM), and it FOCUSES ON THE PLAYER CHARACTER: the camera, the choices and
   the danger are his; the companions "auto do stuff" (the gambit law, FF12, 8/28: the
   automated companion). All three were already ruled; he is saying them again because the
   fight he saw was none of them. THE FIGHT VERDICT (DIRECTION, rule 17) now carries two
   numbers every round: seconds from the cloud to the fight over, and how many of the
   presses were his versus the companion's. -> COMBAT [fight looks] note, DIRECTION [judge
   the fight] note.
3. "We talked a lot about this": correct, the Battle Brothers study (8/28) and the gambit
   ruling. Nothing is re-opened; the 9/20 section of that addendum records his phrasing.
4. "Has to be a lot better": the measure is the four things of the playable cut on a phone.

### 2. ANALOG HORROR FOR EVERY PIXEL AND EVERY SOUND
5. A LAW, LOCKED, "end of story forever": for the rest of the cycle, as long as the game is
   not done, every pixel and every sound is thought about as ANALOG HORROR first. The whole
   enchilada: tiles, bodies, faces, the interface, the loading screen, the fight, the
   music, the room tone, the voices.
6. "Machine party" is the reference he named 8/3 (Mike Klubnika's game; laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_NO_PAINT_8_3_26.md);
   it stands and it is the bridge. "Not putting a grim filter" is the 8/3 debate: the grime
   is a machine at bake time, not a paint. FULLY COMMIT amends that debate by date: analog
   horror is not a VHS filter over a normal frame either. It is what is IN the frame, the
   light, the stillness and the sound, decided at the source. The grime machine stays; the
   direction it serves is now named.
7. Analog horror is a GENRE direction, not a reference game. NEVER ADD A REFERENCE GAME HE
   HAS NOT NAMED stands: no named series, channel or film is studied or cited unless he
   names it. DIRECTION writes the bible from the genre's own grammar.
8. THE SOUNDS COMPLEMENT IT. The 9/6 sound ruling ("post-apocalyptic FFX, that fantasy
   beach vibe") is AMENDED by date: the sound serves analog horror first; what of the FFX
   sound survives is what SOUNDS' school finds fits inside it (the manager's default: a
   warm, beautiful melody heard through a dead broadcast is itself analog horror; he
   corrects in the VOTE tab). The 120 BPM law stands.
9. Routing: DIRECTION [analog horror] first line (the bible, then the fight verdict judges
   against it, then the compare-to-the-world gate carries it); SOUNDS [analog horror
   sound] first line (school, then the keep/redo list of every sound); UI [analog horror
   ui]; WORDS Q27 [analog horror voice]; COOK [horror grime] held until the bible; PORTRAIT
   note on [faces first]; RUN note on [loading screen]; COMBAT note on [fight looks]; EYES
   E28 [horror check] standing. Under rule 18 these are school and measurement rounds
   except where they touch one of the four things, which are drawn to the bible from now.

### 3. THE ALPHA OPENS IN THE VOTE TAB
10. "Everything that needs to get voted on goes into the vote section" is reaffirmed:
    the VOTE tab is the only place he votes (rule 15a).
11. THE ALPHA OPENS IN VOTE. After the loading screen (rule 18a), the alpha lands on the

====================================================================================================
# PAOLO'S 8/1 LIST — EVERY DEFECT DIAGNOSED (8/2/26)

> "until all the request in this thing I copied from a couple chats ago you get done
> you cannot move on"

Twelve investigators, read-only, each measuring on the REAL surface rather than
reading source, each followed by an adversarial verifier told to default to
REFUTED unless it could independently confirm the anchor exists and the patch is
not a placebo. This file is the result. It exists so no future session re-derives
any of it.

---

## wallheight_gate.js "THE TALL DOOR IS NOT SQUASHED" goes 6/0 -> 5/1 when the city full-pixel patch (TPX 22->44) is applied — the exact 44x44 -> 44x88 draw, named.

**already done:** False  **confidence:** high

### ROOT CAUSE

THE OFFENDING DRAW IS tallTex's OWN CACHE-FILL, AND IT NEVER TOUCHES THE SCREEN.

City blob line 9285 (patched numbering; 9269 unpatched), inside tallTex():
    xx.drawImage(im,0,0,w,h*n);
It is reached lazily from facadePass line 9323, `const d2=tallTex('hdoor',v,2)`, on the first frame the gate grabs, because TALLCV is cold at that moment. `im` is saTex('hdoor',v), a TPX x TPX canvas; `cc` is a NEW OFFSCREEN canvas of w x h*n. At TPX=44 that is a 44x44 source stretched once into a 44x88 offscreen cache canvas. The destination context is `cc`, NOT the world canvas `cv`.

The orchestrator's elimination of "the d2=tallTex('hdoor',v,2) call (its source is already 44x88)" was half right and that half is what hid it: the BLIT of d2 is 44x88 -> 44x88 on cv and is perfectly 1:1. It is the CALL — the derive-once-and-cache that d2 depends on — that performs the stretch, one level down the stack, on a different canvas.

WHY THE GATE CANNOT SEE THE DIFFERENCE. gates/wallheight_gate.js classifies a draw purely by destination pixel size:
    const isFacade = x => Math.abs(x.dw - C) < 1.5 && (Math.abs(x.dh - C) < 1.5 || Math.abs(x.dh - 2*C) < 1.5);
Its PROBE records dx/dy/dw/dh/sw/sh/alpha and deliberately throws away which canvas received the draw. So "one cell wide by two cells tall" is the ONLY thing that makes something a facade to this gate. tallTex's cache canvas is BY CONSTRUCTION exactly one cell wide by two cells tall — that is its entire purpose. The gate is therefore failing the precise mechanism its own docstring says it exists to bless: "the 16x32 door tile is derived once and cached, never stretched per frame."

WHY IT ONLY BREAKS AT TPX=44. saTex() prescales every tile to TPX x TPX. At TPX=22 the identical tallTex derivation is 22x22 -> 22x44, and dw=22 misses C=44 by 22px, so it falls out of isFacade and lands in the gate's ungated `offAspect` bucket — where the gate PRINTS IT TODAY, mislabeled as the street lamp. Raise TPX to 44 and the cache canvas dimensions coincide byte-for-byte with a facade destination; the same draw, unchanged, walks into the bucket and fails. Nothing about the render regressed. The gate's measurement was accidentally coupled to TPX being smaller than the on-screen cell.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT CORRUPTION OF THE SAME GATE AT TPX=44 (not currently failing, but the check stops meaning anything): the chunk bake writes CHK x CHK tiles at TPX px into a 704x704 texture canvas. Measured in the gate's own frame, that is 6,353 draws of 44x44 -> 44x44, every one of which now satisfies dw≈C && dh≈C. The gate's `cell()` count goes 34 -> 6,417, so "THREE TILES TALL: facades draw a full cell high (behindCell > 10)" would from then on be measuring the offscreen bake, not facades. Any fix that only silences the aspect failure leaves this lie in place.

### EVIDENCE

1) THE STACK TRACE, captured by wrapping drawImage in a real browser (playwright chromium-1194), on a scratch copy of the alpha with tools/bohemia_city_full_pixel_patch.py applied, HC forced to 44, standing behind a door in suburb cell [12,4], door cell [1577,528]:

  "badCount": 1,
  "bad": [{ "sw":44, "sh":44, "dw":44, "dh":88, "al":1, "cid":"", "cw":44, "ch":88,
    "st": "Error
        at P.drawImage (<anonymous>:15:19)
        at tallTex (about:srcdoc:9285:6)
        at facadePass (about:srcdoc:9323:18)
        at renderHuman (about:srcdoc:9637:3)
        at render (about:srcdoc:9656:107)" }]

  cw/ch = 44x88 is the DESTINATION CANVAS: the offscreen cache, not cv (378x765).

2) THE CODE AT THAT LINE — city blob (patched numbering), tallTex:
  9279   const k=pool+'|'+v+'|'+n; if(TALLCV.has(k))return TALLCV.get(k);
  9280   const im=saTex(pool,v);
  9282   const w=im.width||16, h=im.height||16;
  9283   const cc=document.createElement('canvas'); cc.width=w; cc.height=h*n;
  9284   const xx=cc.getContext('2d'); xx.imageSmoothingEnabled=false;
  9285   xx.drawImage(im,0,0,w,h*n);            <-- 44x44 -> 44x88
  9286   TALLCV.set(k,cc); return cc;
and the caller, facadePass:
  9323         const d2=tallTex('hdoor',v,2);
  9324         if(d2)g.drawImage(d2,dx,dy-C,C,C*2);   /* this one IS 44x88 -> 44x88, innocent */
and the source of the 44px: saTex (blob line 8819-8820)
  const c2=document.createElement('canvas'); c2.width=TPX; c2.height=TPX;
  c2.getContext('2d').drawImage(im,0,0,TPX,TPX);

3) FULL DRAW HISTOGRAM of the measured frame at TPX=44 (source -> dest @ destination canvas):
  44x44->44x44   @704x704   6353    the chunk bake (offscreen) - floods `cell()`
  16x16->44x44   @44x44       18    saTex prescale (offscreen)
  44x44->44x44   @44x44       12    saTex prescale (offscreen)
  704x704->704x704 @378x765   20    chunk blits ON SCREEN
  44x44->44x44   @378x765     34    THE REAL FACADE CELLS
  44x88->44x88   @378x765      1    THE REAL TALL DOOR, 1:1, innocent
  112x112->112x112 @378x765    1    the player
  44x44->44x88   @44x88        1    <-- THE ENTIRE FAILURE, offscreen
  total 6440 draws; only 56 landed on the world canvas.

4) THE GATE HAS BEEN PRINTING THIS DRAW ALL ALONG AND CALLING IT SOMETHING ELSE.
   Running the UNPATCHED gate on the UNPATCHED alpha (main today) emits:
     (not gated: 22x22->22x44 - the street lamp, drawn 1.5 x 3 cells from a square tile on purpose)
   22x22->22x44 is NOT the street lamp. The lamp is drawn C*1.5 x C*3 (66x132 at C=44) and is
   aspect-correct against its source, which is why it does not appear in that bucket at all once
   the bucket is scoped to cv. 22x22->22x44 is tallTex's cache fill at TPX=22, exactly.

5) THE 2x3 CONTROL MATRIX (all runs real browser, gates/wallheight_gate.js machinery unchanged
   except the patch below; "regressed" = I injected a genuine per-frame stretch on cv by replacing
   the d2 blit with `if(wall)g.drawImage(wall,dx,dy-C,C,C*2)`):

   tree                                  original gate     patched gate
   main, TPX=22                          6 pass / 0 fail   7 pass / 0 fail
   + full pixel patch, TPX=44            5 pass / 1 FAIL   7 pass / 0 fail
   + pixel patch + injected stretch      5 pass / 1 fail   6 pass / 1 FAIL

   The bottom row is the proof this is not a rubber stamp: the scoped gate still catches a real
   per-frame aspect change on the surface Paolo sees.

6) INSTRUMENTED COUNTS, patched vs unpatched, same predicates:
   TPX=44: onCvBehind 56, onCvAway 142, cell() unscoped 6417, faded 8 / away 0
   TPX=22: onCvBehind 56, onCvAway 142, cell() unscoped   34, faded 8 / away 0
   faded counts are IDENTICAL scoped or not (every fade is on cv), so scoping `faded` is free.

7) BRANCH STATE: commit da225b3 landed the root-cause writeup, tools/bohemia_city_full_pixel_patch.py
