====================================================================================================
# 03 WEAPONS: CLASSES, SKILLS, AND THEIR SHAPE ON THE TILES (recall unless cited)
# Paolo 9/24: "some weapons hit multiple tiles at the same time, six or three; a machine gun is comparable
# to a greatsword or a battle axe." This file is the shape table he asked about. Numbers are recall.

ONE-HANDED (4 AP an attack, two attacks a turn):
- SWORDS (Shortsword 25-30, Arming Sword 30-40, Noble Sword 35-45; low fatigue 10-12; ignore ~25% armour,
  70% armour damage): SLASH (one tile), RIPOSTE (free counter-attack on every miss against you this turn).
  Shape: ONE TILE. The precise cheap weapon.
- AXES (Hatchet 25-35, Hand Axe 30-40, Fighting Axe 35-45; fatigue 15; ignore ~30% armour, 110-120% armour
  damage): CHOP (one tile, +30% head chance recall), SPLIT SHIELD (destroys shield durability fast). Shape:
  ONE TILE, kills shields.
- MACES (Club, Mace 30-40, Winged Mace 35-45; ignore ~25%, 100% armour damage): BASH (one tile, dazes: the
  target loses AP next turn), KNOCK OUT (stun one turn). Shape: ONE TILE, controls a man.
- HAMMERS (Wooden Hammer, Military Pick / Hammer 35-45; ignore 20-30%, 150% armour damage; some hammers
  ignore 100% of a shield's block): STRIKE (one tile), SHATTER / DEMOLISH ARMOUR. Shape: ONE TILE, eats
  armour.
- CLEAVERS (Butcher's Cleaver, Military Cleaver 40-50, Orc Cleaver; ignore ~20%, 80% armour damage):
  CLEAVE (one tile, BLEED 5 a turn), DECAPITATE (bonus vs low hitpoints; a decapitation cannot rise as
  undead). WHIP (Lash 2 tiles away, Disarm). Shape: ONE TILE, bleeds.
- FLAILS (Flail 35-45, Three-headed Flail): FLAIL (one tile, IGNORES SHIELDS: the shield's defence does
  not count), LASH. Shape: ONE TILE over the shield.
- SPEARS (Spear 25-35, Boar Spear; +20% to hit): THRUST (one tile), SPEARWALL (any enemy entering an
  adjacent tile is hit first and stopped). Shape: ONE TILE + a zone.
- DAGGERS (Knife, Dagger, Rondel 15-25): STAB, PUNCTURE (ignores ALL armour, low damage: the finisher
  for stealing armour intact). Shape: ONE TILE through armour.
- THROWING (Javelins 2-4 range, Throwing Axes, Throwing Spears): one tile at range 2 to 3.

TWO-HANDED (6 AP an attack, one attack a turn; high fatigue 20-25; the greatsword class Paolo means):
- GREATSWORD (Greatsword 55-75, Warbrand 50-70): SWING (hits THREE tiles: the target and the two tiles
  beside it in front, one roll each), SPLIT (hits TWO tiles in a line: the target and the one behind).
  *** SHAPE: A 3-WIDE ARC or a 2-DEEP LINE. THIS IS THE MACHINE GUN. ***
- TWO-HANDED AXE (Battle Axe 60-80; Greataxe 70-90): ROUND SWING (hits ALL SIX adjacent tiles, friend or
  foe, one roll each), SPLIT MAN (one tile, +head chance, huge). *** SHAPE: SIX AROUND. ***
- TWO-HANDED MACE (Two-handed Flanged Mace 60-80): CUDGEL (one tile, dazes), STRIKE DOWN (one tile,
  stuns). Shape: ONE TILE, hard.
- TWO-HANDED HAMMER (Two-handed Hammer 55-75): SHATTER (one tile, 200%+ armour damage), DEMOLISH ARMOUR.
- TWO-HANDED FLAIL (Two-handed Flail 50-70): THRESH (hits THREE tiles in front, ignores shields), LASH.
  *** SHAPE: 3-WIDE, over shields. ***
- TWO-HANDED CLEAVER (Two-handed Cleaver / Orc Cleaver): CLEAVE (one tile, bleed, big), DECAPITATE.
- POLEARMS (range 2, attack from the second row): PIKE: IMPALE (two tiles away, one target), THRUST;
  BILLHOOK: HOOK (pulls the target one tile toward you), IMPALE; LONGAXE: CHOP at range 2, SPLIT
  SHIELD at range 2; POLEHAMMER; WARSCYTHE: REAP (hits the target and adjacent), GOBLIN PIKE. Shape:
  ONE TILE AT DISTANCE 2 (our rifle), REAP is an arc at 2.
- RANGED: BOWS (Short Bow, Hunting Bow, War Bow 30-60 range 7; QUICK SHOT 4 AP, AIMED SHOT 6 AP +hit):
  one tile at range, no reload; CROSSBOWS (Light, Heavy 55-75, range 6; SHOOT 5 AP, RELOAD 4 AP): one
  tile, hard, a reload beat; HANDGONNE (Blazing Deserts: fires a CONE of pellets hitting everything in
  a 3-tile-deep wedge, one shot then a long reload): *** THE SHOTGUN SHAPE. ***
- SHIELDS as weapons: Shield Bash / Knock Back (pushes a man one tile).
NAMED AND LEGENDARY ITEMS: rolled variants with +damage, +durability, -fatigue, unique names and
descriptions; found in legendary locations and on champions.
THE MAP TO OURS (rule 33i default, COMBAT decides the table): pistol = one tile (arming sword), rifle =
two tiles away (pike), scope = three away (bow), machine gun = a 3-wide sweep in one beat (greatsword
SWING), shotgun = a cone (handgonne), a bat or a pipe = mace (daze), a knife = dagger PUNCTURE. Every
shot still costs one; the dial is the important shot.


====================================================================================================
# BATTLE BROTHERS LIBRARY 04_ARMOUR_SHIELDS.md
# source: reference/library/battle_brothers/04_ARMOUR_SHIELDS.md
====================================================================================================
# 04 ARMOUR, HELMETS, SHIELDS (recall)
BODY ARMOUR: durability (armour points) and a fatigue penalty (weight). Tiers: rags/linen 15-25 (-1 to
-2 fatigue), padded tunic/leather 45-65 (-4 to -6), gambeson 75, mail shirt 95 (-10), leather lamellar 105,
scale/reinforced mail 130-160 (-16 to -20), heavy lamellar/coat of plates 200-230 (-26 to -32), named
armours higher. Armour absorbs a hit until it is broken through; repaired with tools between fights.
HELMETS: same shape, 20 (leather cap) to 300 (great helm); full helms lower vision (some -ranged skill or
-initiative). A head hit against no helmet is where men die.
SHIELDS: a shield adds melee and ranged defence (buckler +5/+5 low fatigue; heater/kite +15/+25 recall;
tower shields more, heavy), has DURABILITY that axes destroy, and enables SHIELDWALL (+defence this
turn, costs AP and fatigue) and KNOCK BACK. Two-handed weapons cannot use a shield: the trade is the
whole tactical spine (offence and fatigue vs survival).
ATTACHMENTS (later DLC): a cloak, a padding, a spiked impaler, a leather aketon under mail etc., each a
trade of armour vs fatigue vs a special.
FATIGUE TAX: total fatigue penalty of armour + helmet + weapon + shield is subtracted from max fatigue;
a 230 armour man in a great helm with a two-hander has little left to swing with. Nimble (perk) rewards
light armour; Battle Forged rewards heavy.


====================================================================================================
# BATTLE BROTHERS LIBRARY 05_PERKS.md
# source: reference/library/battle_brothers/05_PERKS.md
====================================================================================================
# 05 PERKS (recall; 7 tiers, one point per level, a tier unlocks every level; ~44 perks)
TIER 1: COLOSSUS (+25% hitpoints), NINE LIVES (survive one killing blow per fight at a few hitpoints),
BAGS AND BELTS (+2 bag slots, no fatigue penalty on bag items), PATHFINDER (all terrain costs 2 AP, less
fatigue), ADRENALINE (act first next turn, costs fatigue), RECOVER (drop fatigue by half, ends turn),
STUDENT (+20% xp until level 11, then a free perk), CRIPPLING STRIKES (more injuries), FAST ADAPTATION
(+hit chance per miss, resets on hit), GIFTED (+3 to every stat... recall: a free level-up's worth).
TIER 2: EXECUTIONER (+20% damage to injured), DODGE (+15% of initiative as defence), FORTIFIED MIND (+25%
resolve), RESILIENT (injuries and debuffs shorter), STEEL BRAW (hits to the head do not injure/kill on
first pass... recall: SHIELD EXPERT +25% shield defence, shields take less damage), BRAWNY (armour fatigue
penalty -30%), RELENTLESS (fatigue does not lower initiative), HOLD OUT (+?), STEADFAST (morale check
bonus).
TIER 3: BACKSTABBER (surrounded bonus +10 per attacker instead of +5), ANTICIPATION (+ranged defence per
distance), SHIELD EXPERT, ROTATION (swap places with an ally, no ZOC penalty), QUICK HANDS (swap weapons
for 0 AP once a turn), TAUNT (enemies attack you), BATTLE FLOW? (recall uncertain), FOOTWORK (leave ZOC
free once), UNDERDOG (surrounded penalty against you halved), LONE WOLF (+15% stats when alone).
TIER 4: WEAPON MASTERIES (Sword, Axe, Mace, Hammer, Cleaver, Flail, Spear, Dagger, Polearm, Bow,
Crossbow, Throwing: each cuts fatigue cost and adds a weapon-specific bonus like +chance to hit or
bleed), REACH ADVANTAGE (two-handers gain melee defence per hit this turn), OVERWHELM (each attack lowers
the target's defence), RALLY THE TROOPS (raise nearby allies' morale, leader perk), INDOMITABLE (halve
damage for a turn).
TIER 5: BERSERK (a kill refunds 4 AP), HEAD HUNTER (misses raise head hit chance), LOOKOUT? (recall), BRAWNY.
TIER 6: FEARSOME (hits cause morale checks), DUELIST (one-hander with no shield ignores more armour),
KILLING FRENZY (+25% damage for two turns after a kill), NIMBLE (light armour: take a fraction of
hitpoint damage), BATTLE FORGED (heavy armour: armour takes less damage per point worn), DEVASTATING
STRIKES? (recall).
TIER 7: THE LAST STAND? (recall).
THE SHAPE: a man is built as a ROLE (tank, two-hander, polearm second row, archer, dagger looter) by the
tier-7 pick (Nimble vs Battle Forged) and the mastery; perks are one line each and read at a glance; the
tree is the same for every man, so builds are the player's story about him.


====================================================================================================
# BATTLE BROTHERS LIBRARY 06_BACKGROUNDS.md
# source: reference/library/battle_brothers/06_BACKGROUNDS.md
====================================================================================================
# 06 BACKGROUNDS (recall; wages in crowns per day; hire cost 50 to 2,000+)
A recruit has a BACKGROUND (his past), a level, stats rolled in the background's ranges with 3 hidden
TALENT STARS on stats, a wage, a hire cost, and HIDDEN TRAITS revealed after hiring (some backgrounds
lean to some traits). Backgrounds also gate EVENTS (a Thief steals, a Monk preaches, a Cultist recruits,
a Noble insults a Beggar) and dialog choices.
CHEAP (wage 5-9): BEGGAR (low everything, may have Lucky), DAYTALER (average, cheap, often decent), FARMHAND
(decent hitpoints, fatigue), VAGABOND, THIEF (high initiative, ranged defence, steals from the company),
HISTORIAN?, JUGGLER (ranged skill, initiative), MINER (fatigue, hitpoints), FISHERMAN, SHEPHERD, GRAVEDIGGER
(resolve vs undead), CRIPPLE (cheap, injured), MESSENGER (initiative), CULTIST (resolve, cultist events),
BUTCHER (cleavers), TAILOR, APPRENTICE (+xp), BRAWLER (melee skill), BEAST SLAYER? (mid).
MID (10-16): MILITIA (balanced soldier-ish), CARAVAN HAND, POACHER (ranged skill, cheap archer),
WILDMAN (hitpoints, fatigue, low resolve/initiative), MONK (resolve, low melee), HOUNDMASTER, WITCHHUNTER
(resolve, ranged), RATCATCHER, BOWYER, LUMBERJACK (hitpoints, two-handed leaning), MINSTREL, DESERTER
(good stats, coward trait risk), GAMBLER, GRAVEROBBER, THIEF.
ELITE (18-30+): HEDGE KNIGHT (best melee, expensive, arrogant), SWORDMASTER (huge melee skill and
defence, low hitpoints, old), SELLSWORD (solid all-round, expensive), RAIDER (former brigand, good melee,
cheap-ish, hated by nobles), ADVENTUROUS NOBLE (resolve, melee, -ranged defence, wage 25, start level
1-3), ASSASSIN (initiative, melee, wage 20, start level 4), RETIRED SOLDIER (veteran, old), BASTARD,
SQUIRE, HUNTER (best ranged), NOMAD, ANATOMIST, MANHUNTER, BARBARIAN (huge hitpoints/fatigue, low
resolve), INDEBTED (a slave with a debt, cheap, miserable), MASTER ARCHER? (rare), KILLER ON THE RUN.
STATS: Hitpoints, Fatigue, Resolve, Initiative, Melee Skill, Ranged Skill, Melee Defence, Ranged Defence.
Level-ups: 3 stats gain a roll each; a star adds to the roll. Level 11 is the practical cap for perks.
TRAITS (two-edged, hidden until hired unless a Barber/event reveals): Strong, Tough, Iron Lungs, Quick,
Brave, Fearless, Lucky, Sure Footing, Eagle Eyes, Deathwish, Bloodthirsty, Determined | Weak, Fragile,
Asthmatic, Clumsy, Coward, Dumb, Fat, Greedy (+wage), Drunkard, Hesitant, Night Blind, Superstitious,
Dastard, Bleeder, Paranoid, Insecure, Impatient, Old (declines), Young (grows). Traits gained by events
and injuries: Survivor, Battle-hardened, Fearsome, Brute, Huge, Tiny, Hate for X, Lost eye, etc.
WHAT A BACKGROUND DOES FOR THE STORY: the roster reads as a cast at a glance (a Beggar, a Hedge Knight,
a Cultist); events pick men by background; a man's death is a story because his past was shown.
(OURS, rule 33 [bb company]: a person's background is what they did before the money died: lineman,
dealer, nurse, cop, casino floor, delivery, ex-con; the deed ledger is our traits.)

# BATTLE BROTHERS LIBRARY 07_ECONOMY.md
# source: reference/library/battle_brothers/07_ECONOMY.md
====================================================================================================
# 07 THE ECONOMY (recall)
CROWNS: one currency. A starting company has ~500-700 crowns and 3 men after the origin fight.
DAILY COST: wages (5 to 30 per man per day; +2 per level; Greedy +2), food (a man eats ~1 unit a day;
bread 3-4 crowns, dried fruit, cheese, salted meat, fish, mead; spoilage per type), tools (to repair;
~1 crown per 3 armour points repaired recall), medicine (per wound day), ammo (arrows/bolts per shot).
A 12-man company burns 150-300 crowns a day; the game is a treadmill that forces contracts.
INCOME: contracts (100 to 3,000+ crowns by difficulty and renown; a negotiation with a mood face;
pushing too hard costs relations), loot sold (weapons and armour sell for a fraction; damaged sells for
less), trade goods (buy where produced: salt, furs, dyes, silk, incense, wine, amber, gems; sell where
absent; margin 20-100%; prices rise as you sell, fall as you buy), legendary loot.
PRICES: per settlement, driven by its type (a fishing village has fish; a city has everything at a
premium), its SITUATIONS (raided: food scarce and dear; well-supplied: cheap), and your relation (allied
house discount). Buying raises the local price, selling lowers it; prices recover over days.
RENOWN: gates contract tiers and pay; shown as a bar. RELATIONS: per house and per settlement.
AMBITIONS: chosen goals with renown rewards, a light spine ("hire 12 men", "amass 5,000 crowns", "win a
contract with three skulls", "defeat a champion", "reach 1,000 renown", "gain a legendary item").
THE LOOP: contract -> pay -> resupply -> a better man -> a harder contract; the crash is running out of
crowns with wages due, which strips men away. (OURS: batteries; a day costs one; the loan of one a night
is the wage; prices per place by supply; ECONOMY [bb money] writes the table.)


====================================================================================================
# BATTLE BROTHERS LIBRARY 08_CONTRACTS_EVENTS.md
# source: reference/library/battle_brothers/08_CONTRACTS_EVENTS.md
====================================================================================================
# 08 CONTRACTS AND EVENTS (recall)
CONTRACTS come from a settlement's hall (a speaker with a portrait: the village elder, the town
magistrate, a noble's steward, a merchant). Difficulty in skulls (1-3), pay offered, a NEGOTIATION: ask
for more (the client's face and words shift: pleased, annoyed, angry; pushing too hard he withdraws and
relations dip), ask for an advance, ask for supplies. Types: escort a caravan; deliver a package (it may be
stolen goods or a body); clear a camp (brigands, orcs, goblins, undead, beasts); hunt a monster (a
Lindwurm, an Unhold, a Nachzehrer pack); patrol a road (kill N enemies); protect a village from a raid
(defend at night); retrieve a stolen item; investigate a disappearance; a noble house's war contracts
(raze a village, defend a stronghold, assault a fortified camp, intercept a supply train); a paid
tournament; a "help the peasants" that turns out to be a rebellion. THE TWIST in most: the caravan carries
contraband and the guards turn on you; the camp is bigger than said; the delivery's recipient is dead;
a third party (another mercenary company) shows up wanting the same pay; the client refuses to pay and you
choose to take it by force; the kidnapped daughter left willingly.
EVENTS: while travelling or camping, a screen with an illustration (painted) and 2 to 4 choices. Kinds:
company events (two men fight over a woman, a man deserts with your crowns, food spoils, a man finds a
puppy, the priest wants to bless the banner), background events (the Thief steals, the Cultist recruits
a brother into the cult, the Hedge Knight demands respect from the Beggar, the Monk heals), location
events (a wounded man on the road who may be bait; a fork with tracks; a merchant offering a deal; a
witch's hut), relationship events (two men become friends or rivals; a mentor-student pair), injury and
trait events (a man loses an eye, gains Fearsome, becomes a Drunkard). Outcomes: morale, hitpoints,
items, crowns, traits, a man leaves, a new man joins, relations change. Cooldowns keep them rare; the
company's composition drives which fire.
AMBITIONS (see 07). ORIGINS (starting stories: the Peasant Militia with cheap men and a 16-man roster,
the Lone Wolf, the Beast Slayers, the Cultists, the Trading Caravan, the Northern Raiders, the Deserters,
the Manhunters, the Gladiators, the Anatomists): each changes rules, not just the start.
(OURS: an ask is a person in a place; one twist each; an event on the map is a mouth with a portrait, two
or three choices, never in the first minute; rule 33 s2, QUESTS [bb events], WORDS [bb event writing].)

# BATTLE BROTHERS LIBRARY 09_ENEMIES.md
# source: reference/library/battle_brothers/09_ENEMIES.md
====================================================================================================
# 09 ENEMIES (recall)
BRIGANDS (human): Thug (rags, clubs, weak), Poacher (bow), Marksman (crossbow, dangerous), Raider (mail,
proper weapons), Leader (the tough one, named), Reaver? (heavy). They break and flee; they loot; the
first hours of every campaign are brigands. Teaching: morale, shields, a leader worth killing first.
NOBLE HOUSE TROOPS: Footman, Arbalester, Billman (polearm), Sergeant, Knight (heavy armour, two-hander).
Teaching: armour walls and second-row polearms.
GOBLINS: Ambusher (bow, poison), Skirmisher (nets, spears), Wolfrider (mounted, fast), Shaman (roots and
buffs), Overseer (whips and buffs). Teaching: reach, nets, status effects; goblins are the "annoying" enemy.
ORCS: Young (fast, weak armour, many), Berserker (rage, two-handers), Warrior (heavy armour, big), Warlord
(huge). Teaching: knockback, armour, a wall that pushes you around.
UNDEAD: Wiederganger (rises again unless decapitated or burned; slow), Fallen Hero (heavy armour), Ancient
Dead (legionaries: shieldwall, spear line, honour guard), Necromancer (raises the dead mid-fight), Ghoul /
Nachzehrer (eats corpses to grow), Vampire (teleports, drains). Teaching: kill order and cleavers.
BEASTS: Direwolf (fast, pack), Webknecht (giant spider, webs), Unhold (troll: regenerates, throws men),
Lindwurm (acid blood, tail), Schrat (tree: spawns saplings, shields), Hexe (charms your men), Alp
(nightmares, night), Kraken (legendary, tentacles), Serpent (drags men), Hyena (desert pack), Sand Golem,
Ifrit (desert). Teaching: each beast is one mechanic made flesh.
BARBARIANS (north): Thrall, Marauder, Chosen (huge), Beastmaster with Unholds, Drummer. NOMADS (desert):
Outlaws, Slingers, Assassins; GILDER? SOUTHERN CITY-STATES troops: Conscript, Footman, Officer, Assassin,
Gunner (handgonne), Mortar.
CHAMPIONS: named variants with more stats and a named item.
THE SHAPE: every enemy is a rule you must learn; the roster of a fight is telegraphed by the party's size
and kind on the map; fights are chosen, not stumbled into. (OURS: the factions' crews on the map, sized
and named at a distance; FACTIONS [bb houses], COMBAT [bb fight].)

# BATTLE BROTHERS LIBRARY 10_UI_AND_FEEL.md
# source: reference/library/battle_brothers/10_UI_AND_FEEL.md
====================================================================================================
# 10 WHAT IS ON SCREEN, AND THE FEEL (recall; UI [bb interface] verifies)
THE MAP HUD: top bar with crowns, food days, tools, medicine, ammo, day count and time-of-day sun; the
company's banner and name; a bottom bar with the roster's faces (small portraits with hitpoint and
morale rings), buttons for camp, roster, inventory, ambitions, the relations screen; a pause/play/2x;
a map with the marker and named settlements; a legend for terrain. Hovering a party shows its kind and
size; a settlement shows its buildings and situations. Right-click cancels.
THE SETTLEMENT SCREEN: the town in one painted view with its buildings as clickable icons; inside, the
market (grid of items with prices), the recruits (a row of faces with background and cost), the tavern
(rumours as one line each; a drink for morale), the temple (heal), the hall (contracts).
THE FIGHT HUD: the hex board; the active man's skills as a row of icons with AP and fatigue cost; his
bars (hitpoints, fatigue, morale); a turn order strip at the top with every face in order; a combat log;
end turn / wait / retreat. Hovering an enemy shows hit chance and his stats. The camera is fixed
isometric with zoom.
THE ROSTER: each man's page: portrait (painted, aged by injuries), background story text, stats with
stars, perks tree, equipment paper doll, traits list with icons, level and xp. A man's page is where the
story lives.
THE FEEL: a hand-painted map that reads like a board game; a fight that is slow, heavy and legible
(every number visible on hover); a company that outlives its men; the loss of a man with a name; the
tension of crowns vs wages; the day/night light on the map; music per region and per crisis; ambient
sound of the terrain; the drum on the fight's first turn.
SOUND (SOUNDS [bb ambience] verifies): map ambience by terrain and time (wind, birds, crickets at
night, rain); footsteps of the marker; a horn when a party is spotted; the fight has a drum, weapon
impacts by material, grunts, death cries, the shield thud; the settlement has crowd murmur and a
blacksmith; music tracks per biome and a battle theme per enemy kind.
(WHAT WE DO NOT COPY, rule 33g: the stills. Ours move: the map breathes, an event is a person speaking,
under the analog horror bible with Newgrounds' hand-made energy. CORRECTED 9/28 (DIRECTION [bb density]): this
line said "a place is a living street" - dead since his third votes (37b) and rule 38b: a place is a
SETTLEMENT SCREEN, as theirs is, and nothing walks the city; the close grid is the fight's and the Strip's.)

====================================================================================================
# THE BATTLE BROTHERS LIBRARY (rule 33j, Paolo 9/27: "download everything or remember everything, all the stats")
Battle Brothers is the reference for the campaign layer, the overworld map, travel, events, places and the
company (its fight is flavour only; Rogue Fable 4 leads the fight). Every [bb ...] school line reads this
library FIRST and cites the file it used; a lane that finds a number wrong fixes it here with a source.

STATUS: volumes 01-10 are written FROM MEMORY by the coordinator on 9/27 because the wiki cannot be
fetched from the fleet's machines (network policy). Every number in them is tagged (recall) until a lane
verifies it against a fetched page. When the hosts battlebrothers.fandom.com and battlebrothersgame.com
are allowed, PLUMBER [bb library] pulls every wiki page and dev blog to text under wiki/ and blog/, and the
volumes cite them.

01_WORLDMAP.md        the map, travel, time, sight, tracks, camps, ambitions, crises
02_COMBAT_RULES.md    hexes, AP, fatigue, initiative, hit chance, armour, injuries, morale, terrain
03_WEAPONS.md         every class, its skills, its tile SHAPE (the machine-gun question), sample stats
04_ARMOUR_SHIELDS.md  head and body armour, shields, helmets, weight and fatigue
05_PERKS.md           the seven tiers, every perk in one line
06_BACKGROUNDS.md     recruits: wage, cost, stat leanings, traits, what they say
07_ECONOMY.md         crowns, wages, prices, trade goods, settlement situations, renown
08_CONTRACTS_EVENTS.md contract types and twists, the event shape, samples, ambitions
09_ENEMIES.md         every faction and its roster, what each unit teaches a fight
10_UI_AND_FEEL.md     what is on screen, the roster, the camp, the fog, day and night, sound

# BATTLE BROTHERS SCHOOL: THE BESTIARY COUNT, AND WHAT EACH ONE IS IN BOHEMIA (coordinator 9/29/26, round zero)
# Paolo: 'research how many combat factions and beasts there are in Battle Brothers and that's the bare minimum
# amount we need, and enemy types.' Counted off the wiki's enemy and faction pages as search returns them
# (the machines cannot open the wiki: network policy). Numbers are (recall+search); COMBAT [bestiary] verifies
# and corrects in the library (reference/library/battle_brothers/09_ENEMIES.md).

## 1. THE COUNT (base game + Beasts & Exploration + Warriors of the North + Blazing Deserts)
COMBAT FACTIONS (a group you can meet on the map with its own roster): 12
  Human: Brigands, Noble Houses, Mercenaries (hedge knights, swordmasters, master archers, deserters), Barbarians,
  Nomads, Southern City-States, Cultists, Militia/Peasants (8).  Non-human: Greenskins (orcs and goblins, 1 or 2),
  Undead (the Wiedergänger line and the Ancient Dead, 1 or 2), Beasts (1).
ENEMY TYPES (a distinct fighter with its own stats and look): about 75
  Brigands 11 (thug, raider, poacher, marksman, marauder, leader, swordmaster, hedge knight, master archer, disguised
  bandit, wardog); Noble Houses 10 (footman, billman, arbalester, man-at-arms, standard bearer, sergeant,
  zweihander, knight, wardog, donkey); City-States 9 (indebted, conscript, gunner, engineer, assassin, officer,
  mortar, citizen, donkey); Nomads 8 (cutthroat, outlaw, slinger, archer, leader, blade dancer, executioner, desert
  stalker); Barbarians 9 (thrall, reaver, chosen, drummer, beastmaster, king, madman, warhound, armoured unhold);
  Cultists ~3; Militia ~3; Orcs 4 (young, warrior, berserker, warlord); Goblins 5 (ambusher, skirmisher, overseer,
  shaman, wolfrider); Undead 10 (wiedergänger, armoured wiedergänger, fallen hero, necromancer, geist, ancient
  auxiliary, ancient legionary, ancient honour guard, ancient priest, necrosavant); Beasts 17 (below).
BEASTS: 17 named
  Direwolf, Frenzied Direwolf, Hyena, Nachzehrer, Webknecht, Unhold, Armoured Unhold, Frost Unhold, Alp, Hexe,
  Schrat (and Sapling), Lindwurm, Serpent, Ifrit, Geist, Kraken (boss), Ijirok (boss).
BOSSES / LEGENDARY LOCATIONS: 3 to 5 (Kraken, Ijirok, the Black Monolith, the Goblin City, the Sunken Library).
CHAMPIONS: any type can spawn as a named champion with a unique item (the 'named' system).
THE FLOOR FOR BOHEMIA, HIS RULE: at least 12 factions, 75 enemy types, 17 beasts, 3 bosses, and champions.

## 2. WHAT EACH ARCHETYPE IS IN BOHEMIA (first attempt, draft; his example leads)
Battle Brothers' roster works because every enemy TEACHES one thing (wolves: they flank; goblins: they kite;
orcs: they shove; undead: they do not stop; necromancer: kill him first). Ours keeps the lesson and swaps the skin.
- NECROMANCER -> THE MECHANIC (his words): a man who keeps reviving his robots; kill him and the machines drop.
- WIEDERGÄNGER (the slow dead that get up again) -> SALVAGE DRONES / DEAD MACHINES that reboot unless put down
  properly; the Amalgamation's cheapest bodies.
- ANCIENT DEAD (the legion that holds a line) -> THE OLD ORDER'S MACHINES: security drones and exo-suited
  remains still running the last order they were given; the horror bible's 'nobody left who should be running it'.
- NECROSAVANT (the vampire that jumps) -> the fast machine that relocates; the dial shot is the only answer.
- GEIST (the scream that breaks morale) -> a SIREN / BROADCAST unit; the too-even voice at volume.
- BRIGANDS -> ROAMING CREWS (37e): scavengers, poachers, marksmen, a leader with a name.
- NOBLE HOUSES -> THE FACTIONS' HOME-BASE GUARDS (the Mob, the Trades, the Network, the Reds...), armoured, in colour.
- MERCENARIES / HEDGE KNIGHTS -> OTHER COMPANIES like yours, the rival crew with a runway look.
- BARBARIANS (with beastmasters and unholds) -> THE LAB-BREAKOUT PEOPLE: cult-like keepers who walk with beasts.
- NOMADS / CITY-STATES (guns, mortars, assassins) -> THE STRIP'S CASINO SECURITY and the desert road crews:
  the only faction with working heavy guns and a mortar.
- CULTISTS -> THE AMALGAMATION'S FAITHFUL (act 2 and 3 grow them).
- GOBLINS (kiting, nets, poison, wolf riders) -> KIDS AND RUNNERS on bikes and dirt quads with slings and nets.
- ORCS (mass, shove) -> THE HEAVY: exo-suit men, crash-bar shields, they push you off the tile.
- BEASTS -> DE-EXTINCT ANIMALS, one for one where the fit is exact: Direwolf = the dire wolf (Colossal's real 2025
  pups make this the most real beast in the game); Hyena = the cave hyena; Unhold = the short-faced bear or the
  ground sloth (armoured = with lab plating); Lindwurm = the big monitor lizards Vegas exotic-pet trade keeps; Alp
  = a night thing (the horror line, not an animal); Schrat = the mesquite/Joshua-tree walker (fantasy; a maybe);
  Webknecht = nothing (no giant spiders; a swarm of lab things instead); Kraken = the reservoir's thing (Lake Mead);
  Ijirok = the mammoth. The beasts list proper: records/BOHEMIA_THE_BEASTS_OF_BOHEMIA_DE_EXTINCTION_ROUND_ZERO_9_29_26.md.
- CHAMPIONS -> NAMED MEN with a unique piece of runway gear, on the tracks FACTIONS already draws.
Every row is WORLD's and COMBAT's to knock down; the COUNT is his and stands.

# BATTLE BROTHERS SCHOOL: THE SEVENTEEN BEAST MECHANICS, EXACT (coordinator 9/29/26, from recall; COMBAT verifies every line against the library 09_ENEMIES and the wiki and corrects it there)
# Paolo: 'create the beast archetypes exactly how they are in Battle Brothers... an Ifrit, when it's big, can become

# THE LESSON | THE BOHEMIA SKIN THAT FITS (first attempt; COMBAT and WORLD decide). All (recall).

 1 DIREWOLF: fast, high initiative, moves far, attacks twice, low armour, comes in packs of 6-10, circles to flank
   and surround | dies fast when caught alone | spears and a line | 'hold the line, do not chase' | the DIRE WOLF PACK
 2 FRENZIED DIREWOLF: the same, stronger and reckless | | | | the pack's alpha
 3 HYENA: fast, pack, its bite SHREDS ARMOUR (tears armour off rather than through it), flees when hurt, returns | |
   kill the leader, they scatter | 'armour is not safety' | the HYENA CLAN
 4 NACHZEHRER (ghoul): weak alone; DEVOURS A CORPSE OR A DOWNED MAN to grow a size (small, medium, large; more HP
   and hit), a large one is a brute | shrinks back when hurt? (verify) | keep it from bodies | 'leave no dead on the
   field' | the HOG SOUNDER (grows on the dead) or the hyena
 5 WEBKNECHT (giant spider): packs; a NET attack that roots a man in place (webbed), then poison bites that stack
   | low HP | cut the net, fire | 'a rooted man is a dead man' | the TEGU AND MONITOR pack, or a keeper's nets
 6 UNHOLD: huge HP and hits, REGENERATES every turn, GRABS a man and THROWS him tiles away, knocks down | slow |
   burst it down in one turn or it heals | 'focus fire' | the SHORT-FACED BEAR, the muscle bull
 7 ARMOURED UNHOLD: the same in barbarian plate | | | | the lab's plated bear
 8 FROST UNHOLD: the same, its hits chill (fatigue drain) | | | | (cold; no skin here; a machine)
 9 ALP: NIGHT ONLY; puts a man TO SLEEP (nightmares that deal damage while he sleeps), TELEPORTS (blinks) each
   turn, paper HP | | wake your men (slap), reach it before it blinks | 'the night has rules' | the SABRE-TOOTH at
   the water (ambush, vanish) or the machine's siren
10 HEXE (witch): CHARMS one of your men to fight FOR HER; the charm breaks when she is hurt or dies; she hides
   behind her charmed | | shoot past the charmed man | 'kill the caster' | the Amalgamation's PREACHER (human)
11 SCHRAT (treeman): heavy bark armour that REGROWS; a splinter shield that hurts attackers; SPAWNS SAPLINGS from its
   body when struck | slow | fire, blunt | 'hit it with the right tool' | the TAMARISK THICKET (stationary, spawns) or
   an old machine
12 SAPLING: the Schrat's small spawn | | | | the thicket's shoots
13 LINDWURM: TWO BODIES on the board (head and tail); the TAIL sweeps and knocks down; its ACID BLOOD damages the
   weapon and armour of whoever cuts it | | polearms, arrows, patience | 'some things you do not melee' | the
   HIPPO (two-tile body, blood that ruins your gear = the hide too thick) or the MAMMOTH (two tiles, the trunk)
14 SERPENT: PULLS a man toward it (drag one or two tiles), then CONSTRICTS (crush, cannot act) | | kill it before
   the squeeze | 'stay out of reach' | the monitor lizard grown large, or the swarm's drag (verify)
15 IFRIT (sand golem): comes in three SIZES; a big one, WHEN DAMAGED ENOUGH, SPLITS into two or three smaller
   ones (his words: 'instead of one gigantic Ifrit it becomes less'); it can BLAST (a sand throw that hits at range
   and staggers); small ones MERGE back into a big one; blunt beats it, blades bounce | | kill the small ones
   before they merge | 'the more you hit it, the more of them there are' | THE SWARM, exactly: a big swarm hit
   splits into two or three, stings at range, re-merges if left alone; or the dino-bird flock
16 GEIST (ghost): incorporeal; its SCREAM sends your men FLEEING (morale checks), it is hard to hit and gone in

17 KRAKEN (boss): from the WATER; TENTACLES rise around the board, GRAB and DRAG men toward the maw each turn,

   the enemy' | THE HIPPO POD at Lake Mead (the shore closes; the drag is the charge), or the Amalgamation's cables
18 IJIROK (boss): a frost stag spirit; FREEZES ground and men (chilled: half speed), TELEPORTS around the board

   strikes the roof and is gone) or the sabre-tooth
Also: champions (any beast as a named version with a unique drop), and the beasts' CONTRACTS (a hunt is posted at
a place; the trophy is the pay). Eighteen lines because the two bosses count; the floor of 17 stands.

# BATTLE BROTHERS SCHOOL: THE WEAPON CLASSES, THEIR RULES, AND OUR ARSENAL (coordinator 9/29/26, recall; COMBAT verifies in the library 03_WEAPONS and corrects there)
# Paolo: 'what type of guns would fit their type of melee weapons... Battle Brothers has a handgun; is that a bazooka now?'
# Each line: BB CLASS | ITS RULE (what makes it that class) | OUR WEAPON THAT FITS | notes. Reach is in house tiles (9/22: pistol 1, rifle 2, scope 3).

HIS ANCHORS (9/29, records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_MOSTLY_CITY_A_BLOCK_WAR_PISTOL_IS_A_DAGGER_9_29_26.md): A PISTOL IS A DAGGER (cheap, fast, close, the finisher everybody carries); A MACHINE GUN IS A TWO-HANDED HAMMER 'or something' (the big two-hander: COMBAT picks per gun, the light MG sweeps like the greatsword (33i), the heavy MG knocks down like the hammer). The table follows his anchors.

MELEE
- SWORD (riposte, precise, low fatigue, weak vs armour) | a RIPOSTE stance and a sure hit | the MACHETE and the BAT: the sure-hit close weapon; riposte is the counter-swing
- AXE (splits shields, heavy) | breaks SHIELDS/cover | the FIRE AXE and the SLEDGE: breaks cover tiles (cars, barriers, doors) in one swing
- MACE (stuns, ignores some armour) | STUN, a lost turn | the TASER BATON and the PIPE: stun; the riot baton
- HAMMER (crushes armour first) | ARMOUR-FIRST damage | the SLEDGE and the CLAW HAMMER: strips plates before flesh
- CLEAVER (bleed, decapitate) | BLEED over turns | the KUKRI, the BUTCHER'S CLEAVER, the CHAINSAW (bleed and fear)
- FLAIL (ignores shields) | HITS PAST cover | the CHAIN and the MORNING-STAR (a padlock on a chain): hits over cover
- DAGGER (puncture ignores armour, cheap, fast) | ARMOUR-IGNORING stab | the KNIFE and the ICE PICK: the puncture, the finisher
- SPEAR (spearwall: stops the charge, +hit) | ZONE CONTROL, a line nobody crosses | the BAYONET RIFLE and the REBAR SPEAR: spearwall; the rifle's butt and blade as one weapon
- POLEARM (reach 2, hooks, knocks back) | REACH 2 in melee, hook and push | the HOOK POLE and the SCYTHE: reach 2, pull a man off a roof
- TWO-HANDED SWORD / GREATSWORD (sweeps 3 tiles) | HITS THREE TILES | the MACHINE GUN sweeping a line (33i, his ruling)
- TWO-HANDED AXE / GREATAXE (splits, round swing) | HITS ALL AROUND | the FLAMETHROWER (a round of fire) or the chainsaw sweep
- TWO-HANDED MACE / HAMMER (knock down, crush) | KNOCK-DOWN | the SHOTGUN'S BUTT / the BREACHING RAM
- WHIP (disarm, reach) | DISARM | the BOLA / the CATTLE WHIP (the keepers')
- THROWING (javelins, axes: short-range volley) | RANGE 1-2 thrown | THROWN KNIVES, HATCHETS, MOLOTOVS (fire)
RANGED
- BOW (reach 6-7, fast, weak vs armour) | many shots, far, weak on plate | the COMPOUND BOW: quiet, ammo you can make; reach 3 like the scope
- CROSSBOW (armour piercing, slow reload) | ONE HEAVY BOLT, reload | the HUNTING RIFLE (scope 3) and the CROSSBOW itself: one shot, plates cracked
- SLING (cheap, stuns) | STUN at range | the SLINGSHOT and the ROCK: the kids' weapon
- HANDGONNE (Blazing Deserts: one shot, a CONE that hits everyone in front, long reload) | THE CONE | THE SHOTGUN: reach 1, everybody in the spread, one shell, reload
- FIRELANCE (a one-shot fire burst forward, then a spear) | ONE BURST then melee | the FLARE GUN / the improvised pipe gun; then the bayonet
- MORTAR (city-states: long arc, splash, minimum range) | SPLASH ON A TILE, useless close | THE BAZOOKA / RPG and the mortar: one shot, a tile and its neighbours
- BOMBS (net, smoke, acid, fire, holy water) | UTILITY THROWS | the NET (the keepers), SMOKE (the swarm's answer), FIRE (molotov; the swarm's other answer), the fire extinguisher
OURS WITH NO BB PARENT (allowed: the mechanic is new and named)
- THE PISTOL (reach 1, cheap, common; a routine hit costs one) | the sword's role at range: the sure short shot
- THE RIFLE (reach 2) | the polearm's role at range
- THE SCOPE (reach 3, the dial's weapon) | the crossbow's role, the shot that matters
SHIELDS AND ARMOUR
- SHIELDS (block, shieldwall) | the RIOT SHIELD and the CAR DOOR; shieldwall is a line of doors
- ARMOUR by weight (fatigue vs protection) | plates, vests, helmets, the attachments (36c): the same trade

AMMUNITION (the Bohemia rule Battle Brothers never needed): bullets are scarce in act 1 (a bullet costs one), reloading
is a craft, bows and blades are real; TUNING [ammo] sets how scarce; ECONOMY prices a round; by act 3 the reclaimed
future makes bullets again. This is why act one feels medieval (42 s5).

# THE BEASTS OF BOHEMIA: WHICH ANIMALS COULD REALLY BE BROUGHT BACK, AND WHICH WOULD THRIVE IN A BROKEN CITY (coordinator 9/29/26, round zero)
# Paolo: 'do big brain research on all animals in history; if they were revived with genetic coding, which ones
# would do really well in a hurt human civilization; that's where we get our beasts; not radiation; beasts humans
# genetically brought back that broke out of their labs when the dollar went to shit; take your time; all animals
# that have ever existed and we could get their DNA from whatever fossil.' REALISM FIRST, then the fun.

## 1. THE HARD LIMITS (what the real science allows, 2026)
- DNA HAS A SHELF LIFE. The oldest DNA ever read is about 1 to 1.2 million years (Siberian mammoth teeth, 2021) and
  the oldest environmental DNA about 2 million (Greenland permafrost, 2022); models put the outer wall near 2.6
  million years, and only in permafrost. WARM ground kills it in tens of thousands. So: NOTHING OLDER THAN THE ICE
  AGE COMES BACK. No dinosaurs, no Titanoboa, no Megalania, no giant dragonflies. Anyone who says otherwise in the
  game is lying, and that is a good line for a mouth.
- WHERE DNA SURVIVES: permafrost (Siberia, Yukon), BONE-DRY CAVES (Nevada, Arizona, Patagonia: dung, hair, skin),
  cold deep lakes, museum skins and eggs (last 400 years), frozen tissue (the San Diego Frozen Zoo). TAR PITS
  RUIN IT (La Brea's sabre-tooths have almost no usable DNA); so does the tropics.
- YOU NEED A MOTHER. De-extinction is editing a living relative's genome and growing the animal in a surrogate
  of the right size. Mammoth -> elephant. Dire wolf -> grey wolf (done, April 2025: three pups from 13,000-year-old
  DNA). Thylacine -> a dunnart, with an artificial womb. Moa and dodo -> chicken germ cells. NO LIVING RELATIVE
  OF THE RIGHT SIZE, NO ANIMAL: ground sloths (the tree sloth is 5 kg), glyptodons, giant beavers, elephant birds
  are the hard cases; big cats and bears and horses and camels are easy.
- WHAT IS REAL TODAY: the dire wolf (2025), the woolly mammoth on track for 2028, thylacine, dodo, moa, bluebuck,
  quagga (back-bred), aurochs (back-bred as Tauros cattle), Pyrenean ibex (cloned 2003, lived minutes). By the
  crash years (2040 to 2045) a lab in the desert holding a dozen species is not fantasy; it is a decade of the
  current pace.

## 2. THE VALLEY'S OWN DEAD (the free story)
Tule Springs Fossil Beds, 20 miles north of the Strip, is one of the largest Ice Age finds on Earth (100,000 to
12,500 years ago): COLUMBIAN MAMMOTH, CAMELOPS (the American camel), DIRE WOLF, AMERICAN LION, SABRE-TOOTH CAT,
GIANT GROUND SLOTH, BISON, HORSE. Gypsum Cave, inside the valley, kept Shasta ground sloth dung and hair dry enough
that its DNA was read in 1998. The lab that made the beasts was in Las Vegas because the bones were in Las Vegas;
what broke out is what used to live here. Nobody has to invent a reason.

## 3. THE TEST FOR 'DOES WELL IN A HURT HUMAN CIVILIZATION' (the Mojave, no power, thin people)
Score 0-3 on each: HEAT AND WATER (Vegas summers, no pumps); DIET (generalist and scavenger beats specialist; garbage,
dogs, livestock, people, golf-course grass); BREEDING SPEED; NEAR-HUMAN LIVING (thrives at the edge of a city);
DANGER to a man on foot; DNA + MOTHER (can it really be made). The winners are the ones that would win in real life.

## 4. THE TABLE (first attempt, draft; WORLD and COMBAT refine)
STRONG (thrive; the road's beasts)
- DIRE WOLF (13 kyr; wolf surrogate; MADE 2025). Pack hunter and scavenger, breeds yearly, follows men, heat is fine
  at night. Score 15/18. THE Battle Brothers direwolf, and the most real beast in the game.
- CAVE HYENA / SPOTTED HYENA LINE (30 kyr Eurasian DNA; spotted hyena surrogate). The single best-adapted large
  animal to living beside humans that has ever existed: eats bone, garbage, corpses; matriarch packs; laughs at
  night. 16/18. The Battle Brothers hyena, better than theirs.
- CAMELOPS (12 kyr Nevada bones; dromedary surrogate). A desert camel, water-thrifty, eats creosote; useless as a
  monster, priceless as a BEAST OF BURDEN and a war mount; the caravans' animal. 14/18 (danger 1).
- PLEISTOCENE HORSE (700 kyr DNA read; horse surrogate). Realism check: feral horses ALREADY thrive in Nevada by
  the tens of thousands. Not a lab beast, a wild one, and the truest mount. 15/18.
- AUROCHS / FERAL CATTLE (back-bred; cattle). Vegas had ranches; a 900 kg bull in a dead suburb is a real killer of
  men and the valley's meat. 13/18.
MID (survive near water and ruin; the boss and the hunt)
- AMERICAN LION (12 kyr Nevada; lion surrogate). 350 kg, hunts alone or in pairs, needs big prey; with the
  mammoths and camels gone it hunts cattle, horses and people. Slow breeder. 12/18. A boss, not a road beast.
- SMILODON, the sabre-tooth (28 kyr; DNA poor from tar, better from cold sites; lion surrogate). Ambush, short
  legs, cannot chase; lives at the edge of the reservoir and the golf courses. 10/18. Rare boss.
- SHORT-FACED BEAR (12 kyr; brown bear surrogate). 900 kg scavenger with a nose that smells a carcass for miles;
  the Battle Brothers unhold in fur. Needs meat volume; hangs on where crews leave bodies. 11/18.
- SHASTA GROUND SLOTH (Gypsum Cave DNA; NO mother of the right size: the hard one, a lab stretch a decade past
  the others). Slow, plant-eater, a walking meat locker; a HUNT, not a threat. 8/18, but it is Vegas's own.
- COLUMBIAN MAMMOTH (Nevada; elephant surrogate; the real program). Needs 150 kg of forage and 100 litres of water
  a day: survives only at Lake Mead's shore and the dead golf courses. One herd, a landmark, the Ijirok. 9/18.
- HARRINGTON'S MOUNTAIN GOAT (Grand Canyon caves, dung DNA; goat surrogate). Cliffs and the Spring Mountains; food
  for crews, not a fight. 11/18.
- BISON ANTIQUUS (bison surrogate; trivial). Herd, water-bound, dangerous when pushed. 12/18.
WEAK HERE (real to make, wrong for the Mojave; possible imports from other labs)
- WOOLLY RHINO, CAVE BEAR, CAVE LION, IRISH ELK, STEPPE BISON, MUSK OX: cold animals, die in a Vegas July. Scores 5-7.
- THYLACINE (Australia; small, shy, eats small game): survives in the hills, a rumour more than a fight. 7/18.
- MOA, ELEPHANT BIRD, DODO: flightless, slow breeders, walking meat; the dodo is a joke and Bohemia can use a
  joke; the moa (3 m tall) is a real kick. 6-8/18.
- PASSENGER PIGEON, CAROLINA PARAKEET, GREAT AUK, STELLER'S SEA COW: no threat, some are food; the pigeon in the
  billions is a SKY EVENT (the feed would post it). 4-6/18.
- QUAGGA, TARPAN, BLUEBUCK: grazers, food and mounts. 9/18.
IMPOSSIBLE (say so in a mouth; the lie is a good line)
- Dinosaurs, Megalania, Titanoboa, Meiolania, terror birds, Deinotherium: too old, no DNA, ever.
NOT LAB ANIMALS BUT ON THE ROAD ANYWAY (the manager adds, rule 41)
- Vegas's EXOTIC ESCAPEES: the Strip's show tigers and lions, the private-zoo big cats, monitor lizards and pythons
  from the pet trade, feral dogs in packs (the realest danger in any collapsed city), coyotes, feral hogs from
  the river states. The horror bible likes these: the animal that was always here, now unowned.

## 5. THE SHAPE FOR US (defaults, in VOTE, one line)
The road's beasts are the dire wolf pack, the hyena clan, feral dog packs and feral cattle; the mounts and burden are
Pleistocene horses and Camelops; the bosses are the American lion, the short-faced bear, the sabre-tooth at the
water and one mammoth herd at Lake Mead; the hunts are the ground sloth, the bison and the goat; the sky event is
the pigeon. Everything came out of one lab north of the city, at the fossil beds, when the money died. Count
against the floor: 12 named beasts here plus the escapees; the floor is 17; WORLD and COMBAT fill the rest from
this table, never from radiation.

## 6. SOURCES (research; none is a reference game)
Colossal Biosciences' dire wolf (Time, April 2025), mammoth and moa programs (CNN, Forbes 2026); the million-year
mammoth DNA (Science, 2021) and the two-million-year Greenland DNA (Nature, 2022); Tule Springs Fossil Beds (NPS,
Travel Nevada, San Bernardino County Museum); the Gypsum Cave sloth DNA (Poinar et al., Science 1998, recall).

# PAGE BOHEMIA_THE_BEASTS_OF_BOHEMIA_ROUND_ONE_THE_INVASIVE_LENS_9_29_26.md
# source: records/BOHEMIA_THE_BEASTS_OF_BOHEMIA_ROUND_ONE_THE_INVASIVE_LENS_9_29_26.md
====================================================================================================
# THE BEASTS OF BOHEMIA, ROUND ONE: THE INVASIVE LENS (coordinator 9/29/26; Paolo: 'do you need to do more research on the animals from earth's history that if came back would be crazy good invasive species?' Yes; this is it.)
# Round zero (records/BOHEMIA_THE_BEASTS_OF_BOHEMIA_DE_EXTINCTION_ROUND_ZERO_9_29_26.md) asked CAN IT BE MADE and
# DOES IT FIT THE DESERT. This round asks the question nature asks: WHICH ONES TAKE OVER, judged by the animals that
# already did it in real life. Numbers are (recall); WORLD [creatures] verifies and cites.

## 1. WHAT MAKES AN INVADER (the biology, five traits; the more, the worse)
1. BREEDS FAST AND YOUNG (the feral hog: two litters a year of six, breeding at eight months).
2. EATS ANYTHING (hog, rat, hyena, raccoon: garbage, crops, carrion, eggs, small animals).
3. TOLERATES A WIDE CLIMATE (the Argentine tegu lizard sleeps through a frost; a python does not).
4. NOTHING HUNTS IT where it lands (no predator, no disease, no hunter with ammunition).
5. LIVES WELL BESIDE HUMANS (the edge of a dead city is a buffet: dogs, cattle, gardens, dumps, water tanks).
A large animal can still take over if 4 and 5 hold: it just takes decades instead of years.

## 2. THE REAL CASES (each one is a precedent a lane can cite)
- ESCOBAR'S HIPPOS (Colombia): four escaped a private zoo in 1993; about 170 by 2023, the largest hippo
  population outside Africa, breeding in rivers with no predator. A dead drug lord's pets became a national
  problem in thirty years. THE MODEL FOR ONE BIG ANIMAL AT ONE WATER.
- AUSTRALIA'S FERAL CAMELS: dromedaries let go when trucks replaced them; about a million by 2008 across the
  outback, culled to a few hundred thousand. THE MODEL FOR CAMELOPS: a desert camel with no predator owns a desert.
- THE UNITED STATES' FERAL HOGS: six to nine million across 35 states, the most destructive invasive mammal on
  the continent, breeding faster than any hunt. THE MODEL FOR ANY FAST-BREEDING OMNIVORE.
- NEVADA'S OWN MUSTANGS AND BURROS: tens of thousands of feral horses and burros on Nevada range right now, in
  the Mojave and the Great Basin, protected by law and outgrowing it. PROOF that horses and donkeys go feral in
  this exact valley without any lab.
- FLORIDA'S PYTHONS AND TEGUS: Burmese pythons emptied the Everglades of small mammals in twenty years (pet
  releases and a hurricane-wrecked breeding facility, 1992: A LAB THAT BROKE OPEN IS A REAL EVENT); the tegu
  spreads because it survives cold. THE MODEL FOR THE PET-TRADE REPTILES.
- EUROPE'S RACCOONS, BRITAIN'S GREY SQUIRRELS, THE STARLING: small, fast, city-loving; the sky and the attic.

## 3. THE TABLE, INVASIVE LENS (score the five traits, 0-3 each, max 15; 'made' from round zero)
S TIER: TAKES THE VALLEY IN ONE ACT
- CAVE HYENA / SPOTTED HYENA LINE  14/15. Every trait. Clans of 20 to 80, eat bone and garbage, laugh at
  night, kill dogs, take children; the only large carnivore that grows its numbers next to a human town. The
  road's true owner by act 2.
- FERAL HOG (not a lab animal; already in the river states, arrives by act 2)  15/15. The real champion. Digs up
  every garden and grave, breeds like rats, 200 kg boars charge. The valley's food and the valley's plague.
- CAMELOPS and feral dromedaries  12/15 (slow breeder, but nothing else in the desert can touch it). The caravan
  animal and the desert's cattle; a bull camel in rut kills men.
- DIRE WOLF  12/15. Packs of 6 to 15, follow the cattle and the dogs, cross a mountain in a night; competes with
  coyotes and feral dogs and wins. The lesson beast (they flank).
- FERAL HORSE (already here)  12/15. Herds on every dry lakebed; mounts for whoever can catch one.
A TIER: TAKES A PLACE
- FERAL CATTLE / AUROCHS  11/15 (needs grass and water; the golf courses and the river).
- THE HIPPO AT LAKE MEAD (a zoo escapee, the Escobar model; the lake's water is 10 to 27 C, inside a hippo's
  range)  10/15. One pod, one water, the deadliest animal in Africa now the deadliest at the reservoir. The
  Battle Brothers Kraken, alive.
- ARGENTINE TEGU and pet-trade MONITORS  11/15. Two-metre lizards that sleep through the winter and eat eggs,
  chickens, dogs; the lindwurm at small size, in numbers.
- BISON  10/15. Herds at the water; a stampede across a home base is a raid by nature.
- THE PASSENGER PIGEON  12/15 for spread, 1 for danger. Billions in a decade, strips a field, fouls a water
  tank, blackens the sky: THE FEED'S FIRST WEATHER EVENT.
B TIER: A LANDMARK, NOT A PLAGUE (slow breeders; the bosses)
- AMERICAN LION 7/15, SMILODON 6/15, SHORT-FACED BEAR 6/15, MAMMOTH 4/15 (one herd, one shore), GROUND SLOTH
  4/15, MOA 6/15. Each is one fight you remember, never a hundred.
C TIER: DIES HERE
- The cold animals (woolly rhino, cave bear, musk ox), the pythons (Vegas frosts), the thylacine (no cover, no
  small game left once the hyenas arrive).

## 4. WHAT IT DOES TO A HURT HUMAN CIVILIZATION (the game's lesson, never preached)
Invaders do not attack cities; they EAT THE MARGINS a city lives on. Hogs take the gardens and dig the graves.
Hyenas take the dogs, then the goats, then the weak. Wolves take the cattle. Pigeons take the grain and foul the
water. Camels and horses take the grass and become the transport. Hippos close the shore. The realistic economy
follows: the first thing a settlement builds is a WALL and a WATER TANK with a lid (LIFE+CITY [build a lot]), the
first contract is a HUNT (QUESTS' contracts), the first trade good is HIDE and MEAT (ECONOMY), and the man who
can catch a horse is rich (PEOPLE backgrounds).

## 5. THE SHAPE FOR US (amends round zero's default, in VOTE as one line)
Road beasts: hyena clans, dire wolf packs, feral dogs, hogs from act 2. Nature's transport: horses, burros,
camels. Water bosses: the hippo pod at Lake Mead, the lion and the bear at the shore. Small horrors: tegus and
monitors in the dead pools. Sky: the pigeon. Landmarks: one mammoth herd, one sabre-tooth, the sloth. WORLD
[creatures] fills the 17 from this and round zero; COMBAT [bestiary] takes the lessons; EYES checks the
count against the floor.

# PAGE BOHEMIA_THE_BEASTS_OF_BOHEMIA_ROUND_TWO_DINOSAURS_INSECTS_PLANTS_BIRDS_MICROBES_9_29_26.md
# source: records/BOHEMIA_THE_BEASTS_OF_BOHEMIA_ROUND_TWO_DINOSAURS_INSECTS_PLANTS_BIRDS_MICROBES_9_29_26.md
====================================================================================================
# THE BEASTS OF BOHEMIA, ROUND TWO: DINOSAURS, INSECTS, DEEP TIME, PLANTS, BIRDS, MICROBES (coordinator 9/29/26)
# Paolo: 'what about dinosaurs and insects and even very early on earth shit, what about invasive plants or birds,
# earth animal history is so big, are you bullshitting me?' Not bullshitting; too narrow. Rounds zero and one
# stayed on mammals. Here are the other doors, each held to the same rule: only what real science allows.

## 1. DINOSAURS: THE HONEST WALL, AND THE BACK DOOR THAT IS REAL
- THE WALL: no dinosaur DNA exists or can. The youngest non-bird dinosaur is 66 million years old; DNA is gone
  after about a million in the best cold, and amber does not keep it (tested; the film lied). Nothing from
  deep time comes back by cloning: no T. rex, no raptor, no Titanoboa, no Megalania, no giant dragonfly.
- THE BACK DOOR: BIRDS ARE DINOSAURS, and the old genes are still in them, switched off. Real labs have already
  switched some back on: chicken embryos grown with a dinosaur-like snout instead of a beak (Harvard, 2015),
  embryos with the leg bones of their ancestors, the 'chickenosaurus' program (Jack Horner) that aims at teeth,
  a long tail and clawed hands. That is not cloning; it is waking the ancestor inside a living bird. A lab in
  the 2040s that does this to an OSTRICH, an EMU or a CASSOWARY (a cassowary already kills people with a 12 cm
  claw) gets a two-metre flightless runner with teeth and hands. REALISTIC, and it walks a desert well. This is
  Bohemia's 'raptor', and every character who calls it a dinosaur is half right.
- THE SAME DOOR FOR OTHER ANIMALS: elephants carry mammoth genes (that is how the mammoth program works), horses
  carry zebra stripes, cattle carry the aurochs. Waking old genes in living animals is the cheap half of the lab.

## 2. INSECTS: NO GIANTS, BUT THE REALEST LAB ESCAPE IN HISTORY
- NO GIANT BUGS: the Carboniferous dragonfly with a 70 cm wingspan lived in air with 35% oxygen; today's 21%
  cannot feed a body that size. Physics, not DNA, keeps them dead.
- THE PRECEDENT THAT IS EXACTLY OUR STORY: the AFRICANIZED 'KILLER' BEE. In 1957 a lab in Brazil breeding a
  hardier bee let 26 swarms escape; they crossed South and Central America and reached Nevada in the 1990s. A
  lab animal that broke out and took a continent, already in Las Vegas. It is not fiction; it is the model.
- THE ENGINEERED ONES THAT ARE REAL NOW: gene-drive mosquitoes (released in Florida and Brazil to crash wild
  mosquito populations; a drive that escapes its target is the nightmare the papers debate), sterile-insect
  fly programs, RED IMPORTED FIRE ANTS (a ship escape, now the US South's plague), the ASIAN GIANT HORNET
  (Washington state, 2019 to 2021, eradicated with effort that a collapsed state cannot spend).
- FOR THE GAME: the swarm is an enemy KIND Battle Brothers does not have and we get for free: a beast you cannot
  fight with a gun, only with fire, water, smoke and walls; a hive on a home base is a raid by nature; a
  gene-drive mosquito is a disease clock on a district (WORLD's water and LIFE+CITY's lidded tank again).

## 3. VERY EARLY EARTH: NOTHING WALKS, BUT SOMETHING WAKES
- No animal from deep time can be made. What can, and does, come out of old ice is MICROBES: a 30,000-year-old
  giant virus revived from Siberian permafrost (2014), 48,500-year-old 'zombie viruses' revived alive (2023),
  anthrax from a thawed reindeer carcass that killed a child and 2,000 reindeer (Siberia, 2016). Bacteria
  spores from salt crystals have been claimed at 250 million years (disputed).
- FOR THE GAME: a plague is a beast without a body; the lab's cold rooms and the thawing north are where it
  comes from; the rumour arrives before the sickness; the long-injury rule (36b) already has the shape (out
  for weeks, a mark that stays). PEOPLE and TUNING, one row, later; not a road beast.

## 4. PLANTS: THE BIGGEST INVADERS ON EARTH, AND THE ONES ALREADY IN THE VALLEY
- ALREADY HERE, REAL: TAMARISK (salt cedar) chokes the Colorado and Lake Mead's shore, drinks the river, salts
  the soil; SAHARA MUSTARD and RED BROME carpet the Mojave and carry fire; CHEATGRASS turns the West into a
  fuse (the Great Basin's fire cycle went from every 60 years to every 5); BUFFELGRASS in Arizona; RUSSIAN
  THISTLE is the tumbleweed itself, a Russian import. The dead city burns because of plants nobody planted.
- REVIVED FROM DEEP COLD, REAL: a 32,000-year-old flowering plant grown from permafrost seeds (2012); a
  2,000-year-old Judean date palm grown from a seed found at Masada ('Methuselah', 2005), now fruiting. Old
  plants come back easier than old animals.
- ENGINEERED, REAL: drought crops, fast poplars, the lab's own 'reclaimed ground' plantings (the 32b future gets
  techier: reclaimed ground is planted ground). A crop that escapes is a weed with a patent.
- FOR THE GAME: plants are ECONOMY and WORLD, not COMBAT: what grows on a held lot, what burns, what the camels
  eat, what a garden yields (the hog's target), the date palm as the reclaimed future's tree. The fight's one
  terrain effect stays the mound (rule 33); a burning brome field is a road event, not a tile stat.

## 5. BIRDS: THE ONES WE CAN REALLY MAKE, AND THE ONE THAT HUNTS MEN
- HAAST'S EAGLE (New Zealand, gone ~1400): 15 kg, a 3 m wingspan, hunted 200 kg moa, and by Maori account
  hunted people; DNA is good; a living eagle is the surrogate. THE ONE BIRD THAT IS A BOSS. Deserts suit eagles.
- THE PASSENGER PIGEON (billions; the sky event); the CAROLINA PARAKEET (a green flock in the palms; Los Angeles
  already has feral parrots by the thousand, real); the GREAT AUK (coast only); the DODO (a joke and food); the
  MOA and ELEPHANT BIRD (3 m flightless meat; slow to breed; a hunt).
- ALREADY INVASIVE, REAL: the STARLING (200 million in the US from 100 released in 1890), feral pigeons, house
  sparrows, feral chickens (Hawaii, Florida), feral peacocks (Los Angeles), Egyptian geese. The dead city's
  sky is loud.
- TOO OLD: terror birds, teratorns (La Brea tar), Argentavis. Say it in a mouth.

## 6. THE SEA AND THE RIVER (Lake Mead and the Colorado are the only water)
- Real invaders already there: QUAGGA MUSSELS (Lake Mead, 2007, clog every pipe and pump: the water system's
  own beast, ECONOMY Q7), Asian carp on the way, largemouth bass. The hippo (round one). No sharks, no
  megalodon (deep time), no plesiosaurs.

## 7. THE SHAPE FOR US (adds to rounds zero and one; in VOTE as one line)
Four beasts that were missing: the DINO-BIRD (an edited ostrich or cassowary with teeth and hands; the raptor),
the SWARM (killer bees, hornets, fire ants; fought with fire and walls, never a gun), HAAST'S EAGLE (the sky
boss), and the PLAGUE (a thawed thing with no body; PEOPLE's row). Plus the plants as the world's own hand:
tamarisk on the shore, brome fires, tumbleweeds, the date palm of the reclaimed future. The floor of 17 beasts is
now met three times over on paper; WORLD picks, COMBAT gives each a lesson, EYES counts.

# PAGE BOHEMIA_THE_BEASTS_OF_BOHEMIA_ROUND_THREE_THE_SEVENTEEN_9_29_26.md

# THE BEASTS OF BOHEMIA, ROUND THREE: THE LAB'S OWN DESIGNS, THE KEEPERS, AND THE SEVENTEEN (coordinator 9/29/26; his 'one more round')
# Rounds zero to two asked what can be made, what takes over, and what lives past mammals. This round adds the
# animals nobody revived because the lab DESIGNED them, the people who use animals as weapons, and then names
# THE SEVENTEEN with everything a lane needs to build each one. Numbers (recall); WORLD verifies.

## 1. THE DOOR NOBODY OPENED: ANIMALS THE LAB MADE NEW (real, today)
- ORGAN PIGS: pigs edited with human genes so their hearts and kidneys can go into people; real transplants
  happened in 2022 to 2024; farms of them exist under pharmaceutical guard. Let loose, they are hogs (S tier)
  with a story: every one carries a human gene, and people will not eat them. The horror bible likes that.
- MUSCLE-DOUBLED LIVESTOCK: cattle, pigs and dogs edited to lack the gene that limits muscle (myostatin;
  Belgian Blue cattle have it naturally; edited beagles were made in China in 2015). A 1,200 kg bull with
  double muscle is the aurochs made worse. Feral in a decade.
- HUMANIZED MICE AND RATS by the million in every research town; released, they are rats. Rats are the most
  successful invasive mammal in history and no game beast; but a plague rides them (PEOPLE [the plague]).
- LAB PRIMATES: Florida has a wild colony of rhesus macaques since the 1930s (a tourist attraction's release)
  that carries a herpes virus deadly to people; research macaques number in the tens of thousands. A monkey
  troop in a dead casino is real, funny, and dangerous. Not a beast to fight; a place's hazard and a rumour.
- THE ALMOST-HUMAN LINE: human-monkey and human-pig embryo chimeras have been grown in labs (2019 to 2021) for
  organ research and stopped by rule at a few weeks. Bohemia does not put a half-man on the road (his beasts
  are animals; the Amalgamation is the villain), but a rumour that the lab 'went further' is exactly the horror
  bible's institutional lie, and WORDS may use it as a lie.
- GLOW AND MARKER ANIMALS: fluorescent fish (sold in pet stores now), glowing rabbits and pigs; harmless, and a
  night-time tell on the map: a green shine in the dark is a lab animal. DIRECTION's analog horror gift.
- DE-DOMESTICATION: dogs are the realest beast of every collapse. A pack of former pets turns wild in one
  generation (India's 30 million street dogs kill ~20,000 people a year by rabies). Feral dogs are act 1's first
  fight and never stop being one.

## 2. THE KEEPERS (the Battle Brothers beastmaster, made real)
People use animals as weapons and tools, and a faction that does is a faction others fear:
- WAR DOGS (the noble houses' wardogs; police and military dog lines exist by the thousand); HUNTING BIRDS
  (falconry is a living craft in Nevada; Haast's eagle on a glove is a boss's pet); CAMEL CAVALRY (real for two
  thousand years, the desert's own); HORSE RAIDERS (Nevada's mustangers); THE HYENA MEN (Nigeria's hyena
  handlers are real: chained hyenas as street performers and guards); BEE-KEEPERS AS SIEGE (hives thrown
  over walls is a medieval tactic and a real one).
- FOR THE GAME: the beast-keeper faction (round zero's 'barbarians with unholds') is a roster PEOPLE and FACTIONS
  write: a handler background, a beast slot in the company (the player can hire a handler and his dog, camel or
  bird; the automated companion may be an animal), and the raid where the enemy brings a hyena.

## 3. SIZE ON THE FIGHT BOARD (a tile is a house, 40 metres or so; rule 38h)
A house-sized tile holds a whole pack, so beasts are GROUPS on a tile, not single figures, and the biggest are
still one tile: a dire wolf pack (6 to 10 animals) = one tile of wolves that can split; a hyena clan = one to two
tiles; a hog sounder = one tile; a mammoth herd = two tiles; a hippo pod = one tile at the shore that never
leaves the water tile; the eagle = no tile (it strikes the roof and leaves); the swarm = a tile that spreads one
tile a beat until fire or water; the dino-bird = one tile, moves two a beat (the runner); the lion = one tile,
one animal, hits once and hard (the dial shot's target). COMBAT [bestiary] turns this into the data file with
the 9/22 reach rule; TUNING numbers it.

## 4. WHAT EACH IS WORTH (ECONOMY, batteries are the money, everything costs one)
Hide and meat (hog, cattle, camel, horse: the valley's food), ivory (mammoth tusks are a real trade today from
thawing Siberia), camel milk and burden, horse transport, honey (the swarm's upside), eggs (moa, a meal for a
company), feathers (the eagle), a live capture (a handler's dog or camel is worth a season's pay), bounties (a
hyena clan's contract). A beast is a contract and a market, not only a fight.

## 5. THE SEVENTEEN (the floor met, one line each: ORIGIN | CORRIDOR | ARRIVES | LESSON (the BB archetype) | BOARD | WORTH)
 1 FERAL DOG PACK | Vegas's own pets | none | act 1 day 1 | wolves flank (direwolf lite) | 1 tile, splits | hide
 2 DIRE WOLF PACK | Vegas lab + California | I-15 | act 1 | they flank; kill the alpha (Direwolf) | 1 tile | pelt, bounty
 3 HYENA CLAN | Arizona lab | the Colorado | late act 1, owns act 2 | they take the weak at the edge; matriarch (Hyena) | 1-2 tiles | bounty
 4 FERAL HOG SOUNDER | the river states | the Colorado, I-40 | act 2 | they charge and dig; walls (Unhold lite) | 1 tile | meat
 5 CAMELOPS / FERAL CAMEL | Vegas lab + Australia-model releases | US-95 | act 1 | a mount, not a monster; the bull in rut | 1 tile | burden, milk
 6 FERAL HORSE HERD | already here | none | act 1 | catch one and you are rich | 1 tile | mounts
 7 FERAL / AUROCHS CATTLE | Nevada ranches, edited bulls | none | act 1 | the charge (Unhold) | 1 tile | meat, hide
 8 AMERICAN LION | Vegas lab | none | act 2 | one hit; the dial shot (Lindwurm-class boss) | 1 tile, 1 animal | pelt, renown
 9 SHORT-FACED BEAR | Utah lab | the Colorado | act 2 | it smells the dead you leave; scavenger boss (Unhold) | 1 tile | pelt
10 SABRE-TOOTH | Vegas lab | none | act 2, at the water | ambush; never chases (Alp-class night horror) | 1 tile | pelt, renown
11 HIPPO POD AT LAKE MEAD | a zoo escape (the Escobar model) | none | act 2 | the shore is closed (Kraken) | 1 water tile | renown
12 THE MAMMOTH HERD | Utah reserve (the real program) | the Colorado | act 3 | a landmark, a hunt of a lifetime (Ijirok) | 2 tiles | ivory
13 THE DINO-BIRD RUNNER | California lab (atavism) | I-15 | act 2 | fast, flanks, a claw; the 'dinosaur' (Goblin wolfrider) | 1 tile, 2 a beat | eggs, renown
14 THE SWARM (killer bees, hornets, fire ants) | Brazil 1957, already in Nevada | none | act 1 | fire, smoke, water, walls; no gun (new) | spreads 1/beat | honey
15 HAAST'S EAGLE | New Zealand DNA, a Utah raptor lab | the sky | act 3 | it strikes the roof; the sky boss (new) | no tile | feathers, renown
16 TEGU AND MONITOR LIZARDS | the pet trade | none | act 1 | small and many; eggs and chickens (Nachzehrer lite) | 1 tile, many | hide
17 THE GROUND SLOTH | Vegas lab (Gypsum Cave DNA; the hard one) | none | act 3 | a hunt, not a fight; slow (Schrat-class) | 1 tile | meat, renown
Also on the road, not counted: bison, burros, moa, the pigeon sky, macaques in a casino, rats and the plague,
the lab's glow animals as a night tell. The seventeen is the manager's default, in VOTE as one line; WORLD's
file is the truth; COMBAT gives each its lesson; COOK draws the first three (dog, dire wolf, hyena).

## 6. WHAT CLOSES (rule 41)
The beast research is DONE at four rounds. From here it is data (WORLD), lessons (COMBAT), numbers (TUNING),
art (COOK to DIRECTION's card), prices (ECONOMY), keepers (PEOPLE, FACTIONS) and words (WORDS). A fifth round
is a lane's page, not the manager's.

# PAGE BOHEMIA_THE_COMBAT_BOARD_ASSETS_WHAT_WE_HAVE_AND_WHAT_WE_NEED_9_29_26.md
# source: records/BOHEMIA_THE_COMBAT_BOARD_ASSETS_WHAT_WE_HAVE_AND_WHAT_WE_NEED_9_29_26.md

# THE COMBAT BOARD: WHAT WE HAVE, WHAT WE NEED, TERRAIN BY TERRAIN (coordinator 9/29/26; Paolo: 'think about all the assets you're gonna need for the combat board... no single combat map is exactly the same... different terrains, nature zones, tile blockers')
# Counts of what we HAVE are from the board's STATE lines and the banks folder (174 bank files, 49 district kits
# registered, 71 dossiers, the 7/28 street bank, the recooked car, the fortress buildings, COOK's map markers and
# land cut, 65 sounds); COOK [board assets] counts them exactly. The NEED column is the manager's first list.

## 1. HOW BATTLE BROTHERS BUILDS A BATTLE MAP (the model)
The world tile's terrain picks a tileset (plains, steppe, forest, swamp, hills, mountains, snow, desert, beach); a
settlement or camp fight adds its buildings; blockers (trees, rocks, tents, fences, walls, carts) are scattered
with rules (forests dense, plains open, hills stepped); elevation is a height map (hills and mountains give the
high-ground bonus); weather and night change the light and sight range; a seed makes each map unique. Roughly a
dozen terrain sets, three or four blocker kinds each, three heights, day/night/rain/snow.

## 2. OUR TERRAINS (the valley's, real; each is a KIND the map cell carries and the board is cut from)
 T1 THE SUBURB BLOCK (houses, yards, streets, sidewalks, cars, walls, sheds)          HAVE: the 7/28 street bank, the
    house tiles, the car from above, 49 district kits. NEED: roof tiles as standable high ground (37g), burnt and
    collapsed variants, fences and gates as blockers.
 T2 THE STRIP (casino fronts, the boulevard, fountains, signs, the Sphere, the tower)  HAVE: fortress buildings, the
    seven landmarks (partly), signs. NEED: the boulevard's width as two tiles of road, marquee blockers, a fountain
    tile, planters, the porte-cochere as cover.

## 3. THE KINDS EVERY TERRAIN NEEDS (the board's grammar; each kind is a data row, MODS' line)
FLOOR (the walkable ground look: 3 to 5 per terrain) | BLOCKER (a tile you cannot enter: 3 to 6 per terrain,
some destructible) | COVER (a tile that is half a blocker, cars, barriers, counters) | MOUND / ROOF (the one
terrain effect, high ground, 1 to 3 per terrain) | EDGE (what the board's border looks like: a road, water, a
fence, a cliff) | DRESSING (the small things that sell the place with no rule: signs, bones, trash, tracks) |
LIGHT (day, night, dusk; the sodium lamp, the fire) | WEATHER (dust, rain, the monsoon flood, heat shimmer;
looks only). Fifteen terrains x eight kinds is the inventory sheet COOK fills with HAVE / NEED counts.

## 4. THE COUNT, HONEST (CORRECTED BY HIM THE SAME HOUR, records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_MOSTLY_CITY_A_BLOCK_WAR_PISTOL_IS_A_DAGGER_9_29_26.md: 'most of it will be city-based terrain... every combat fight damn near like a block war'; the order below is REVERSED: CITY GAPS FIRST, the nature terrains after, because nature is the valley's edge and the beasts' ground, a minority of fights)
We have the CITY half well (T1, T2 partly, T8, T13, T14 partly) and the NATURE half almost not at all (T4, T5,
T6, T9, T11, T15). Battle Brothers is mostly nature; our valley is mostly desert and ruin around a city, so the
nature half looked like the bigger cook. BUT HE RULED MOST FIGHTS ARE BLOCK WARS, so the FIRST cook is the CITY'S GAPS: T1's roofs as high ground, burnt and collapsed variants, fences and gates; T7's barriers and the overpass; T8's cart corrals and the big-box roof; T9's trailers and tanks; T11's rubble mounds; T3's containers; THEN T4 OPEN DESERT, T5 THE SHORE, T6 THE HILLS, T15 THE LANDFILL for the beasts.
Every cook goes through DIRECTION's card and the reference check (compare to the real Mojave, real freeways,
real landfills), and every tile is house-sized (rule 38h).

## 5. THE GENERATOR (COMBAT [board generator] with WORLD's kits)
Input: the map cell (its terrain kind, its district kit if any, the time, the weather, a seed). Output: a board
cut from the district's own layout where there is one (rule 38h: it still reads as that block), or built from the
terrain's floor/blocker/mound rules where there is not; the edge from the neighbouring cells; the beasts' and the
enemies' spawn rules per terrain (hyenas at the landfill, the hippo at T5, the lion at T10's water). Never the
same twice; always readable as the place he tapped on the map.

# THE REVAMP LIST (coordinator 9/24/26, at Paolo's ask, EVERYTHING IS A THUMB: decided, he corrects in VOTE)
# His words: "think about everything we're doing and the parts that need to get cut: progress stops and we
# use those assets for different reasons... we can't be building on top of shit like this... it might need to
# be excavated from the files... a lot of these parts might have to be built from the ground up, using assets
# from shit we already have." (records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_CUT_AND_REBUILD_9_24_26.md)
# Three words per system: KEEP (build on it), CUT (progress stops; assets kept and reused; the code is
# excavated to archive/ so nobody builds on it), REBUILD (from the ground up, on assets we have).

## KEEP: build on it
- THE FIGHT BOARD (COMBAT): house tiles, the 112 body at every frame width, the beat, reach lit, the dial.
  RF4 first from now; BB flavour: weapon shapes (the machine gun is the greatsword), the mound.
- THE PEOPLE (PEOPLE, PORTRAIT, CHARACTER, ANIMATION): names and the county mix, faces and the face maker,
  bodies and the runway clothes, heredity, the rig and its clips, the deed ledger, standing, witnesses,
  rumours, memory, the creditor who remembers. This IS the company.
- THE MONEY (WORLD, ECONOMY): batteries, the purse, the loan of one a night, the strike, the shelves the
  day after, prices per place, the treasuries (once they save).
- TERRITORY (FACTIONS): who holds what, colour on the ground, tracks and whose they are, the lit circuits.
- THE VALLEY DATA (WORLD, LIFE+CITY): the 96x96 seed-built valley, its places (the shop, the shed, the
  pump, the Stratosphere, the Sphere), the clock and night. The MAP is drawn from it.
- THE DOOR: the loading screen, BEGIN, NOTES, the VOTE tab and the registry, the cracked phone and the
  feed (on the map).
- THE LOOK: the analog horror bible (with the Newgrounds era inside it), the approved tile banks, the
  fortress buildings, the footprints, the ground ruler. Every approved piece of art is an asset.
- THE SOUNDS WITH A REAL SOURCE: the door, the cloud, the song, the fold, the phone, the room, the
  footstep that is not sand.
- THE THREE ACTS (DYNASTY): the flip, the derive, the prepared names; the map is their surface.

## CUT: progress stops, assets kept, code excavated
- CROSS-VALLEY WALKING AS TRAVEL (RUN): the pad-walk from block to block, the stride as a travel unit,
  the walk-out-of-your-block work, sealed yards as travel blockers, the zoom ladder as a travel tool.
  Rows: [fast travel] (the map IS fast travel), [travel map] as an encounter system (folded into
  [bb map]), [tap walk] across the valley, [land on it], [open reachable] as a walking problem.
  WALKING WITHIN A PLACE STAYS (the street you arrive on, one step per house).
- THE CITY BUILDER AS A MODE (LIFE+CITY): the builder drawer, BUILD HERE and the plot panel as a
  separate screen. Rule 24 killed modes. Building comes back later as an act on the street feeding the
  derive's "what was built". The building tiles are assets and stay.
- THE COLD OPEN (RUN, PEOPLE): the family cutscene ("DAY 1 BEGINS BEFORE THE DAY", WATCH / NOT NOW) and
  the banner that eats fingers with it. Rule 32a. RAY, DENISE, MARCO and NINA stay as people you meet.
- THE ASKS AS A TEXT STREAM (QUESTS, WORLD, WORDS): notices, the night card, offer cards, the spoken ask
  as a line on screen. Rebuilt as contracts and events from people in places.
- THE NOISE-BUILT SOUNDS (SOUNDS): in the graveyard already (32e); 28 redos.
- THE OLD PAGES (PLUMBER): retired judge pages (~20 MB), records/target nobody loads (46.7 MB), the 29
  engine modules nobody loads, the workshop pages that present things. Off the site, into archive/.
- THE ALPHA'S TABS AS PLAY (UI): the tab strip stays a workshop shelf for the lanes; the GAME is one mode:
  map, street, fight, one HUD.

## REBUILD from the ground up, on assets we have
- THE MAP (RUN, with WORLD, FACTIONS, COOK, UI): the party marker, tap to travel, the clock running,
  roads faster than dirt, parties roaming and leaving tracks, places as destinations, arrival on a
  street. Built on the city view drawing, the valley data, the territory colours, the footprints.
- PLACES (WORLD, LIFE+CITY): a place is a block with its buildings as services; the shop, the shed, the
  pump, the fortress are the first four.
- CONTRACTS AND EVENTS (QUESTS, WORDS, PORTRAIT): a person in a place asks, pay negotiated the BB way,
  one twist each; an event on the road is a face with two or three real choices. Built on the asks
  generator, the boss ladder verbs, the word banks, the portraits.
- THE COMPANY (PEOPLE): a roster, a daily cost in batteries, who is on the marker, what they say on the
  road, who leaves. Built on the companion, the names, the faces, the deeds.
- ONE HUD (UI): the same controls on the map, the street and the fight; the phone on the map.
- THE DERIVE (DYNASTY, WORLD): act 2 and 3 computed from the ledgers; the ruin is the start; the map at
  three dates.
- THE DEMO (RUN): loading, travel + arrival, the fight, the first person; one map, a few places.
- THE SOUNDS (SOUNDS): 28 from real material.

## THE ORDER (mine: "the running order is mine")
1. RUN [bb map] school, PLUMBER [bb budget] and [excavate]: know what the map costs and clear the
   ground before a line is built.
2. The map with two places and the marker; arrival on the street we have; the fight we have.
3. One contract with a twist; one event on the road; the company as a roster of two.
4. The demo re-cut on that. Then everything else.

## THE EXCAVATION RULE
A CUT system is moved to archive/ THE ROUND IT IS CUT (GRAVEYARD IS FINAL; the registry line says what
replaced it); nothing in slices/ or engine/ loads from archive/ (PLUMBER gates it); the assets it used
stay where the live systems read them. Nobody builds on a cut system again: a row that touches one is
refused by the coordinator.

## AMENDED 9/27 BY PAOLO ("two scales", "one house doesn't equal one tile", "restart the whole enchilada"; laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_TWO_SCALES_ONE_GAME_9_27_26.md)
- MOVED FROM KEEP TO REBUILD: THE FIGHT BOARD (the RF4 fight moves onto the close grid in cells; house tiles
  are dead; reach re-derived in cells; the mound one cell; weapon shapes in cells). THE WALKED SURFACE
  (the close grid: tiny character, one cell per step, an honest grid where a house is many cells).
- MOVED FROM KEEP TO ASSET: the 112 px bodies, clothes and clips (the HD source the small sprites are cut
  from; the portraits and vote pages keep using them). The walked sprite is REBUILT small.
- NEW REBUILD ROWS: WORLD+LIFE+CITY [honest grid], COMBAT [fight on the grid], CHARACTER [small body],
  ANIMATION [small clips], COOK [cell tiles], DIRECTION [two scales look], RUN [two scales], PLUMBER [grid budget].
- THE ORDER, AMENDED: (1) [honest grid] for ONE block + PLUMBER [grid budget] + [bb map] school; (2) the
  tiny character walking that block, one cell per press, the squeeze to the map and back; (3) the fight on
  that grid; (4) the first person by name; (5) the demo re-cut: the first sixty seconds are a game.
